title: Overnight Communications Agent
description:
About Four Seasons:

Four Seasons is powered by our people. We are a collective of individuals who crave to become better, to push ourselves to new heights and to treat each other as we wish to be treated in return. Our team members around the world create amazing experiences for our guests, residents, and partners through a commitment to luxury with genuine heart. We know that the best way to enable our people to deliver these exceptional guest experiences is through a world-class employee experience and company culture.

At Four Seasons, we believe in recognizing a familiar face, welcoming a new one and treating everyone we meet the way we would want to be treated ourselves. Whether you work with us, stay with us, live with us or discover with us, we believe our purpose is to create impressions that will stay with you for a lifetime. It comes from our belief that life is richer when we truly connect to the people and the world around us.

About the location:

Why us? Why here? Why now? Working at the Four Seasons Resort The Biltmore in Santa Barbara offers more than just a career—it’s a chance to thrive in one of the world’s most idyllic settings. From the moment you arrive, the resort feels like a peaceful escape, surrounded by lush gardens and ocean breezes that make every day feel special. You’ll be part of a team that crafts unique spaces, where Spanish coastal elegance meets modern design, creating an environment that’s both vibrant and welcoming. Whether you live in Santa Barbara, Ventura, Goleta, Ojai, or Santa Ynez, you’ll enjoy the Mediterranean climate, easy access to world-class beaches, and proximity to renowned wine country for days-off escapes. The sense of community runs deep, and working here means becoming part of something timeless, where the resort’s storied past blends seamlessly with today's luxury. Whether you're sharing the resort’s beauty with guests or simply taking in the sunset on your way home, every moment here is unforgettable.

We are looking for a passionate and driven Overnight Communications Agent to join our team and significantly contribute to reopen our newly remodeled resort in the American Riviera, Santa Barbara!


What you will do:

The Overnight Communications Agent will oversee the day-to-day operation of the Communications function, supporting service delivery across multiple departments. You will be responsible for guest and internal communications, including calls, messages, and requests, are handled efficiently and in line with Four Seasons standards. This role requires strong communication, consistency, and the ability to maintain quality across a high volume. You will act as a key point of contact for operational communication, ensuring clarity, speed, and accuracy at all times.

  • Oversee all incoming and outgoing guest and internal communications
  • Maintain Four Seasons standards for telephone etiquette and communication quality
  • Have warm and professional phone polish and demeanor
  • Coordinate communication between hotel departments and across properties
  • Manage escalations, guest concerns, and service recovery with professionalism
  • Monitors incoming Chat Message via FS Messengers and reply or add other departments to the conversations when appropriate
  • Respond swiftly and effectively in any hotel emergency or safety situation.
  • This position requires an applicant with a flexible schedule and the ability to work all shifts, weekends and holidays.
  • Assisting in preparing the welcome letter for the arrival of VIP, Preferred Partner guests etc.
  • Handle guest complaints in accordance with Four Seasons policy

What you bring:

We are looking for individuals who have:

  • Previous experience in a Communications, PBX, or Front Office role within a hotel
  • Strong communication skills and confident, professional telephone manner
  • Excellent organization skills and attention to detail
  • Ability to remain calm and make decisions in a fast‑paced environment
  • A proactive, solution‑focused mindset
  • Confidence working across multiple systems and stakeholders
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Facilitation skills
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills (i.e. ability to identify when training is the actual solution and provide it if required)
  • Coaching & Influencing skills
  • Fluency in reading, writing, and spoken English is required. 2nd language is an asset
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, both in person and by telephone.
  • Excellent and unwavering customer service.

Schedule & Hours:

  • Schedule & Availability: As our resort operates 24/7, 365 days a year, our Overnight Communications Agent are expected to maintain flexibility to work overnight shifts, including weekends and holidays, as needed.

What we offer:

  • Hourly Rate: $23.95
  • Dynamic Employee Culture where you are encouraged to be your true self!
  • Inclusive and diverse employee engagement events all year-round
  • Competitive benefits (Medical, Dental, Vision, Employee Assistance Program, and 401k Retirement Plan) as well as Vacation & Holiday Pay
  • Sick Pay, Disability Coverage and Life Insurance
  • Exclusive discount and travel programs with Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts around the world
  • Complimentary Employee Meals
  • Comprehensive learning and development programs to help you elevate your craft.
  • And so much more!

Join the iconic Four Seasons Resort The Biltmore Santa Barbara, a classic estate infused with modern luxury! Learn more about the American Riviera

Job Summary

The Tele-sitter provides continuous observation and surveillance of assigned patients via video-monitoring. Interacts with individual patients while "rounding". Provides verbal redirection to prevent patients from engaging in at risk behaviors and notifying the nursing staff if patient requires assistance. The Tele-sitter carries out various clinical responsibilities as well as documentation of tasks and supports
and upholds the Patient Bill of Rights.

Essential Functions

  • JOB SPECIFIC COMPETENCIES:
    Demonstrates the required job specific technical/professional knowledge, skills and abilities *
    1. Monitors and observes up to 15 patients on one screen at one time and remains alert while on duty
    2. Maintains visual observation of patients at all times and communicates effectively using a microphone and
    headset
    3. Communicates with hospital staff and responds quickly to patient and behavioral changes
    4. Uses basic computer operation skills
    5. Provides assistance to patients while “rounding”, including toileting
    6. Collects data and charts observations and activities, reporting pertinent changes in the patient’s condition
    to the Registered Nurse.
    7. Complies with hospital safety regulations, environment of care, risk management, and infection control
    policies. Assists in maintaining and providing a clean, safe environment.
    8. Performs delegated or other specialized functions as educationally prepared.

    3. Utilizes positive communication skills when interacting with people of different cultures, values and
    beliefs.
    4. Demonstrates the ability to acknowledge customer concerns and takes corrective action.
    5. Demonstrates compliance with identified customer service behaviors.
    6. Provides escort to customers when necessary.
  • PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT:

    Participates in Department/Hospital-wide activities which improve

  • MISSION/STRATEGIC PLAN:

title: Scrum Master - Remote

You’ll work closely with team members and technical leads to set priorities, communicate progress, and address challenges before they affect delivery. The ideal candidate is a confident, approachable leader who can bring people together, coach teams through change, and help them take ownership of their work.

Compensation

$90,000 - $140,000


What You'll Accomplish

  • Work with three Scrum teams to facilitate all standard Scrum ceremonies, remove impediments, and navigate a scaled agile environment (release planning, quarterly planning).

title: Howard-NRDC Legal Fellow
description:
Overview

NRDC (the Natural Resources Defense Council) works to safeguard the Earth, its people, its plants and animals, and the natural systems on which all life depends. NRDC combines the power of more than 3 million members and online activists with the expertise of some 800 policy advocates, lawyers, scientists, and communication experts to confront the climate crisis, protect nature, ensure the rights of all people to clean air, clean water, and healthy communities. As an international nonprofit environmental organization, NRDC is working to address the world’s most urgent environmental challenges, and advance innovative, science-based, and enforceable solutions.

Since our founding in 1970, NRDC has helped craft and deliver many of America’s foundational environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act. Today, we continue to lead in advancing and defending strong environmental protections at the local, state, federal and international levels, as well as through the marketplace. Our team works across the United States and around the world, from offices in Chicago, Los Angeles, New York City, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C., as well as in Beijing, and New Delhi (a subsidiary of NRDC India Pvt. Ltd.).

Supported by our members and online activists, NRDC is driving impactful solutions that confront the climate crisis, defend nature and safeguard public health across Asia, Africa, and the Americas. At NRDC, we believe lasting change happens when people bring their talent, passion, and expertise together for a common purpose: to build a cleaner, healthier, and more resilient world. Learn more at nrdc.org

NRDC is seeking a Howard-NRDC Legal Fellow to work with the Litigation Team in one of our U.S.-based offices.

Position Summary

NRDC is seeking a recent graduate of Howard University School of Law to work as a fellow with the Litigation Team in one of our U.S. offices: Chicago; New York; San Francisco; Santa Monica; or Washington, D.C. This is a 2 year fellowship starting Fall 2027 through Fall 2029.

The Howard-NRDC Legal Fellowship is open to candidates who graduated from Howard University School of Law in 2024 or later, as well as current Howard Law students who will graduate this academic year (2026-2027). Applicants must be available to start no later than Fall 2027.

The position you are applying for is part of the bargaining unit represented by The Washington Baltimore News Guild (WBNG / The Newsguild-CWA Local 32035).

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the following essential functions:

  • Work with teams of lawyers and paralegals on active cases and case development projects, including by both providing support on cases led by senior attorneys and by leading cases, or substantial aspects of cases, under the supervision of senior attorneys.
  • Collaborate with NRDC program staff, clients, experts, and coalition and community partners to support litigation goals.
  • Conduct legal research and factual investigations.
  • Write briefs, motions, and memoranda.
  • When opportunities arise, participate in court hearings; engage in discovery and conduct record and document review; and/or prepare for and take depositions.
  • Contribute to the Team and NRDC’s litigation capacity in other ways, e.g., by managing legal intern hiring and supervision, serving on institutional committees, organizing continuing legal education (CLE) presentations and other trainings, building relationships with other components of NRDC and allied groups, and engaging in development outreach.

The above list of duties is not comprehensive but generally demonstrates the types of matters under this position’s responsibility. Other duties may be assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum Education & Experience:

  • A Juris Doctorate (J.D.) (graduation year 2024 or later) and 0 to 3 years of post-graduate experience.
  • Admitted to the the bar of the jurisdiction in which the applicant intends to practice, or willing to complete the requirements for admission to that bar before or during the first year of the fellowship. (NRDC covers a portion of any necessary bar exam and bar preparation expenses.)

Skills, Abilities, Competencies

  • Strong legal writing and analytical skills.
  • Strong oral communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and take initiative.
  • Ability to work effectively with a team.
  • Strong work ethic and growth mindset.
  • Ability to maintain composure and sense of humor under deadline pressure.
  • Ability to travel occasionally to other NRDC US offices and attend court hearings and other case-related meetings as appropriate (approximately 10% or less of total working time annually)
  • Demonstrated competency in working with people with different social identities than their own (including race, gender, sexual identity or orientation, age, class, and disability).
  • Creativity and resourcefulness.
  • Demonstrated commitment to public service, equity, or social justice.
  • Commitment to NRDC’s mission, values, and DEI principles

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position within the described work environment.

Frequently: Perform desk-based computer tasks

Frequently: Ability to interact and communicate with employees and others as necessary

Frequently: Attend planned meetings and collaborate with management and coworkers

Occasionally: Ability to attend events and activities in the office or offsite

Work is sometimes performed primarily in office. The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet in office settings and moderate in other situations. Hours of employment may sometimes require working flexible and/or longer hours, including nights and weekends, when necessitated by projects. The job includes work-related situations such as those involving challenging, important, urgent, time-sensitive, or multiple matters.

NRDC is committed to advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion, both in our work and in our workplace. We believe that celebrating and actively welcoming diverse voices and perspectives is essential to solving the planet's most pressing environmental problems, and we encourage applications from candidates whose identities have been historically under-represented in the environmental movement.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, marital status, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

We offer competitive salaries, excellent benefits, and a supportive working environment. Salary is based on a nonprofit scale and is commensurate with skills and experience. Internal equity will be reviewed and considered to determine a final offer. For this position, the salary range is $94,500 to $105,000.

Perks & Benefits

Not only do we care about taking care of our planet, we care about taking care of you. When you join our team, we invest in your total well-being. Here is a small glimpse on how we plan to support you:

  • Time to Unplug & Recharge: Enjoy a generous time-off policy, highlighted by a company-wide year-end Rest & Recharge Week to reset for the new year.
  • Family – First: Generous family leave policy beyond federal requirements for all NRDCers
  • For your Future: Matching 403b whether you contribute or not
  • Hybrid Policy: The freedom to balance your time around your needs that means, 8 days per month in-office. In-office day requirements can be met with off-site work events such as retreats, conferences, and other work-related travel.
  • Well – being: Premium Comprehensive healthcare and mental health programs.

To apply, visit www.nrdc.org/careers and upload your résumé and cover letter. Please mention where you saw this posting and upload any additional materials that showcase your abilities. Due to the high volume of applications, we will contact only those candidates we would like to interview. Please no phone calls, emails, or in-person résumé drop-offs.

If you experience technical problems while applying or if you are a person with a disability and need assistance applying online, please reach out to iCIMS Customer Care at 1-800-889-4422.

For more about NRDC, visit www.nrdc.org.

title: EMEA Service Supply Chain Planner
description:
EMEA Service Supply Chain Planner

Description -

Job scope/summary:

The scope of the SSC Print Planning team is to plan, source and deploy across EMEA the right printing commercial and consumer parts to our customers: Break-Fix (Onsite/Channel/MPS) / Part sales (RPB) / MPS supplies.

The Supply Chain Planner will manage a given portfolio /product line; he/she will plan inventory for EMEA Network for the products assigned to drive high level of availability within the inventory limitations, minimizing SC planning related costs.

Planning activity for a specific portfolio:

  • End-to-End Planning: Maintain part availability to support customer needs: Calculate the needs for spare parts (or Whole Unit Exchange), place appropriate supplier Purchase Orders and monitor the planned deliveries from suppliers.
  • Inventory Management: Manage inventory in EMEA Network (Central warehouse, Virtual Hubs, Country Hubs) by defining inventory targets for all EMEA locations.
  • Lifecycle Management: Work on problems of diverse complexity and scope (New Product Intro, Life-Time Buys, Rolls, Upgrades, others)
  • Customer Delivery Performance: Analyze planning performance of the products assigned; timely spot deviations and launch effective mitigation plan

  • Manage Good Inventory Scrap costs (Excess & Obsolescence) –
  • Minimize Planning-driven costs (Inbound, exception, airfreight, rebalancing, reverse)
  • Develop Finance / Cost acumen linked to planning activity, understand the cost impacts and balance with SL expected results
  • Bring creative ideas to improve Cost and/or SL. Develop data analysis capability in order to prioritize actions that will strongly influence results.

Key deliverables/accountabilities:

  • Inventory: Gross inventory
  • Operational : Material availability & delivery performance (LOF, Fill Rate, Backlog)

Internal:

  • SCOAH
  • Field & Channel
  • RPB
  • Category and MPS

External:

Other requirements:

  • Fluent in English language

Personal skills and qualities:

description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit

Reporting to the Senior Vice-President, Marketing, Personal and Business Banking, the Vice-President, Enterprise Media & Owned Channels is accountable for leading CIBC’s enterprise media ecosystem across paid media, owned channels, and generative visibility. This role drives client acquisition, brand equity, digital adoption, and revenue growth across lines of business through enterprise media strategy, performance marketing, owned channel delivery, organic social leadership for Personal and Business Banking, and the development of modern agile marketing capabilities.

The Vice-President operates as Chapter Area Lead for Enterprise Media & Owned Channels within CIBC’s agile operating model, leading a chapter area of approximately 225 marketing professionals. The operating model reflects a deliberate two-speed structure: chapter members supporting Personal and Business Banking (PBB) are forward-deployed into PBB Crews and Squads, while non-PBB execution is delivered through dedicated Centres of Excellence (COEs) within the Chapter Area. This leader is accountable for chapter capability, craft excellence, career development, operating standards, and culture, while ensuring high-quality business delivery across both forward-deployed and centralized execution models.

CIBC employee experience principles:

  • Always professional… so our team members can excel and be their best professional self.
  • Radically simple… so our team members can focus on what they need to do and make an impact.
  • Genuinely caring… so our team members can feel valued for who they are and what they contribute.

CIBC leadership capabilities:

  • Envisions the future…to innovate purposefully to create new value and harness new capabilities in order to meet the evolving needs of our diverse stakeholders.
  • Inspires hearts and minds…to build an inclusive culture where we make bold choices, collaborate, and empower others to take chances and do what’s right for our stakeholders.
  • Drives action and impact, together…to align with urgency around what matters, making decisions with speed and always making a real difference.

What You’ll be Doing

  • Serve as Chapter Area Lead for Enterprise Media & Owned Channels, accountable for the capability, craft, career development, and culture of approximately 225 media and owned channel professionals.
  • Forward-deploy chapter members into PBB Crews and Squads while maintaining dedicated COEs for non-PBB execution, balancing delivery commitments with chapter-level standards, talent development, and operational excellence.
  • Act as a change leader in CIBC’s agile operating model, guiding teams through agile ways of working and adapting media, owned channel, and discovery strategies into iterative, test-and-learn delivery models.
  • Define and continuously evolve the chapter resourcing model, determining the optimal blend of internal talent, agency partnerships, freelance or contingent support, offshore or nearshore capabilities, and AI-enabled solutions to deliver a scalable and flexible enterprise capability.
  • Develop and lead CIBC’s enterprise paid media strategy across digital and traditional channels, including paid search, paid social, programmatic display, video, audio, out-of-home, and broadcast.
  • Champion performance marketing to drive acquisition, digital sales, and measurable ROI through optimization, personalization, retargeting, and disciplined media investment allocation.
  • Oversee enterprise paid media investment allocation, agency relationships, platform partnerships, and trading partnerships to maximize reach, efficiency, and business outcomes, ensuring recommendations align with strategic priorities and are reviewed with business partners prior to execution.

title: Technology Security Engineer
description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

Perth Airport is Australia’s Western Hub connecting the people, businesses and communities of Western Australia with the rest of Australia and the world. Operating 24 hours a day, seven days a week throughout the year, Perth Airport plays a significant role in providing economic, social and cultural benefits to West Australians

We are delivering a $5 billion infrastructure program to transform the airport, including new and expanded terminals, a parallel runway, multi-storey car parks and our first on site hotel. This investment will deliver a single, integrated airport precinct and a world class passenger experience.

Beyond aviation, the Perth Airport estate spans more than 2,100 hectares and supports a $1.5 billion portfolio of industrial and commercial assets, with significant opportunities for future development.

We are on the lookout for a Technology Security Engineer to help protect and strengthen the cyber security of Perth Airport’s technology environment. Working closely with cyber security specialists and technology teams, you will play a hands on role in monitoring security threats, managing security platforms, driving compliance with cyber security policies, and responding to incidents.

About the Role

  • Monitor the organisation’s cyber security posture and respond to alerts, threats and vulnerabilities in a timely manner.
  • Manage and maintain key security platforms including SIEM, endpoint security, email security, privileged access management and logging tools.
  • Identify, test, package and coordinate the deployment of security patches across a diverse technology environment.
  • Lead the investigation and response to cyber security incidents, providing technical expertise and post incident analysis.
  • Produce accurate and timely reporting on cyber security performance, risks and compliance activities.
  • Review and assess technology changes to ensure cyber security risks are appropriately managed before implementation.
  • Coordinate security audits, penetration testing and compliance activities to support ongoing risk management.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage AI and automation to improve security outcomes, operational efficiency and decision making.


About You

  • Tertiary qualifications in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cyber Security or a related discipline, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in systems administration or cyber security, with exposure to enterprise security technologies and environments.
  • Strong knowledge of cyber security frameworks and standards such as NIST and ISO 27001.
  • Experience supporting technologies such as SIEM, SCCM, Microsoft 365 security tools, vulnerability management platforms and malware protection solutions.
  • Sound understanding of authentication technologies including Active Directory, public key infrastructure and multi factor authentication.
  • Strong technical knowledge of networking, firewalls, proxies and Windows and Unix operating systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build trusted relationships across technical and business stakeholders.
  • A collaborative and results focused approach, with the ability to remain calm under pressure, make timely decisions and adapt in a fast paced environment.
  • Customer focused and proactive, with a commitment to finding practical solutions and delivering positive outcomes.
  • A willingness to embrace AI enabled technologies, apply sound judgement to AI generated outputs and support responsible and secure AI use.

Why Join Perth Airport?

title: Commercial Review Appraiser
description:
OH0713 NW Bancshares HQ

Job Description

The Commercial Review Appraiser independently engages qualified appraisers and evaluators, establishes the appropriate valuation product and scope of work, and reviews commercial and residential appraisals and evaluations for compliance, credibility, and supportability. The role exercises independent judgment and discretion in determining the acceptability of real estate valuations for credit decisions, prepares clear and well-supported review memoranda that communicate valuation conclusions and identified risks, and escalates matters when appropriate and in accordance with policy/procedures. The position supports the integrity and independence of the Bank's real estate valuation program, contributes to vendor management activities, and assists with policy and procedure development, reporting, market analysis, valuation validations, and special projects.

Essential Functions
• Determine the appropriate valuation product and scope of work based on the collateral, transaction risk, and policy/regulatory requirements.
• Engage qualified appraisers or evaluators and exercise independent judgement in vendor selection, assignment complexity, scope expectations, and deliverable acceptability. Monitor active job pipeline to ensure SLAs are satisfied and communicate delays when appropriate.
• Independently review commercial and/or residential appraisals, in accordance with policy, for credibility, compliance, supportability, and adequacy for credit decisions.
• Maintain appraisal independence and adhere to USPAP, FIRREA Title XI, Interagency Appraisal and Evaluation Guidelines, and Northwest policies and procedures.
• Validate existing valuation valuations and provide acceptance sign-offs for third-party appraisal reviews when appropriate.
• Analyze market data, valuation trends, collateral risk, and report findings for Lending, Credit and Management use.
• Contribute to vendor management, approved appraiser/evaluator monitoring, service quality, and appraiser list governance.
• Act in a consultative capacity, working with credit and other internal partners to assess risk and stay abreast to market conditions.
• Identify, communicate, and independently resolve valuation, scope, compliance, or process issues; escalate material exceptions as appropriate.
• Contribute to appraisal/evaluation policy, procedures, workflow management, reporting, and market analysis enhancements.
• Provide support to Collateral Services Specialists.
• Complete special projects and provide valuation support for portfolio, REO, acquisition-related, and other department initiatives as assigned.
• Maintain strong knowledge of current regulations, standards and practices associated with real property valuation.
• Administer collateral workflow platform.

Additional Essential Functions
• Ensure compliance with Northwest’s policies and procedures, and Federal/State regulations
• Navigate Microsoft Office Software, computer applications, and software specific to the department in order to maximize technology tools and gain efficiency
• Work as part of a team
• Work with on-site equipment

Safety and Health for those without supervisory duties

• Perform work tasks in a safe manner
• Report any and all injuries to supervisor
• Know what to do in case of an emergency

QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education
Bachelor's Degree

Work Experience
5 - 6 years Preparing appraisals and/or reviewing appraisals And
2 - 3 years Working within a bank appraisal department

General Employee Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
• Ability to establish effective working relationships among team members and participate in solving problems and making decisions
• Ability to present and express ideas and information clearly and concisely in a manner appropriate to the audience, whether oral or written
• Ability to actively listen to what others are saying to achieve understanding, sharing information with others and facilitating the open exchange of ideas and information
• Ability to establish courses of action for self to accomplish specific goals, develop and use tracking systems for monitoring own work progress, and effectively use resources such as time and information

title: OR Surgical Tech(Full-Time, Varied Shifts)
description:
Job Title: Surgical Technologist
Department: Operating Room
Location: Rochester General Hospital
Hours Per Week: 40 Hrs.
Schedule: 7a-3:30p; 3p-11:30p, 11p-7:30a

SUMMARY:

The Surgical Technologist plays a vital role as a key member of the surgical team, serving as the primary scrub technologist during procedures. This individual is responsible for preparing, organizing, and managing surgical instruments, supplies, and equipment to ensure efficient and safe operations. The Surgical Technologist maintains strict adherence to sterile techniques and demonstrates continuous attention to preserving the integrity of the sterile field throughout each procedure.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Maintain a minimum of 15 Continuing Medical Education hours annually.
  • Prepare and check instruments, equipment, and supplies for surgical procedures.
  • Set up and maintain a sterile field, following strict aseptic techniques.
  • Assist with patient draping and ensure the surgical team is properly attired.
  • Pass instruments and supplies to the surgeon during procedures.
  • Perform accurate sponge and sharp counts with the circulating nurse.
  • Clean and prepare instruments for sterilization.
  • Support specialty surgical services and stock OR rooms as needed.
  • Prepare sterile dressings and assist with post-operative care.
  • Help orient new staff and contribute to unit goals and objectives.
  • May handle medications, sharps, and syringes on the sterile field.



REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Candidates must meet one of the following requirements:

  • Graduated from a CAAHEP- or ABHES-accredited Surgical Technology program and obtain certification through a nationally accredited credentialing organization within 12 months of graduation.
  • Graduated from an accredited school of practical nursing.
  • Qualify under the "Grandfathering Clause" by providing proof of at least one year of employment as a surgical technologist in a healthcare facility between December 31, 2010, and December 31, 2014.
  • Qualify under the "Hard-to-Fill Clause" by graduating from an accredited program and obtain certification through a nationally accredited credentialing organization within 24 months of hire.

New Graduates:
• Official transcript from accredited school or letter emailed directly from the school’s registrar’s office confirming program completion will be accepted upon graduation.
• Primary source education verification required within 90 days of start date.

EDUCATION:

LICENSES / CERTIFICATIONS:

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Heavy - Clinical - Heavy clinical roles require continual lifting of more than 50 lbs., pushing and pulling patients or equipment, and working in physically awkward or restrictive positions. Staff must maintain balance and coordination in confined, uneven, or emergent care settings while performing both fine and gross motor tasks. High sensory acuity is needed to recognize patient cues and environmental alerts. Emotional and cognitive demands are significant due to urgent decision-making, managing distressed patients, and functioning effectively in high-pressure clinical situations. Environmental exposures commonly include infectious agents, biohazards, noise, and chemicals. Employees may be required to complete mask-fit testing, TB screening, and participate in extended or on-call shifts.

For disease specific care programs refer to the program specific requirements of the department for further specifications on experience and educational expectations, including continuing education requirements.

Any physical requirements reported by a prospective employee and/or employee’s physician or delegate will be considered for accommodations.

Our design teams are involved with every step of the process bringing these world class products to life. From conducting end user research to identify new needs, to designing and prototyping tools to ensure we meet our customers high expectations, to creating robust tests to guarantee the tools we make stand up to the toughest environments, our engineers own every aspect of the process along the way.

The Job

You’re a strong problem solver who loves digging into the details to fully understand what is going on. You have fixed a lot of problems, so you know how sort out what is meaningful and what is not to be as efficient as possible. You have run DOE’s and done the statistics to make well informed decisions.   • Experience with product development: Design, DFM, root cause analysis, test instrumentation and data acquisition and analysis
  • Quality - use of statistical tools, process capability, DOE’s, stack-ups
  • Coordination of internal and external resources
  • Accountable for managing the design process and owning the results
  • Enjoy Full/fast-paced design cycles that average 2 years and a dynamic work environment
  • Possible international travel to visit manufacturing locations

title: Vice-President, Digital Discoverability and Shopping
description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit

The Vice-President, Digital Discoverability and Shopping (Crew Lead) is a senior enterprise leadership role accountable for both the steady-state performance and the transformational agenda of CIBC’s pre-authorization public-facing digital presence across all business segments and across Canada and the United States.
This role sits at the intersection of strategy, technology, design, data, content, governance, and people leadership, requiring the ability to inspire and align a large, multi-disciplinary organization behind a single, ambitious vision.

The Crew Lead owns end-to-end business accountability for CIBC’s digital discoverability and digital storefront ecosystem. This includes ensuring CIBC is discoverable and compelling across search engines, AI-powered search experiences, organic social media, online communities, creator ecosystems, and other emerging discovery channels.

The role leads a materially scaled organization and is accountable for crew operating model decisions, prioritization, roadmap trade-offs, transformation delivery, and cross-domain alignment. The role also shapes standards and decisions beyond one team through significant enterprise influence across Marketing, Technology, PR/Communications, Legal, Compliance, and business segment leaders.

CIBC employee experience principles:

  • Always professional… so our team members can excel and be their best professional self.
  • Radically simple… so our team members can focus on what they need to do and make an impact.
  • Genuinely caring… so our team members can feel valued for who they are and what they contribute.

CIBC leadership capabilities:

  • Envisions the future…to innovate purposefully to create new value and harness new capabilities in order to meet the evolving needs of our diverse stakeholders.
  • Inspires hearts and minds…to build an inclusive culture where we make bold choices, collaborate, and empower others to take chances and do what’s right for our stakeholders.
  • Drives action and impact, together…to align with urgency around what matters, making decisions with speed and always making a real difference.

What You’ll be Doing


Strategy & Roadmap Leadership

  • Define and maintain the enterprise digital discoverability and storefront strategy and multi-horizon roadmap aligned to enterprise marketing OKRs and business segment priorities across Canada and the U.S.
  • Own strategic and operational accountability for both long-term modernization and day-to-day performance of the digital storefront, balancing business growth, client experience, governance, and risk.
  • Represent the function in senior planning, prioritization, and investment discussions, with meaningful influence over enterprise roadmap and budget decisions.

People Leadership & Crew Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop a large, multi-disciplinary crew, including senior product and delivery leaders.
  • Set a clear vision, priorities, and ways of working while fostering a high-performance, inclusive culture.
  • Drive cross-squad alignment, resolve prioritization conflicts, and build strong leadership capability across the organization.
  • Model agile ways of working and lead through ambiguity, scale, and transformation.

Digital Discoverability, SEO & Generative Visibility

  • Own SEO strategy and execution across all pre-authorization pages in Canada and the U.S., including technical SEO, keyword strategy, content optimization, metadata, tagging, and Core Web Vitals management.
  • Develop content and authority-building strategies designed to increase CIBC citation frequency and brand presence within large language model outputs.
  • Monitor the evolving AI search landscape and assess implications for financial product discovery across both markets.

Organic Social, Community & Influencer Discoverability

  • Own and execute CIBC’s organic social media program for discoverability and generative visibility, with accountability for strategy, production, publishing, discoverability, and performance across relevant platforms.
  • Lead the development of platform-specific content strategies and discoverability playbooks that optimize formats, cadence, keywords, hashtags, and recommendation performance.
  • Develop CIBC’s strategy for authentic visibility in online communities and forums that increasingly shape search and AI-generated outcomes.
  • Own creator marketing execution end-to-end to ensure CIBC is discoverable, credible, and compelling across AI-powered search and answer engines,, including talent identification, vetting, contracting, campaign execution, measurement, and long-term relationship management.
  • Ensure all activity aligns with enterprise brand governance, compliance requirements, escalation protocols, and market-specific regulations.

Industry Awards, Digital PR & Brand Authority Building

  • Partner with PR/Communications on the enterprise industry awards strategy ensuring the program is a measurable driver of SEO authority and AI search visibility.
  • Develop a digital PR strategy with Communications and PR teams to strengthen CIBC’s online authority through earned media, third-party citations, and high-domain-authority backlinks.
  • Monitor competitor activity and industry trends to identify authority-building gaps and opportunities.
  • Ensure award recognition and brand authority signals are reflected across relevant digital properties and knowledge platforms where appropriate.

Web Experience Design, Shared Capabilities & UX

  • Lead UX design strategy and continuous optimization, including user research, usability testing, information architecture, journey mapping, and always-on analytics-driven improvement.
  • Own discovery-to-application journey optimization and friction reduction across client journeys.
  • Champion mobile-first and accessibility-first design principles across digital experiences.
  • Provide business ownership for shared customer-facing capabilities such as site search, appointment booking, chatbot, and branch/location finder where applicable.

Content Strategy, Publishing Operations & Management

  • Define and own the enterprise content strategy for the pre-authorization digital presence, ensuring content is on-brand, compliant, bilingual where required, and optimized for user experience, SEO, GEO, social discoverability, and influencer amplification.
  • Oversee the content governance model, including publishing workflows, review and approval processes, and content standards across Canada and the U.S.
  • Lead cross-domain prioritization and coordination across publishing squads to deliver stable, error-free, and timely digital releases.

Analytics, Performance Reporting & Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO)

  • Own web analytics implementation and governance, including tagging, tracking, metadata standards, and data integrity across markets.
  • Own the CRO strategy and testing roadmap, including A/B and multivariate testing to improve client experience and conversion performance.
  • Analyze user behavior data such as heatmaps, session recordings, funnel analytics, and self-serve outcomes to identify and remove friction points.
  • Develop clear performance dashboards and attribution approaches that connect discoverability signals to downstream business outcomes.

AI Integration & Operational Efficiency

  • Maintain a crew-level AI adoption roadmap, identifying opportunities to embed AI across user-facing experiences and internal operations.
  • Drive the use of AI to automate and streamline back-end processes including content publishing, QA, tagging, reporting, and workflow efficiency.
  • Ensure AI adoption aligns with enterprise governance, privacy, compliance, and risk standards.

Technology & Platform Management

  • Partner closely with Marketing Technology, Engineering, and related teams on CMS-related integrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure dependencies, security, and compliance requirements.
  • Ensure site reliability, performance, and uptime standards are met through strong partnership with platform owners and technology teams.
  • Evaluate and enable tools and platforms that support discoverability, content operations, analytics, and performance optimization.

Transition & Transformation

  • Lead the formal transition of website and discoverability accountability from current teams, including knowledge transfer, documentation, and technical debt remediation.
  • Define and execute the digital storefront transformation roadmap, including platform modernization, search and discovery modernization, journey optimization, publishing governance, and new ways of working.
  • Build new-to-bank capabilities across social, online communities, influencers, awards, and emerging discovery channels to make CIBC the answer wherever prospects search.

Governance, Compliance & Risk

  • Ensure all website content, experiences, social activity, influencer programs, community engagement, and marketing claims meet regulatory and legal requirements across Canada and the U.S.
  • Maintain governance standards for content accuracy, accessibility, compliance, brand alignment, escalation protocols, and crisis response across all digital channels and markets.

What We’re Looking For

  • 12–18 years of progressive experience in digital marketing, web strategy, digital product management, or integrated brand and discoverability strategy
  • 7–10 years of people leadership experience, including success leading large, multi-disciplinary teams in complex, matrixed organizations
  • Demonstrated experience leading leaders, owning high-traffic consumer-facing digital experiences, driving measurable performance outcomes across multiple markets, and leading large-scale digital transformation initiatives
  • Strong experience in agile operating models, organic social at scale, influencer strategy and execution, community engagement, awards programs, and cross-border operations across Canada and the United States.
  • Financial services or other highly regulated industry experience is strongly preferred.
  • Deep expertise in SEO, technical SEO, content optimization, GEO, AI search, organic social strategy, influencer marketing, online communities, UX, information architecture, conversion optimization, analytics platforms, CMS and digital marketing tooling, and AI-enabled operational improvement.
  • Strong stakeholder management, strategic thinking, storytelling, and the ability to translate complex insights into compelling narratives for senior leadership.
  • Consumer-obsessed, externally oriented, inspiring, collaborative, systems-minded, and able to lead at scale through ambiguity while balancing action with sound judgment in a regulated, multi-market environment.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential.

  • We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive compensation, a banking benefit*, wellbeing support and additional offers such as employee and family assistance programs and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.

title: Data Engineer I
description:

Relationship – Pursuing depth, trust, and collaboration

Data reporting and insights: standardized and optimized reports and performance trackers for U.S. teams and clients
Analytical storytelling: leveraging data to tell a compelling story
Software development: supporting the dynamic needs of our team
Tool creation: building easy-to-use solutions to complex data problems
Data operations and cloud data management: building and maintaining data pipelines from source systems to cloud data storage, and retrieving data from a wide variety of sources
About the Role

The Data Engineer I contributes to the development, testing, and maintenance of data pipelines that power Harvest Group's data products across retail partners including Walmart, Sam's Club, Target, Amazon, Costco, and Kroger. This is an entry-level engineering role focused on building foundational skills in SQL, transformation frameworks, and cloud data platforms. The Data Engineer I works alongside senior engineers to deliver reliable, well-tested data transformations and models. This role combines the core competencies of data architecture and data operations into a unified engineering discipline.

What You'll Do

Develop and test transformation models and SQL following team conventions and coding standards.
Support the build-out of new data pipelines for retailer data products alongside senior engineers.
Investigate and resolve data quality issues escalated from product support.
Write and maintain data tests, schema documentation, and source freshness checks.
Monitor scheduled pipeline runs and troubleshoot basic failures.
Participate in Agile/Scrum delivery, including sprint planning, daily standups, and retrospectives.
Participate in code reviews, learning from feedback and improving over time.
Document resolutions, processes, and data lineage in the team knowledge base.
Grow your understanding of the retail data landscape and how Harvest Group technology supports clients across multiple retailers.
What We're Looking For

Required
Working SQL skills, including joins, aggregations, CTEs, and window functions.
Familiarity with version control (Git) and collaborative development workflows.
Curiosity, attention to detail, and demonstrated follow-through.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Ability to collaborate effectively with U.S.-based teams and clients across time zones.
Ownership mindset with a proactive approach to problem solving and continuous improvement.
Nice to Have
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, or equivalent experience.
Exposure to a SQL-based transformation framework (dbt preferred).
Exposure to a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift).
Familiarity with an orchestration platform (Airflow, Astro, or Prefect).
Basic Python scripting for data processing and automation.
Understanding of data modeling patterns (dimensional modeling, normalization).
Exposure to CPG or retail data (Kroger / 84.51, Walmart / Luminate, Nielsen, Circana).
We encourage all interested candidates to apply.

Please note that we only accept resumes submitted in English.

Job Summary:

Oregon State University's Center for Advocacy, Prevention & Education (CAPE) is seeking a CAPE Specialist to fill a full-time, 9-month, professional faculty vacancy at our Cascades Campus in Bend, OR.


This position will work both work as confidential & legally privileged advocate and will be providing prevention & education outreach related to gender-based violence and sexual health.

This position focuses on comprehensive gender based violence prevention and education (including sexual health), using theory driven and evidence informed practices to foster safe, supportive and inclusive learning and living environments at Oregon State University Cascades. Additionally, this position provides confidential and legally privileged advocacy services (including safety planning, academic & housing support, accompaniment support for medical & legal needs, emotional support and other resources/referrals) to those in the University community who have experienced gender-based violence (sexual assault, dating/domestic violence, stalking and sexual harassment/discrimination).


Key Responsibilities:


  • Assist in the creation, planning, implementation, and facilitation of CAPE programming and community-based events and activities
  • Facilitate CAPE workshops to various groups across campus, on the topics of gender-based violence, sexual health, consent, survivor support, trauma informed care, etc.
  • Provides confidential, survivor-centered advocacy to those who have experienced complex or complicated interpersonal violence situations, including experiences that occurred prior to a student’s arrival to the university. Connects survivors to various campus and community entities providing services (such as Counseling and Psychological Services, University Housing and Dining, the Bridge, Student Health & Wellness and the Office of Equal Opportunity and Access, etc); accompanies survivors as needed throughout reporting processes (Title IX, Equal Opportunity and Access, and law enforcement) and evidence collection exams; and directly provides academic and housing accommodations as needed. Advocates connect survivors to broader systems, and provide emotional support and care throughout the process.
  • Build partnerships and collaborate with key stakeholders on and off campus to develop comprehensive sexual health, gender based violence prevention, and survivor support programming
  • Assist with assessment efforts and data collection, analytic strategies and report writing
  • Serve on committees within SHS, CAPE and other relevant university and community committees.




Qualifications:

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field such as public health, community health, health promotion, education, human development, social work, psychology, or related field
  • Advocacy experience at full time equivalency - 2 years "Two years providing direct service in an advocate role to survivors of gender-based violence as primary job duty"
  • Prevention/Education at full time equivalency - 2 years “Two years of experience working in sexual health, gender-based violence prevention, peer education, and/or health promotion”
  • Possess relevant statewide certifications regarding advocacy training
  • Ability to pass criminal background, drive University vehicle
  • Demonstrated knowledge, understanding and interest in gender-based violence prevention and sexual health education
  • Demonstrated ability to use independent judgment and make ethical decisions
  • Demonstrated commitment to inclusive excellence.

This position is designated as a critical or security-sensitive position; therefore, the incumbent must successfully complete a criminal history check and be determined to be position qualified as per University Standard: 05-010 et seq. Incumbents are required to self-report convictions and those in youth programs may have additional criminal history checks every 24 months.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s Degree in relevant field of study
  • Experience and competency serving in advocacy or counseling to underserved and traditionally marginalized student groups such as but not limited to LGBTQ+ communities, BIPOC students, international students, survivors with disabilities, first-generation survivors, survivors with high financial need
  • Experience working in a university setting
  • CHES/MCHES certification
  • Bilingual (Spanish preferred)
  • Experience speaking in front of diverse audiences and the ability to adapt materials quickly so that the audience can understand the concepts being presented.

$57,275-$69,500

2027-01-04

Your work will span digital platforms for clients, as well as the tools and workflows used by frontline teams. You'll lead design across projects at different stages, from open-ended problems that require research, discovery, and clear experience direction to initiatives that need detailed designs, testing, and close collaboration with delivery teams. You'll consider how the client journey moves between digital services and frontline support to create connected, intuitive experiences. In this role, you'll help shape thoughtful, inclusive, and practical design solutions that improve experiences for both clients and employees.


At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.


How you'll succeed


  • Lead end-to-end design - Lead design from discovery through delivery by framing problems, identifying user needs, exploring concepts, and translating the chosen direction into clear, usable designs. Create journey maps, service flows, wireframes, prototypes, detailed screens, and design specifications as needed.
  • Design connected experiences - Consider the full journey across client and frontline platforms, including what clients can do independently, what employees need to provide support, and where guidance or handoffs are required.
  • Use evidence to inform decisions - Partner with researchers and stakeholders to plan and interpret interviews, usability testing, analytics, and other feedback. Apply insights to refine designs and clearly communicate your recommendations.
  • Collaborate with delivery teams - Work closely with product managers, content designers, researchers, developers, business analysts, and other designers. Clarify interactions and requirements, respond to implementation questions, and adapt designs as teams learn.
  • Build alignment and drive clarity - Facilitate workshops and design discussions, present work to stakeholders, and make trade-offs clear. Bring structure to ambiguous problems and help teams move toward informed decisions.
  • Elevate design quality - Apply design system patterns, accessibility standards, and inclusive design principles. Contribute new patterns or enhancements when existing guidance doesn't fully meet user or business needs.

Who you are


  • You have relevant experience. You bring 8+ years of experience designing digital products, and your portfolio demonstrates your contribution to both early exploration and delivered experiences. Experience designing for complex services or regulated environments is an asset.
  • You give meaning to data. You understand user research and know how to translate findings, data, and stakeholder input into practical design decisions that improve the user experience.
  • You're digitally savvy. You're proficient in Figma and prototyping, and you have experience designing for web and mobile platforms. You understand inclusive design and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) accessibility standards.
  • You act like an owner. You can work independently, manage multiple priorities, and maintain momentum when requirements or direction change. You take accountability for moving work forward and delivering high-quality outcomes.
  • You're motivated by collective success. You communicate clearly, explain the reasoning behind your work, listen to different perspectives, and build trusted partnerships with colleagues and stakeholders.
  • Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

title: Education Coordinator
location: Hillsboro, OR, Enterprise Site, Washington County
description:
About Oregon Child Development Coalition (OCDC):

Oregon Child Development Coalition (OCDC) is a nonprofit organization serving children and families across Oregon through early education and family support programs. At OCDC, our work has purpose. Every role contributes to creating stronger families, healthier communities, and brighter futures for children across Oregon.


Position Summary:

The Education Coordinator implements a developmentally and culturally appropriate education program in compliance with Agency policies and procedures and Head Start Performance Standards.


Essential Functions:

Classroom Observations:

  • Observes classrooms for developmentally appropriate practices, required posted materials, adequate and appropriate materials, safety/sanitation, and other Agency required guidelines.

Documentation:

  • Maintains complete and accurate required records, forms, reports and documentation of classroom monitoring and observations.
  • Completes reports on time.
  • Determines what documents to transfer to the transition program.

Guidance and Support:

  • Reviews weekly planning forms and children’s files and provides appropriate feedback and guidance to ensure compliance with agency policies and guidelines.
  • Supervises preparation of classrooms in order to provide a safe environment.
  • Provides supports through entire skills acquisition process.
  • Assists teachers to plan transition activities for children.
  • Guides the teacher toward improved skills in observing and assessing children on an ongoing basis, link this information to individualizing learning experiences and follow children’s progress over time.
  • Demonstrates the knowledge and skills to guide staff in implementing, observing, and evaluating culturally and linguistically appropriate research-based curricula to support diverse children and families.
  • Assists staff to use evidence-based practical, preventive strategies to both decrease the occurrence of challenging behavior and promote young children’s social competence.
  • Performs an assessment of staff needs through observation and communication.

Monitoring:

  • Monitors children’s files and lesson plans for compliance and developmentally appropriate practices.
  • Ensures use of appropriate Agency approved developmentally appropriate curriculums as well as including an anti-bias approach.
  • Ensures that pre-school teachers provide children with quality materials and experiences to promote all areas of development to meet the Head Start Child Outcomes.
  • Reviews all paperwork prepared by teachers.
  • Uses effective strategies for tracking staff progress over time to determine if staff has actually acquired new knowledge and skills as a result of mentoring and coaching.

Coordination:

  • Coordinates developmental screenings, organizing schedules and preparing materials.
  • Coordinates education, mental health, and disabilities training and technical assistance to staff and families.

Implementation:

  • Plans, reviews, assesses, and designs strategies for successful implementation of the Agency education, mental health, and disabilities plan.

Collaboration:

  • Collaborates with Education Supervisor and Content Specialists to coordinate training at local pre-service for staff and throughout the season for staff and families.
  • Collaborates and integrates with other service areas in determining and defining needs, and delivering training.
  • Collaborates with Education Supervisor and Management Team on designing follow-up to trainings which ensure skills acquisition.
  • Collaborates with Family and Health Services in the transition of families and children into public school in the areas of education, mental health, and disabilities.
  • Collaborates with Family and Health Services staff in coordinating meetings with teachers from OCDC and public schools.
  • Collaborates with Site Coordinators to maintain classroom with required furnishings, materials, and supplies.
  • Collaborates with Family and Health Services staff in assisting parents with the transition process.
  • Collaborates with all program service staff and managers to ensure developmentally appropriate inclusion in the classroom of required topics and procedures.
  • Works with other coordinators to ensure an integrated and coordinated transition process.
  • Assists County Management placement team in placement of children in the classroom.

Integration:

  • Administers program integration in the county.
  • Participates in Case Management Team (CMT) meetings.
  • Participates in referrals and Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) development, as needed.

Training:

  • Conducts training for staff and parents as required.
  • Meets with teaching classroom staff on a regular basis to answer questions and provide technical assistance.
  • Demonstrates knowledge and skills in adult learning styles.

Purchasing and Inventory:

  • Ensures that ordering, purchasing, receiving, and distributing materials needed promptly by classrooms in accordance with Agency purchasing guidelines.
  • Maintains inventory control of all educational materials and equipment.

Communications:

  • Maintains and supports integrative communication system with staff.
  • Plans and facilitates weekly teacher meetings.
  • Meets with Education Supervisor on a regular basis to discuss concerns/needs.
  • Meets with other program coordinators as necessary.
  • Informs parents of identified concerns and maintaining required forms.
  • Provides on-going information to parents via memos, home visits, telephone, and personal contact.
  • Maintains close communication with the Family and Health Services Supervisor and Family Advocates regarding children with health needs.
  • Communicates and problem solves with staff.
  • Demonstrates interpersonal skills.

Referrals:

  • Reviews screenings in order to make appropriate referrals.
  • Follows up continually on referrals and IFSP goals within required timelines.

Program Knowledge:

  • Assures that education and mental health activities correlate with established goals, objectives and work plans.
  • Assures program compliance with Head Start Performance Standards, Office of Child Care Division regulations, and other applicable rules.

Supervision:

  • Leads and monitors daily operations.
  • Communicates effectively to build trust.
  • Recruits, selects, orientates, and supervises education, mental health, and disabilities staff.
  • Conducts timely performance evaluations as required and as necessary.
  • Provides on-going individual feedback toward the goal of effective performance through modeling, coaching, recognition/praise, and corrective action as appropriate and in a timely manner.
  • Provides guidance and support to staff developing skills and progress in their position.
  • Provides and supports professional development and training opportunities for staff.
  • Reviews and authorizes staff time records and overtime to ensure compliance with Agency policies and procedures in regard to wage and hour laws and regulations if applicable.

Professional Development:

  • Maintains professional and technical knowledge.
  • Attends designated educational workshops, trainings and seminars, establishing personal networks, participating in training and coordinating activities as part of the statewide OCDC team.

Skill and Knowledge Development:

  • Maintains skill and technical knowledge in assigned subject area.
  • Attends educational workshops, trainings and seminars, establishing personal networks to maintain expertise in field.

Professional and Ethical Conduct:

  • Supports Our Mission, What We Do, and Our Vision and Values in daily activities.
  • Demonstrates and applies continually the principles and values of OCDC’s Code of Ethics, Code of Behavior, and Code of Conduct.
  • Maintains confidence and protects agency operations by keeping information confidential in compliance with OCDC policy and procedures.
  • Applies safety practices in all facets of the performance of duties in compliance with safety standards and immediately reports any unsafe or hazardous working conditions and/or any injury.
  • Abides by the Head Start Standards of Conduct.

Mandatory First Responder:

  • Provides emergency services.
  • Responding to child/adult emergencies by using First Aid and CPR skills.
  • Contacting appropriate medical personnel.
  • Ensuring documentation related to incident is completed.
  • Participating in fire drills and assisting in the evacuation of the children.

Other:

  • Performs other work related or assigned duties.

Education and Experience Requirements:

  • BA/BS degree or higher in Early Childhood Education or Child Development

  • OR

  • BA/BS degree or higher in any field and coursework equivalent to a major relating to early childhood education, with an Oregon Registry Step 10 or higher

  • AND

  • Minimum of 2 years related experience; preferably in areas of supervision, mentoring and coaching.

Pay Range:

  • The pay range for this position is $56,600.00 to $70,800.00 annually.
  • Placement within the range is determined by factors such as relevant experience, skills, certifications, and internal equity.

Benefits:

At OCDC, employee wellbeing is a priority and an essential part of supporting our mission and communities.


OCDC offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial wellbeing, and work–life balance. Eligible employees (20+ hours/week) may receive:


  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Retirement plan with employer contribution
  • Paid time off, sick leave, holidays, and paid leave programs
  • Employer paid life and disability coverage, with voluntary options available
  • Flexible Spending Accounts for healthcare and dependent care
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and wellness resources
  • Optional benefits including pet insurance

  • Successful enrollment in Oregon’s Central Background Registry (CBR) through the OR Dept. of Early Learning and Care.
  • Ability to pass a sponsored physical examination and communicable disease assessment.
  • This position may require driving a personal vehicle, must possess current driver’s license, and auto insurance coverage.

description:
Job Title

Director, Development & Investor Project Services, Project & Development Services

Job Description Summary

The Director, Development & Investor Project Services will provide leadership to the overall project management service line for a designated market, including business development, business operations, financial management, client relations, and project operations. This role is responsible for developing and executing strategic business objectives for Project & Development Services (PDS) through leadership and advanced expertise in collaboration with the PDS Regional Leader and local market Managing Principal. This position actively works to establish and maintain Cushman & Wakefield’s presence as a thought leader and first-class service provider and will collaborate with PDS leadership and local market leadership to expand the development and investor-services platform, strengthen client relationships, and deliver consistent, high-quality outcomes across the project portfolio.
The Director will lead a team that provides development advisory and project management services to developers, asset managers, management companies, real estate investment trusts (REITs,), private equity owners, institutional investors, family offices, and other real estate owners requiring experienced capital-project leadership. Serving as an owner’s representative and trusted advisor, the Director will align project decisions with investment objectives, asset strategy, underwriting assumptions, risk tolerance, schedule requirements, and long-term value creation. The role is accountable for client strategy, team leadership, business development, financial performance, and successful execution of ground-up development, redevelopment, repositioning, and capital improvement programs.

Job Description

Essential Job Duties:

  • Lead and grow a team of project and development professionals, providing oversight, coaching, performance management, and strategic direction for the practice.
  • Lead complex ground-up development, redevelopment, repositioning, and capital improvement projects from due diligence through lease-up, occupancy, and stabilization – demonstrating competence in broad range of varied project types and operate in complex / non routine environment
  • Direct feasibility studies, due diligence, entitlement strategies, consultant coordination, development budgeting, scheduling, procurement, and delivery planning.
  • Provide fiduciary oversight of project finances, including budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, change management, cost reporting, and capital deployment strategies.
  • Establish project governance, stakeholder communication, reporting standards, and decision-making processes for ownership, lenders, investors, and project teams.
  • Lead the selection, contracting, and management of design professionals, contractors, consultants, and vendors to ensure successful project outcomes.
  • Identify, mitigate, and escalate project risks related to scope, schedule, budget, contracts, quality, safety, and stakeholder alignment.
  • Oversee multiple projects, assets, and client relationships while ensuring consistent service delivery, quality standards, and operational excellence.
  • Drive business development through client engagement, market presence, opportunity identification, proposal development, fee negotiations, and account growth.
  • Contribute to the financial performance and strategic growth of the practice through pipeline management, staffing, forecasting, project profitability, and operational leadership.
  • Represent Cushman & Wakefield as an industry leader through client presentations, market engagement, and thought leadership initiatives.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor with internal and external clients to ensure successful delivery of project management services, client goals and objectives are established and achieved; project action plans are implemented, anticipate/respond to all client needs, and generally act as a trusted advisor for comprehensive real estate work
  • Act with fiduciary responsibility to client projects, including complete financial management of project: establish and manage project budgets, maintain monthly forecasts and cash flow analysis, prepare anticipated cost reports and any other reports as required by the client
  • Management of due diligence, programming, design, entitlements, bidding, permitting, procurement, design team selection, schedule creation/management, contractor selection, vendor selection, sustainability and post construction services.
  • Identify and address areas of concern regarding potential liabilities and risk (fee, our reputation, errors and omissions, etc.) with Market Leader.
  • Provide an appropriate level of on-site supervision to ensure proper performance criteria are being met.
  • Leverage PDS technology, processes and best practices to improve project delivery, decision making, and client outcomes.
  • Active management of PDS staff, including adherence to company policy/procedures, staff development, performance management, and team motivation. Convey and ensure adoption of policies and practices to the team.

Education/Experience/Training:

  • Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, Real Estate, Finance, Business Administration or related field. Master's degree preferred. Certification preferred.
  • Twelve or more years of progressive experience in real estate development, construction, owner’s representation, project management, asset management, or related advisory services with 2 or more years of management experience required.
  • Demonstrated success delivering complex ground-up development, redevelopment, and capital improvement projects throughout the full project lifecycle.
  • Experience serving developers, institutional owners, REITs, private equity real estate firms, asset managers, lenders, and other investment-focused clients preferred.
  • Strong understanding of real estate investment strategy, underwriting, capital planning, development economics, and asset value creation.
  • Advanced knowledge of development and construction management, including budgeting, forecasting, procurement, contracting, scheduling, entitlements, permitting, risk management, and financial reporting.
  • Proven leadership, client advisory, business development, and stakeholder management capabilities, with the ability to drive strategic growth and deliver exceptional client outcomes.
  • Ability to contribute to the strategic direction of the assigned department or assigned practice area.
  • Advanced project management skills with expertise in the project management business.
  • Expert in client relations, client management and consulting.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Highly organized with strong analytical skills.
  • A proficient working knowledge of accounting and financial reporting, budgeting, scheduling and processes as they relate to corporate real estate, design and construction.
  • Software skills: Microsoft Office applications, MS Project.

This recruitment will be used to fill ten part-time (a maximum of 24 hours per week) CCE Student Technical Project Assistant - Salimifard for the School of Civil and Construction Engineering at Oregon State University (OSU).


Undergraduate Research Assistant – Sustainable, Healthy, and Resilient Buildings Lab:

The Sustainable, Healthy, and Resilient Buildings lab is looking to recruit Undergraduate Research Assistant students, starting in Fall term and continuing to Winter, Spring, and possibly Summer terms. Start date is flexible with at least one academic year to work in this position.


About Sustainable, Healthy, and Resilient Buildings Lab:

This lab is established and led by Dr. Parichehr Salimifard at Oregon State University, College of Engineering. The mission of this lab is to improve the health and well-being of the public by making the environments in which people spend the majority of their lifetime healthier, more sustainable, and also resilient. The Sustainable, Healthy, and Resilient Buildings Lab research projects have crossovers to fluid dynamics, aerosol science, energy efficiency, sustainability, and environmental health.


Indoor Air Quality:

One of the core research areas of our lab is indoor environmental quality, particularly control, and mitigation of building occupants’ exposure to contaminants and allergen and virus-carrier particles indoors. We have conducted research on aerosols dynamics and sensing; more specifically on particle transport, deposition, resuspension, aerosol sensing, and size characterization. The most recent and emergent contributions of these research projects are in airborne infectious disease and wildfire smoke exposure mitigation and control.

The research assistant will work in lab and/or field research activities to help with various tasks including but not limited to equipment setup, data collection and analysis, and lab maintenance.
