About Fulfillment IQ (FIQ):


Fulfillment IQ is a supply chain engineering and transformation company that helps brands, retailers, and 3PLs design, build, and scale high-performance logistics operations.

We work at the intersection of strategy, operations, and technology where we solve complex, real-world problems across warehouse design, automation, order management, transportation, and end-to-end supply chain execution.

Our teams combine deep domain expertise with strong technical capability, delivering outcomes through consulting, systems implementation, and proprietary platforms that accelerate time-to-value and reduce delivery risk.

If you enjoy working in complex environments, partnering closely with clients, and seeing your work make a tangible impact on how global commerce moves, this is the place where your skills and judgment truly come to life.

Role Overview:

We are seeking an experienced MAWM Configuration Lead Consultant with deep expertise in Manhattan Active Warehouse Management to lead configuration design, solution validation, and implementation activities across large-scale WMS transformation programs.

This role requires strong hands-on configuration expertise, functional understanding of warehouse operations, and the ability to lead client-facing workshops, translate business requirements into scalable MAWM solutions, and guide project teams through design, configuration, testing, deployment, and stabilization.

The ideal candidate will act as a trusted advisor to business, operations, and technical stakeholders while owning key configuration workstreams and ensuring the MAWM solution is aligned with operational goals, system standards, and implementation best practices.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead MAWM configuration workstreams across full-cycle implementation projects.
  • Own configuration design for core warehouse processes, including receiving, putaway, replenishment, inventory control, picking, packing, shipping, cross-dock, and labor-related workflows.
  • Translate business requirements into scalable Manhattan Active WMS configuration solutions.
  • Lead client workshops and design sessions to gather requirements, validate process flows, and define future-state workflows.
  • Configure Manhattan Active WMS using Configuration Director and related MAWM tools.
  • Manage and govern multi-configuration environments across project phases.
  • Collaborate with functional consultants, technical teams, integration teams, QA teams, and client stakeholders to ensure solution alignment.
  • Review and validate configuration changes to ensure quality, consistency, and adherence to project standards.
  • Support integration discussions involving APIs, JSON payloads, Postman testing, ERP integrations, and external systems.
  • Partner with technical teams on Manhattan ProActive Extension requirements, validation, and solution design.
  • Create and maintain detailed documentation, including configuration specifications, business rules, process flows, test scenarios, and design artifacts.
  • Support SIT, UAT, regression testing, defect triage, and go-live readiness activities.
  • Identify risks, configuration gaps, process inefficiencies, and opportunities for optimization.
  • Provide guidance and mentorship to junior consultants and configuration team members.
  • Support deployment, hypercare, stabilization, and post-go-live improvement activities.
  • Act as a key point of contact for configuration-related decisions, risks, escalations, and solution recommendations.

Required Skills & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or a related field; or equivalent work experience.
  • 5-8 years of experience in WMS consulting, supply chain systems implementation, or warehouse technology transformation.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Manhattan Active Warehouse Management configuration.
  • Minimum of 2 full-cycle Manhattan Active WMS implementations.
  • Proven experience leading MAWM configuration workstreams or solution design activities.
  • Strong knowledge of warehouse operations, including receiving, putaway, replenishment, cycle counting, inventory control, picking, packing, shipping, and cross-docking.
  • Experience working with Configuration Director and managing multi-configuration environments.
  • Familiarity with Manhattan ProActive Extension development concepts and related solution validation.
  • Working knowledge of APIs, JSON, Postman, and integration testing.
  • Experience supporting system integrations between WMS, ERP, TMS, automation, parcel, labor, and other supply chain systems.
  • Strong experience with SIT, UAT, defect resolution, go-live readiness, and post-go-live support.
  • Ability to lead requirements workshops, design discussions, and stakeholder alignment sessions.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, documentation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to engage business users, technical teams, project leaders, and executive stakeholders.
  • Experience working in Agile or hybrid project delivery environments.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with cloud platforms such as Google Cloud Platform, AWS, or Azure.
  • Experience with Manhattan SCI reporting and analytics tools.
  • Knowledge of distribution center transportation, parcel, automation, robotics, or labor management processes.
  • Experience working with retail, consumer goods, eCommerce, 3PL, or omnichannel fulfillment environments.
  • Prior experience mentoring consultants or leading small project teams.
  • Experience contributing to solution governance, configuration standards, and implementation best practices.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days:

30 Days In

  • Build a strong understanding of the client environment, current MAWM setup, project scope, and implementation objectives.
  • Review existing configurations, process flows, integrations, open issues, and design documentation.
  • Establish relationships with client stakeholders, operations teams, technical teams, and internal project members.
  • Begin contributing to requirements discussions, configuration reviews, and design validation sessions.
  • Identify key risks, gaps, and areas requiring deeper analysis.

60 Days In

  • Take ownership of assigned MAWM configuration workstreams.
  • Lead configuration discussions and support design decisions across key warehouse processes.
  • Drive configuration updates, documentation, and validation activities.
  • Support integration planning, testing readiness, and defect triage.
  • Provide clear recommendations to improve solution quality, usability, and operational alignment.
  • Demonstrate strong progress against project milestones and configuration deliverables.

90 Days In

  • Independently lead configuration deliverables for assigned functional areas.
  • Support or lead go-live readiness, deployment planning, and hypercare preparation.
  • Provide strategic input on MAWM design, configuration governance, and future enhancements.
  • Help deliver measurable improvements in solution quality, system stability, and warehouse process efficiency.
  • Be recognized as a trusted MAWM configuration lead by stakeholders and project teams.

Key Performance Indicators:’

  • Configuration Delivery: Timely and accurate completion of assigned configuration deliverables.
  • Solution Quality: Low defect leakage and strong alignment between configuration and business requirements.
  • Testing Success: High SIT/UAT pass rates and timely defect resolution.
  • Go-Live Readiness: Smooth deployment with minimal rework or stabilization issues.
  • Stakeholder Satisfaction: Positive feedback from client business users, operations teams, and technical stakeholders.
  • Process Improvement: Measurable improvement in warehouse productivity, accuracy, cycle time, or operational efficiency.
  • Team Leadership: Effective guidance, collaboration, and knowledge sharing across project teams.

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

At Fulfillment IQ, we don’t just build supply chain solutions; we build long-term careers.
We believe in giving our people real ownership, real influence, and meaningful responsibility. Whether you’re leading a client relationship, shaping a solution, or building internal capability, your decisions have a visible impact.


We operate with a high-trust, high-standards culture that values clear thinking, collaboration, and accountability without unnecessary hierarchy or bureaucracy.


Here’s what makes Fulfillment IQ a rewarding place to work:

Work That Matters
You’ll help solve real operational challenges that directly impact global commerce, customer experience, and supply chain performance.

Career Growth That Matters
We invest in mentorship, leadership development, and continuous learning — supporting both vertical growth and long-term career progression.

Flexibility to Thrive
We support remote and hybrid work models, flexible schedules, and trust our teams to manage their time responsibly.

We Celebrate Impact

From project wins to personal milestones, we recognize contribution, celebrate progress, and value consistency over heroics.

A Collaborative Culture
You’ll work alongside experienced consultants, engineers, product leaders, and commercial professionals who value ownership, transparency, and high standards.

Perks you’ll appreciate:

  • Employee Health: Comprehensive health and dental coverage for you and your family
  • Time Off: Competitive paid time off and flexible leave policies
  • Retirement: Retirement savings programs and employer contributions
  • Professional Growth: Dedicated learning and development budget
  • Flexible Work: Remote and hybrid work options
  • Perks: Equipment allowances, internet reimbursements, business travel coverage, and employee stock options (ESOP), where applicable.
  • Community Engagement: Team events, meetups, and company offsites

Additional Perks

  • Equipment and workstation allowances

title: 1771 - Liaison Officer - MARSOC
description:
Sigma Defense is seeking a Liaison Officer - United States Marine Corps Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC) to join our team in Camp Lejeune MCB, NC. This position is in the Secretariat for Special Operations (SSO), Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict (OASW(SO/LIC)). The ASW(SO/LIC) serves as the principal civilian advisor and assistant to the Secretary of War and has statutory responsibility for overseeing special operations-peculiar administrative matters pertaining to the readiness and organization of special operations forces (SOF), resources and equipment, and civilian personnel.

Liaison Officer (LNO) will work within the SSO’s Capability Development and Innovation (CD&I) Global Strategic Partnerships Team. LNOs serves as the embedded forward-deployed subject matter expert and force multiplier for SSO. The LNO will advise and assist the Theater Special Operations Command (TSOC) staff on the integration of emerging technologies and will support interoperability and rapid fielding of capabilities to SOF, as required by the Command.

The LNO combines operational knowledge, personal/professional networking, and technical insight to manage and advance capability development opportunities. The LNO must maintain currency and continually adapt and keep their technical expertise current with respect to the evolving operational environment, key operating problems, and associated technological capability gaps. They are responsible for ensuring deployed technologies are supportable and capable of continuing mission operations. The LNO must be a self-starter, be a motivated force multiplier bringing together end users.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled: Sigma Defense Systems is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

Requirements

  • 10+ years of prior service in Special Operations (E7+ or O3+ equivalent preferred).
  • Experience within MARSOC.
  • Strong technical understanding of SOF formations, systems, networks, and acquisition principles.
  • Strong foundation in military/combatant command operations, chain of command relationships, and international partner cooperation.
  • Must be capable of traveling up to 25% of the time throughout the assigned COCOM AOR, forward operating hubs, Washington, D.C., and domestic R&D facilities to witness technical demonstrations, embed with operational units, and evaluate prototypes in austere environments.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen.

Candidate Differentiators:

  • Advanced Degree and/or Professional Military Education (e.g. JPME I, II).
  • Experience navigating the Department of War Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) cycle and joint interoperability frameworks (e.g., CJADC2).
  • Experience handling and managing Special Access Programs / Special Access Required (SAP/SAR) level technical data.
  • Experience with defense innovation ecosystems.
  • Experience identifying, tracking, and evaluating emerging commercial and defense technologies, including uncrewed systems, artificial intelligence, edge computing, resilient communications, and electronic warfare.

Personnel Clearance Level:

  • Candidate must possess an active TS clearance - and have the ability to obtain SCI security clearance or higher.
  • A clearance will not be sponsored.

Education Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in an Communications, Political Science, Business Administration, Criminal Justice, or International Relations field of study.

Essential Job Duties (not all-inclusive):

  • Serves as the primary local interface to Special Operations Command and performs liaison functions between the Command and CD&I.
  • Accomplishes task requirements with designated government project leads, ensures demonstration and evaluation schedules are met, and manages the relationship between the customer and contract personnel.
  • Supports ongoing capability development activities to meet emergent operational needs within the Combatant Commander Area of Responsibility.
  • Develops and refines technical and operational requirements for SOF-peculiar capability gaps.
  • Leverages an understanding of SOF operational mission profiles to help identify technology requirements, shortfalls, and potential mitigation strategies.
  • Demonstrates project management leadership to avoid/mitigate risks in meeting contract-specific performance requirements for planning, execution, and scheduling of technology assessments and demonstrations, as required.
  • Demonstrated operational understanding of SOF mission profiles, capability development cycles, and rapid acquisition pathways.
  • Coordinates, plans, and executes technology assessments, operational evaluations, and leadership theater visits, while delivering regular situational reports and technical briefs across classified and unclassified channels.

Salary Range: $140,000 - $170,000 annually.

Benefits

  • Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Medical Insurance to Include HSA, FSA, and DFSA Plans
  • Life and AD&D coverage
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • 401(k) Plan with Company Matching Contributions
  • 160 Hours of Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • 12 (Floating) Holidays
  • Educational Assistance
  • Highly Competitive Salary

title: Principal Architect - Solutions Architect
description:
When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

What you’ll be doing...


At Verizon, we do much more than sell technology. We deliver game-changing solutions that enhance the agility, productivity, and global reach of our customers. As an Enterprise Architect, you will build deep, consultative technical relationships with your customers, effectively becoming a trusted advisor. You will play a key role in driving customer outcomes that leverage the power of Verizon 5G and edge computing. This is a high-impact role working closely with your sales partners, sales engineers, and customers to identify and qualify neutral host and private network opportunities and design solutions that solve our customers’ most pressing business challenges.


Are you ready to enhance a best-in-class 5G enterprise architecture team that thrives on teamwork and collaboration? Can you see yourself delivering innovative technology and solutions that connect people worldwide and transform how communities live, work, and play? Are you ready to unleash the transformative possibilities of 5G? Welcome to Verizon – a company you can be proud to represent and be a part of.



What we’re looking for...


  • Design modern 5G connectivity solutions, including complex private core and edge compute as features and capabilities that help customers meet their expressed business outcomes.
  • Develop scalable and repeatable network architectures to deliver high-performing, highly reliable, and highly secure wireless services to our customers.
  • Stay informed of regulatory and compliance requirements changes and adapt our reference architectures accordingly.
  • Act as a trusted, unbiased advisor to customers, providing strategic insights to help achieve their business goals through our technology.
  • Emphasize the value of licensed spectrum and scalability of neutral host networks to private networks, edge compute, and beyond.
  • Review, validate, and approve network designs and provide feedback. Revise designs where applicable
  • Build and present design packages to customers in partnership with other Verizon stakeholders.
  • Explore and explain how future solution enablement is possible through Verizon’s agile and modern network architecture.
  • Help customers extract maximum value out of the network by advising and supporting multi-carrier, device, and application onboarding.
  • Partner with sales and specialists during offer discussions to ensure the value of Verizon’s network methodology is clear to customers.
  • Work closely with network and service delivery teams to ensure the cohesive execution of a build.
  • Be the voice of the customer and the market.

You’ll need to have:


  • Bachelor’s degree and five or more years of relevant work experience.
  • Five or more years of experience in the tech industry with experience in pre-sales, customer-facing consulting, or other relevant technical expertise.
  • Experience in architecting and developing large cellular network solutions for small, medium, and large enterprises and/or government agencies.
  • Experience with designing 4G/5G/CBRS wireless technologies, software-defined networks, and cloud and edge computing architectures.
  • Experience with designing distributed antenna systems (DAS) and small-cell-based In-Building systems.
  • Experience and knowledge about Wi-Fi and a strong familiarity with the concept of private networking, neutral host networking, and hybrid (public/private) network architectures.
  • Strong technical acumen in 5G network architecture and end-to-end solution discussions including supported devices and applications.
  • Deep knowledge of IT/OT processes and development of enterprise technical strategy.
  • Experience in architecting and developing software or infrastructure for scalable, distributed systems.
  • Experience in managing multiple projects or deals under tight timelines.
  • Willingness to travel throughout the US and abroad.
  • Valid driver's license and passport.

Even better if you have one or more of the following:


  • Master’s degree in engineering or advanced network certifications and experience.
  • IBWave Level 2 or above certification
  • Deep understanding of 3GPP Specifications for 5G, specifically Rel-16+
  • Direct experience working with wireless network integrators and RAN OEMs like Nokia, Ericsson, Samsung, and Celona.
  • Ability to quickly learn, understand, and work with new emerging technologies, methodologies, and solutions for digital transformation.
  • Experience with onboarding domestic and international mobile network operators onto neutral host networks.

If Verizon and this role sound like a fit for you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every “even better” qualification listed above.

Where you’ll be working

In this mobile role, you'll primarily work from customer or field location(s), with occasional visits to a Verizon location for in-person training and meetings.

Scheduled Weekly Hours

40

Equal Employment Opportunity

Verizon is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to veteran status, disability or other legally protected characteristics.

Benefits and Compensation

Our benefits are designed to help you move forward in your career, and in areas of your life outside of Verizon. From health and wellness benefit options including: medical, dental, vision, short and long term disability, basic life insurance, supplemental life insurance, AD&D insurance, identity theft protection, pet insurance and group home & auto insurance. We also offer a matched 401(k) savings plan, up to 8 company paid holidays per year and up to 6 personal days per year, paid parental leave, adoption assistance and tuition assistance, plus other incentives, we’ve got you covered with our award-winning total rewards package. title: Pest Control Technician
description:
Benefits Start Day 1 for Full-Time Colleagues - No Waiting Period!

For more information about our benefits, see below!

We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to many of the world's leading brands and serve consumer and business customers across multiple industries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet."

What do our Pest Control Technicians do?

The primary purpose of this role is to perform our industry leading pest management services for residential customers. You will be responsible for identifying and eliminating pests from residential properties by conducting thorough inspections, determining the type of pest infestation, applying appropriate treatments like pesticides and traps, and providing preventative measures to prevent future infestations, all while adhering to safety regulations and communicating with clients about pest control solutions.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

  • Conduct thorough inspections of client properties to identify signs of pest infestations, damage, and entry points

  • Apply approved pest control products, including chemicals, baits, and traps, to effectively eliminate pests while adhering to safety standards

  • Educate customers on pest prevention methods and the importance of maintaining a pest-free environment. Provide advice on how to reduce the risk of future infestations.

  • Build relationships with customers, schedule and confirm their appointments, help with sales to current customers, and expand our product to new customers

  • Ensure that all pest control equipment is properly maintained, stocked, and in good working condition

  • Adhere to all local, state, and federal regulations regarding pest control products and safety protocols

  • Drive and safely operate a company provided service vehicle (we provide routine maintenance)

Essential Job Functions:

  • Working in tight, confined spaces such as basements, attics, crawl spaces, narrow aisles, or passageways

  • Working around animals, insects and termites

  • You’ll sometimes be working around mechanical parts, vehicles, electrical current, heights and scaffolding, fumes, dust, and chemicals, and we’ll train you how to handle all of these conditions safely

  • Able to work both inside and outside in your local climate in company-provided weather gear

  • Lots of moving around — regularly sitting, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling, up and down stairs, ladders, scaffolding, ramps, and poles

  • You’ll need to wear personal protective equipment (PPE), like an OSHA-compliant respirator

What do you need?

  • Clean shaven face- for safety reasons (rebreathers have to be able to seal your face)

  • High school diploma or GED; related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience

  • Possess a valid driver’s license from state of residence.

  • Licenses/certificates as required by federal, state, and/or local regulations (covered by us)

  • Available to work Monday-Friday and weekends as needed

  • Open to learning and becoming knowledgeable in all areas of pest control

  • Solid reading, writing, and verbal communication skills

  • Basic math skills — You’ll need to be able to follow instructions for mixing on product labels

  • Customer-facing experience preferred

#ZipRTX

title: Vans: Supervisor - Westminster
description:
Vans is the original brand rooted in the authentic lifestyle of skateboarding. We are driven by our mission to inspire and empower everyone to live “Off The Wall” – embracing the youthful spirit of freedom, non-conformity, and relentless progression. Yesterday’s “Off The Wall” moment is today’s new normal, and at Vans, we believe in constantly outdoing ourselves. Together with our communities across the globe, our vision is to push culture forward because we believe that the pursuit of progression never ends. We are constantly inspired by the future generation of positive catalysts within our community.

So, before we get to the job details, take a minute to learn a little more about us – our values and our culture. If you can see yourself working side-by-side with a team of people who think and live “Off the Wall,” Vans just may be the place for you.

To learn more about our values and our culture, visit Vans Careers or .

Supervisor

What will you do?

A day in the life of a Supervisor at Vans looks a little like this.

As a Supervisor, you play a key role in supporting the store’s leadership team and driving abets-in-class customer experience. You will lead by example, coach and develop associates, and ensure operational excellence across customer engagement, merchandising, and store standards. In partnership with the Store Manager and Assistant Store Manager, you will help maximize store profitability, foster an inclusive team culture, and contribute to the store’s success. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced retail environment, enjoys mentoring others, and is passionate about delivering exceptional service. Let’s break down that day-in-the-life a bit more.

  • Deliver a high level of personalized customer engagement through genuine interactions.​
  • Support the store team in achieving and exceeding sales goals by monitoring progress against key performance indicators, while also achieving individual goals.​
  • Model selling behaviors and foster a consumer-centric mindset through authentic customer interactions.​
  • Coach and develop associates to deliver high levels of customer engagement and meet productivity goals.​
  • Supervise daily store operations, including opening and closing procedures, floor coverage, and task delegation.​
  • Support stockroom operations by organizing inventory, processing shipments, and ensuring timely product flow to the sales floor.​
  • Assist in training and onboarding new team members; provide ongoing feedback and support.​
  • Maintain visual merchandising standards and ensure product replenishment aligns with brand directives.​
  • Support inventory integrity through proper shipping, receiving, and loss prevention practices.​
  • Promote community engagement by participating in local initiatives and events.​
  • Uphold company policies, safety standards, and operational procedures.​
  • Foster a positive and inclusive store environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and learning.

What do you need to succeed?

We all bring unique skills to work each day. For this role, there are foundational skills needed to succeed, along with 1+ years of retail or store leadership experience in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment​. A High School Diploma or equivalent is preferred; but we value hands-on experience and demonstrated achievements most.

The foundation skills you will need in this position are:

· Proven ability to drive results through store teams and exceed sales and profit goals.​

· Skilled in coaching, motivating, and building high-performing, diverse teams.​

· Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to influence across all levels.​

· Solution-oriented and flexible in a fast-paced, dynamic retail environment.​

· Capable of working independently, managing shifting priorities, and meeting business expectations.​

· Comfortable using word processing, spreadsheets, and retail software tools.​

· Ability to stand and move throughout the store for extended periods and perform physical tasks such as bending, reaching, squatting, climbing ladders, and lifting light to moderate weight, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Are you in?

title: Facilities Executive
description:
Job Title

Facilities Executive

Job Description Summary

This role is responsible for the day-to-day management, maintenance, and operational readiness of school facilities, ensuring a safe, secure, and conducive environment for learning and teaching.

Job Description

About the Role

  • Ensure the day-to-day operations of the facility(s) or campus, including janitorial, life-safety, engineering, site services, and general maintenance are implemented and carried out in a manner consistent with C&W policies and client directives. Ensure all contracts are reviewed on a regular basis and are bid out as required and confirm invoices match contract pricing
  • Supervise all maintenance programs relating to the interior and exterior conditions and appearance of the properties
  • Under the direction of the Facility Manager, respond promptly to requests for building maintenance, repairs, cleaning needs, etc. from building occupants and for the implementation of ongoing contract programs to address and resolve needs and problems
  • Compile information necessary to ensure all site-specific documentation and reports are completed accurately and on time, including (and as applicable): Property Information Book, Site Operating Manual, Emergency Procedures Manual, IIPP Manual, Local Code Compliance Log, ADA Compliance Log, OSHA Log, Safety Meeting Log, Elevator Logs, Janitorial Log, Purchase Order Log, Vendor Certificates of Insurance, As-built Drawings, IIPP Manual, Paid Invoices File, General Files, Contract Files, Annual Property Conditions and Year-end Performance Report and other reports and documentation as required
  • Prepares budgets, financial reports (monthly and quarterly), contracts, expenditures and purchase orders related to the facility(s) or complex as directed
  • Assist in providing information and reports necessary for the development of capital budgets for the facility. This includes contributions towards a five-year plan of maintenance, facility improvement, and cost reduction initiatives
  • Collect, analyze and prepare reports of such statistical data as may be required to provide accurate and current assessment of facility management objectives
  • Expected to be thoroughly familiar with the management contract, vendor agreements, and other building/facility contracts and all requirements contained therein
  • Monitor and ensure that tenants and vendors comply with insurance requirements and coordinate all claims as required
  • Proactively inspect the facility, systems, rooms, common areas, etc. and report back any findings or issues to the Facility Manager

About You

  • Diploma preferably in Building, Technical, Facilities Management, Mechanical & Electrical Engineering, Building Services or a relevant discipline, preferably with M&E background.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in facilities management, building operations, maintenance, technical services or equivalent.
  • Where the relevant Diploma is not held, at least 8 continuous years of relevant working experience as a Facilities Management Executive or equivalent.
  • Preferably with Tier 4 Certified Facilities Management Expert accreditation by SIFMA.

Job Description

Tarleton State University, a distinguished Doctoral National Comprehensive University, invites applications for the position of Professional Counselor in the Department of Student Counseling Services. As part of a vibrant academic community dedicated to excellence in teaching, research, and service, this role offers the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to a university that values innovation, collaboration, and inclusive growth. Join us in advancing knowledge and transforming lives—on campus and beyond. Tarleton State University continues to grow its impact across Texas, with four distinct campuses located in Stephenville, Fort Worth, RELLIS-Bryan and Waco, along with a robust online community that extends our reach even further.

At the heart of it all is Stephenville, where Tarleton State offers a dynamic environment for faculty and staff. From a lively live music scene and numerous local festivals to rich traditions rooted in the surrounding community, Stephenville provides a vibrant and welcoming atmosphere.

No matter where you're located—on campus or online—you are part of a mission that transforms lives and makes a difference across the state of Texas and beyond.

________________________________________________________________________

Important Immigration Information:

A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. Please be advised that Tarleton State University will NOT pay this fee. Therefore, if you need immigration sponsorship for your employment, we recommend that you consult with your private immigration counsel at your own expense to ascertain whether your current immigration status would make a potential offer of employment from Tarleton State University subject to this fee.

In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate.

________________________________________________________________________

Under the leadership of the Director of Student Counseling Services (SCS), the Professional Counselor provides specialized clinical mental health services to students through individual and group counseling, crisis intervention, risk assessment, consultation, outreach, case management, and care coordination. The position serves as a resource to the university community by supporting student well-being, responding to mental health concerns and crises, consulting with faculty, staff, students, and community partners, and collaborating with campus and community stakeholders to promote student success. Responsibilities also include maintaining timely and accurate clinical documentation in accordance with state licensure requirements and university policies, participating in clinical consultation and staffing activities, and contributing to outreach and educational programming related to mental health and wellness.


The Professional Counselor position is designed to allow for flexible scheduling and service delivery as needed to support the priorities of leadership and the evolving needs of the campus community. Serves as Campus Security Authority (CSA).


The position is on-site at Tarleton State's Stephenville campus. Occasional travel to the Fort Worth campus and offsite events allows for continued support and engagement across multiple university communities.


Required Education, Experience, Skills

To be qualified as a Professional Counselor I:

  • Master’s or doctoral degree in counseling, psychology, social work, or a related field.
  • Must hold a provisional clinical license (e.g., LPC-Associate, LMFT-Associate, LMSW).
  • Employees holding a provisional license must obtain full licensure within the timeframe required by the Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council (BHEC) and remain in compliance with SCS standards to maintain eligibility for continued employment.

Proposed Salary Range for Professional Counselor I: $49,000 to $68,330.50


To be qualified as a Professional Counselor II:

  • Master’s or doctoral degree in counseling, psychology, social work, or a related field.
  • Minimum of two years of related professional experience.
  • Must hold a current, unrestricted Texas license as a Licensed Psychologist (LP), Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT), or Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), and maintain the license in good standing with BHEC as a condition of continued employment.

Proposed Salary Range for Professional Counselor II: $53,745 to $76,321


Position level (I or II) will be determined by the candidate's qualifications and professional experience.


Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:


  • Knowledge of standard office software (Word, PowerPoint, Excel etc).
  • Excellent written communication, analytical, interpersonal, and organizational skills
  • Adherence to the ethical principles and code of conduct for the relevant Texas State Licensing Board and all relevant laws for the State of Texas
  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others
  • Ability to present information clearly and concisely
  • Knowledge of and adherence to professional and ethical guidelines.
  • Ability to work with sensitive information and maintain confidentiality.

All clinical staff must maintain appropriate Texas licensure in good standing and comply with all applicable laws, regulations, ethical standards, and professional conduct requirements established by BHEC, the State of Texas, and Tarleton State University as a condition of continued employment. Employees must also successfully complete all required background screenings in accordance with university policies and procedures.


Compensation & Benefits

title: Quality Control Laboratory Leader
description:
Interested in a career that matters?




This position leads a Quality Control Laboratory team in Valinhos, São Paulo, ensuring the efficient execution of laboratory activities, proper operational planning, and timely delivery of high-quality results. The role works closely with Production, Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, Planning, and other business partners to maintain operational excellence while meeting regulatory, safety, data integrity, and quality requirements.


The Role & Your Impact

As Group Leader, you will combine technical expertise with inspiring people leadership. You will create an environment built on trust, collaboration, accountability, and commitment to deadlines and quality.

Your leadership will be essential to ensuring that the team understands and lives the company culture in its daily work, remains engaged in continuous improvement initiatives, and has opportunities to develop and grow. By enabling the team to deliver consistent and sustainable results, you will contribute directly to the reliability and agility of the Quality Control Laboratory.


Your Key Responsibilities in this role:

  • Lead the operational performance of the assigned laboratory team, ensuring that laboratory tests are conducted properly, efficiently, and in accordance with official company protocols and production schedules;
  • Plan and coordinate the laboratory’s operational routine, ensuring timely and reliable delivery of results;
  • Monitor operational and team performance indicators, taking proactive action to mitigate risks and remove obstacles;
  • Identify development opportunities within the team and support the consistent application of company values and expectations;
  • Coordinate and actively participate in the local implementation of new methodologies developed by global teams, as well as in the optimization of methods applicable to the area;
  • Ensure compliance with applicable regulations, procedures, and company quality standards;
  • Ensure that the local team is appropriately trained to operate the laboratory effectively;
  • Interpret laboratory results and prepare detailed technical reports when required;
  • Lead continuous improvement, process simplification, and productivity initiatives;
  • Participate in internal and external audits, providing technical support related to the laboratory area;
  • Collaborate regularly with colleagues from different regions, sharing learnings and ensuring alignment across teams;
  • Promote effective collaboration with local stakeholders in Production, Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, Planning, and other business functions;
  • Ensure that operational speed never compromises quality, data integrity, employee safety, or regulatory compliance;
  • Travel nationally and internationally when required.

What you'll need to be successful in this role:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Pharmacy, Biotechnology, or a related field;
  • Advanced English communication and reading proficiency;
  • Active or in-progress CRQ registration;
  • Experience in laboratory analyses, including physicochemical and/or microbiological testing, preferably in Quality Control laboratories;
  • Experience managing teams;
  • Strong communication skills to ensure effective alignment and relationships with stakeholders across the organization, both locally and globally;
  • Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills;
  • Strong organization, proactivity, and commitment to deadlines and quality;
  • High attention to detail, strong time-management skills, and the ability to solve diverse technical and operational problems;
  • Ability to make decisions, set priorities, and act with a sense of urgency;
  • Availability for occasional national and international travel, including work on weekends when required;
  • Availability to work on-site in Valinhos, PR, from Monday to Friday, 07h30 to 16h30, with occasional weekend activities.

Additional Skills & Interests We Value:

  • A proven track record of developing talent and building engaged teams;
  • Excellent ability to communicate and influence at different levels of the organization;
  • Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills;
  • A resilient, collaborative, and solution-oriented mindset;
  • A continuous improvement and simplification mindset;
  • The ability to balance operational excellence, people development, and focus on internal customers and business needs.

Our purpose guides the way

And it’s how we'll impact the future. Now, more than ever, the world needs change. And with biosolutions, the possibilities for transformation are endless. description:

At LPL financial, our work makes a difference. That is why we share a passion for doing it ethically and exceedingly well. Because we have a clear focus and we are empowered to deliver results, we see every day that we are creating something special together.


Your Life

title: MAWM Solution Design Lead
description:
General Information:

Job Title: MAWM Solution Design Lead

Job Location: San Antonio, TX / Atlanta, GA, United States (Onsite/Hybrid) OR fully remote across the United States for exceptional candidates.

Job Type: Full-time, Permanent

Hiring Timeline: Immediate

Reporting Line: Co-Founder, COO & SVP Enterprise Systems

Travel Expectations: Up to 25-35% travel, based on customer requirements.

Existing Vacancy: Yes

Application Deadline: Open until Filled

Salary Range: 125K – 150K USD per year (negotiable)

About Fulfillment IQ (FIQ):


Fulfillment IQ is a supply chain engineering and transformation company that helps brands, retailers, and 3PLs design, build, and scale high-performance logistics operations.

We work at the intersection of strategy, operations, and technology where we solve complex, real-world problems across warehouse design, automation, order management, transportation, and end-to-end supply chain execution.

Our teams combine deep domain expertise with strong technical capability, delivering outcomes through consulting, systems implementation, and proprietary platforms that accelerate time-to-value and reduce delivery risk.

If you enjoy working in complex environments, partnering closely with clients, and seeing your work make a tangible impact on how global commerce moves, this is the place where your skills and judgment truly come to life.

Role Overview:

Many of our enterprise clients have already made the move to Manhattan Active WM. They have a template, a few sites live, and an internal IT team that knows the system. What they need next is a senior design leader who has been through multi-site rollouts before, who can see the operational roadblocks coming before they hit, and who can make the client's own team stronger along the way.

As a Manhattan WMS Solution Design Lead, you are that person. You own solution design for Manhattan Active WM programs, drive operational conversations with warehouse and business leaders, and translate what you hear into sound, scalable designs. You bring options with clear tradeoffs rather than a single prescribed fix, and you coach the client's IT team so the capability stays with them after you leave.

Mandate:

  • Own the end-to-end solution design for Manhattan Active WM rollouts across multiple distribution centers, including template-based deployments to new sites
  • Act as the operational voice on client teams that are often IT-led: lead conversations with DC leadership, operations managers, and business stakeholders
  • Anticipate and resolve the business process gaps, site-to-site inconsistencies, and change-management roadblocks that surface when facilities move onto a new WMS
  • Translate requirements into multiple solution options with clear pros, cons, and effort, supported by demos or proofs of concept where useful
  • Train, mentor, and upskill client IT and project teams on Manhattan Active WM design and configuration practices

Must Have:

  • 5-10 years of recent, hands-on experience on Manhattan WMS products, including Manhattan Active WM and prior experience on an earlier Manhattan platform (WMOS or SCALE)
  • Solution design or design lead experience on Manhattan WMS programs. This is a design role; a background focused only on testing or support will not be a fit
  • Experience across multiple DCs or sites, ideally supporting a phased, multi-site rollout rather than a single-site implementation
  • Strong operational understanding of warehouse processes: receiving, put-away, replenishment, waving and allocation, picking, packing, and shipping
  • Proven ability to lead business process workshops, stakeholder interviews, and requirement-gathering sessions with operations and IT audiences
  • Track record of anticipating and resolving business process transformation challenges, not just configuring a system
  • Ability to create functional specifications, solution design documents, and fit-gap analyses
  • Ability to provide effort estimates and implementation recommendations, and to present options and tradeoffs to operational and executive stakeholders
  • Experience coaching or training client team members on Manhattan design and configuration
  • Excellent client-facing communication and presentation skills
  • Based in the United States and able to travel 25–35%

Nice to Have:

  • Prior experience at Manhattan Associates or a leading Manhattan implementation partner
  • CPG, Grocery, or other high-volume Retail DC experience.
  • Warehouse automation integration exposure (WES/WCS, AS/RS, Exotec, sortation, goods-to-person)
  • Experience with Manhattan Active platform extensibility, integrations, EDI, or ERP interfaces
  • Familiarity with other Manhattan Active modules (e.g., Labor Management, Transportation Management)


Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead solution design for new site rollouts, scale-ups, and enhancements on Manhattan Active WM programs
  • Assess each facility's current-state processes against the client's system template and identify gaps, risks, and required changes
  • Facilitate business process workshops and requirement-gathering sessions with DC operations and business teams
  • Translate client requirements into multiple solution options with pros, cons, and effort estimates
  • Build and present demos or proofs of concept to support client decision-making
  • Create and maintain functional specifications and solution design documentation
  • Act as a primary techno-functional point of contact for operations and IT stakeholders on assigned initiatives
  • Train and mentor client IT team members, building their long-term self-sufficiency on the platform
  • Partner with configuration specialists, technical teams, and testers to ensure designs are delivered as intended
  • Present proposed solutions and recommendations to operational and executive stakeholders

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days:

30 Days:

  • Ramp up on the client's Manhattan Active WM template, live sites, rollout roadmap, and key stakeholders
  • Build working relationships with the client's IT team and DC operations leaders

60 Days:

  • Lead design for your first site rollout or enhancement workstream
  • Deliver the first options-based solution proposal, with clear tradeoffs, to the client
  • Begin structured knowledge transfer with the client's IT team

90 Days:

  • Fully own solution design for assigned sites and initiatives
  • Be recognized by the client as a trusted operational and design advisor
  • Demonstrate a repeatable approach for surfacing process risks early in each rollout

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

  • Site rollout and design milestone adherence
  • Number of options-based solution proposals delivered (vs. single-fix recommendations)
  • Client satisfaction with design quality, workshops, and presentations
  • Process risks identified and resolved before go-live
  • Growth in client team self-sufficiency on Manhattan Active WM
  • Quality and completeness of functional specifications and design documentation

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

At Fulfillment IQ, we don’t just build supply chain solutions; we build long-term careers.
We believe in giving our people real ownership, real influence, and meaningful responsibility. Whether you’re leading a client relationship, shaping a solution, or building internal capability, your decisions have a visible impact.


We operate with a high-trust, high-standards culture that values clear thinking, collaboration, and accountability without unnecessary hierarchy or bureaucracy.


Here’s what makes Fulfillment IQ a rewarding place to work:

Work That Matters
You’ll help solve real operational challenges that directly impact global commerce, customer experience, and supply chain performance.

Career Growth That Matters
We invest in mentorship, leadership development, and continuous learning — supporting both vertical growth and long-term career progression.

Flexibility to Thrive
We support remote and hybrid work models, flexible schedules, and trust our teams to manage their time responsibly.

We Celebrate Impact

From project wins to personal milestones, we recognize contribution, celebrate progress, and value consistency over heroics.

A Collaborative Culture
You’ll work alongside experienced consultants, engineers, product leaders, and commercial professionals who value ownership, transparency, and high standards.

Perks you’ll appreciate:

  • Employee Health: Comprehensive health and dental coverage for you and your family
  • Time Off: Competitive paid time off and flexible leave policies
  • Retirement: Retirement savings programs and employer contributions
  • Professional Growth: Dedicated learning and development budget
  • Flexible Work: Remote and hybrid work options
  • Perks: Equipment allowances, internet reimbursements, business travel coverage, and employee stock options (ESOP), where applicable.
  • Community Engagement: Team events, meetups, and company offsites

Additional Perks

title: *Lab Assistant - Clinical Lab
description:
Overview

Department: Clinical Lab

Schedule: Per Diem Days (as needed)

Facility: Prime Healthcare St Francis Hospital

Location: Evanston, IL

Responsibilities

The Laboratory Assistant will follow the guidelines set by CLIA. Unlicensed laboratory personnel (“aides”) may not, read, result, verify or interpret any laboratory test. Unlicensed laboratory personnel may not perform any test involving the quantitative measurement of specimen or reagent, or perform any mathematical calculation in determining a test result or validity of a test procedure. Unlicensed laboratory personnel may not perform instrument calibration or review quality control results to monitor the performance of the instrument or test procedure. Unlicensed personnel require direct and constant supervision by a CLS or other licensed person during the entire time they are assisting in the analytical testing phase.

The Laboratory Assistant: 1) performs computer entry, filing, telephone communication and other clerical duties, 2) demonstrates good telephone etiquette and be able to greet patients and other visitors in a polite and friendly manner, 3) possesses good communication skills, 4) demonstrates adequate knowledge of the terminology of tests ordered in the laboratory, 5) demonstrates a good working knowledge of phlebotomy and the equipment used in collecting specimens from newborns to geriatric patients, 6) processes pathology, microbiology, immunology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, chemistry, and blood bank specimens (pre-analytic phase only) 7) processes specimens for reference laboratory, 8) stocks and orders routine supplies, 9) keeps storage areas, trays, centrifuges, and collection areas clean, 10) processes or places specimens on laboratory instruments in accordance with established policy and procedures, 11) with proper documented training the laboratory assistant may perform, instrument preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, assist in quality control procedures, perform, primary culture inoculations, stain slide preparations, and subculture from liquid media, 11) other tasks or responsibilities may be assigned by the department manager/director, i.e. monitor, mail, fax, answer phone, inter departmental deliveries. Etc. 12) Assist in Pathology with training and eval, 13) Runner 14) assist in transcribing of post-analytic results.

title: Staff Engineer, System Validation
description:
Staff Engineer, System Validation
Location: San Jose (on-site)
Ayar Labs is shattering AI data bottlenecks by moving data at the speed of light. As pioneers of co-packaged optics (CPO), we are using light instead of electricity to move data faster, further, and with a fraction of the energy needed to fuel the explosive growth of AI models.
Backed by industry giants like NVIDIA, AMD and Intel and manufactured in partnership with the world’s leading semiconductor ecosystem, Ayar Labs’ co-packaged optics solution is key to unleashing next-generation AI scale-up architectures.
We are seeking an experienced Validation Engineer to spearhead the validation efforts that ensure our groundbreaking products meet and exceed both component and system-level requirements.

This pivotal role will drive the transition of our technology from initial release to customer deployment, guaranteeing a seamless and high-performance experience for our clients. If you are a seasoned validation expert with a passion for solving complex technical challenges and an interest in laser, photonics, CMOS, and system-level concepts, this is your chance to make a significant impact on the future of interconnect technology.



Essential Functions:
  • Lead Validation Strategy: Define and implement comprehensive validation methodologies that guarantee our products meet both component and system-level product requirements. This includes developing test plans, defining success criteria, and selecting appropriate test equipment and methodologies.
  • Lead New Product Introduction (NPI): Collaborate with Design, Package, and Reliability Engineering to ensure a smooth and successful transition of products from development to mass production.
  • Drive Product Bring-up: Collaborate with Design Engineering to bring up cutting-edge silicon photonic and laser products, troubleshooting and resolving any technical issues that arise.
  • Validate Component and System Performance: Perform rigorous design validation on new chips and products through electrical and optical characterization of VLSI integrated circuits and optoelectronic systems.
  • Make Critical Decisions: Collaborate with multi-disciplinary teams to drive decisions around design trade-offs and specification adjustments, balancing performance, manufacturability, and time-to-market to ensure products are ready for customer deployment.
  • Develop Test Software and Infrastructure: Create and maintain software scripts and test hardware stations required for efficient and comprehensive validation.
  • Ensure Timely Delivery: Manage project schedules and execution to meet product timelines and customer demand, while maintaining the highest quality standards.


Basic Qualifications:
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
  • 5+ years of experience with component and system test equipment (BERT, DCA, OSA, etc.) and standard signal quality metrics (TDECQ, SRS, URS).
  • 5+ years of experience in programming languages (Python, etc.) for test automation and data analysis.
  • Knowledge of communication protocols and standards (Ethernet, PCIe, etc.).
  • Able to analyze complex technical problems, identify root causes, and develop effective solutions.
  • Understanding of data analysis, process control, and statistical methods.
  • Experience with SoC validation planning, bring-up, debugging, and optimization.
  • Experience with high-speed SerDes and their characterization and optimization.


Preferred Qualifications:
  • Master's or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
  • 5+ years Industry experience in semiconductor lasers, photonics, system test, and validation
  • Knowledge of component and system test equipment (BERT, DCA, OSA, etc.) and standard signal quality metrics (TDECQ, SRS, URS).
  • Proficiency in programming languages (Python, etc.) for test automation and data analysis.
  • Knowledge of optical transceiver packaging and integration challenges.

title: Data & Visualization Analyst

This role bridges the gap between raw data and meaningful insight, combining business analysis expertise, data engineering proficiency, and dynamic dashboard development into a seamless client experience. title: FUNCTIONAL SAFETY SOFTWARE DEVELOPER – ADAS
description:
Why join Aptiv?


You'll have the opportunity to work on cutting-edge applications, develop breakthrough technologies, and deliver innovative solutions to some of the world's leading automotive brands. See your work come to life on the road, helping make mobility safer, greener, and more connected. Ready to shape the future of mobility with us?


YOUR ROLE


As a Functional Safety Software Developer – ADAS, you will develop safety-critical software for Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and next-generation vehicle platforms. You will work on AUTOSAR-based embedded software, Functional Safety implementation, and Automotive SPICE-compliant development processes while contributing to solutions that make driving safer and smarter.


Responsibilities


· Develop Embedded C/C++ software for safety-critical ADAS applications.

· Configure and integrate AUTOSAR components using Vector DaVinci and related tools.

· Implement and verify ISO 26262 Functional Safety requirements.

· Perform software development activities aligned with ASPICE SWE.1 through SWE.6.

· Configure and optimize Memory, OS, BSW, and MCAL modules.

· Debug software issues on target hardware platforms and support system integration activities.

· Collaborate with global teams to deliver high-quality automotive software releases.


YOUR BACKGROUND


· Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electronics, Electrical Engineering, Instrumentation, or related disciplines.

· 6-10 years of automotive embedded software development experience.

· Strong hands-on experience in Embedded C/C++.

· Experience in AUTOSAR architecture, configuration, and integration.

· Experience with Vector DaVinci configuration tools.

· Hands-on implementation experience in ISO 26262 Functional Safety projects.

· Experience executing ASPICE SWE.1 to SWE.6 activities.

· Experience working with NXP, Infineon, or TI microcontrollers.

· Strong debugging and root-cause analysis skills.

Highly Preferred

· EB Tresos configuration experience.

· MCAL development/configuration experience.

· Safety configuration implementation.

· DFA (Dependent Failure Analysis).

· FTA (Fault Tree Analysis).

· Experience in ADAS, Radar, Camera, Domain Controller, Autonomous Driving, or Active Safety projects.


Please Note


This role is intended for hands-on software developers with AUTOSAR, Functional Safety, and Embedded C/C++ expertise. Profiles focused primarily on validation, testing, project management, or safety documentation without software development experience may not be a fit.


WHY JOIN US?


· You can grow at Aptiv. Aptiv provides an inclusive work environment where all individuals can grow and develop, regardless of gender, ethnicity or beliefs.

· You can have an impact. Safety is a core Aptiv value; we want a safer world for us and our children, one with: Zero fatalities, Zero injuries, Zero accidents.

· You have support. We ensure you have the resources and support you need to take care of your family and your physical and mental health with a competitive health insurance package.


YOUR BENEFITS AT APTIV


· Higher Education Opportunities (UDACITY, UDEMY, COURSERA are available for your continuous growth and development)

· Life and accident insurance

· Sodexo cards for food and beverages

· Well Being Program that includes regular workshops and networking events

· EAP Employee Assistance

· Access to fitness clubs (T&C apply)

· Creche facility for working parents


APPLY TODAY, AND TOGETHER LET'S CHANGE TOMORROW!

Job Description:

What’s the role?

Shell is seeking a Retail Site Assurance Advisor to join its team in Calgary.


The purpose of the role is to provide independent assurance across Shell's Company Owned retail network in Canada, with risk and assurance responsibilities extending to other business channels and locations as required, strengthening business controls, minimizing losses, supporting compliance, and enabling resilient business performance.


Key Accountabilities

Retail Site Assurance & Auditing

  • Provide on-site assurance coverage across Company Owned retail sites throughout Canada.
  • Conduct scored, sample-based audits of service stations to monitor Retailer compliance with company requirements, operating procedures and business controls.
  • Assess the effectiveness of site-level controls and identify financial, operational, inventory and compliance risks.
  • Document audit findings, provide clear feedback to Territory Managers and District Managers and recommend proportionate corrective actions.

Loss Prevention & Investigations

  • Identify, investigate and recommend solutions to minimize operational and financial losses.
  • Guide and support Territory Managers on general loss prevention and the resolution of loss-related issues.
  • Monitor, investigate and follow up on non-compliant or unusual activity.
  • Conduct root-cause analysis and recommend practical control improvements to prevent recurrence.

Wetstock Governance & Reconciliation

  • Manage retail wetstock reconciliation processes, including the investigation and resolution of operational issues and inventory variances.
  • Collaborate with Territory Managers, Operations, Finance and Wetstock team to address recurring issues and strengthen wetstock controls.
  • Identify trends and recommend preventative actions to reduce future losses.

Retailer Risk Management

  • Provide ad hoc advice and assurance support to the Operations team to minimize potential risk.
  • Monitor and analyze transactional activities to identify trends, anomalies, and potential instances of fraud or misconduct.

Reporting, Insights & Business Support

  • Analyze audit, compliance and loss data to identify control trends and emerging risks.
  • Distribute clear data and insights to Sales, Operations and Finance Management to support informed decision-making.
  • Provide objective oversight through control reviews, investigations and assurance activities, identifying risks and recommending sustainable control improvements
  • Build effective working relationships and act as a trusted advisor to Territory Managers and cross-functional stakeholders.

Success Profile

  • Demonstrates integrity, independence and sound professional judgment.
  • Balances governance requirements with practical business realities and a customer-centric mindset.
  • Builds collaborative relationships across field, operational and functional teams.
  • Communicates findings objectively, respectfully and with a clear focus on solutions.
  • Shows strong attention to detail while recognizing broader business trends and risks.
  • Adapts effectively to changing priorities and works confidently in field environments.
  • undefined

What you bring

  • The candidate must have legal authorization to work in Canada on a full-time basis.
  • Bachelor's degree in accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Commerce or a related discipline.
  • Minimum three (3) years of relevant experience in audit, assurance, accounting, finance, risk management, loss prevention, retail operations or operational compliance.
  • Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret financial and operational data.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide clear, constructive feedback and influence without direct authority.
  • Ability to independently plan and complete field-based work while managing multiple priorities.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and business reporting tools.

Preferred:

  • Finance or accounting background.
  • CPA designation or near completion of the CPA program.
  • Experience conducting audits, control assessments, investigations or compliance reviews.
  • Experience with retail fuel operations, inventory reconciliation or wetstock management.

Travel & Working Requirements

  • Regular travel across Canada to complete site audits, investigations and assurance activities.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to retail locations, subject to Shell policies and applicable requirements.

title: Vans: Supervisor - Woodbury Commons
location: USCA > USA > New York > Central Valley 425 - VAN
description:
Vans is the original brand rooted in the authentic lifestyle of skateboarding. We are driven by our mission to inspire and empower everyone to live “Off The Wall” – embracing the youthful spirit of freedom, non-conformity, and relentless progression. Yesterday’s “Off The Wall” moment is today’s new normal, and at Vans, we believe in constantly outdoing ourselves. Together with our communities across the globe, our vision is to push culture forward because we believe that the pursuit of progression never ends. We are constantly inspired by the future generation of positive catalysts within our community.

So, before we get to the job details, take a minute to learn a little more about us – our values and our culture. If you can see yourself working side-by-side with a team of people who think and live “Off the Wall,” Vans just may be the place for you.

To learn more about our values and our culture, visit Vans Careers or .

Supervisor

What will you do?

A day in the life of a Supervisor at Vans looks a little like this.

As a Supervisor, you play a key role in supporting the store’s leadership team and driving abets-in-class customer experience. You will lead by example, coach and develop associates, and ensure operational excellence across customer engagement, merchandising, and store standards. In partnership with the Store Manager and Assistant Store Manager, you will help maximize store profitability, foster an inclusive team culture, and contribute to the store’s success. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced retail environment, enjoys mentoring others, and is passionate about delivering exceptional service. Let’s break down that day-in-the-life a bit more.

  • Deliver a high level of personalized customer engagement through genuine interactions.​
  • Support the store team in achieving and exceeding sales goals by monitoring progress against key performance indicators, while also achieving individual goals.​
  • Model selling behaviors and foster a consumer-centric mindset through authentic customer interactions.​
  • Coach and develop associates to deliver high levels of customer engagement and meet productivity goals.​
  • Supervise daily store operations, including opening and closing procedures, floor coverage, and task delegation.​
  • Support stockroom operations by organizing inventory, processing shipments, and ensuring timely product flow to the sales floor.​
  • Assist in training and onboarding new team members; provide ongoing feedback and support.​
  • Maintain visual merchandising standards and ensure product replenishment aligns with brand directives.​
  • Support inventory integrity through proper shipping, receiving, and loss prevention practices.​
  • Promote community engagement by participating in local initiatives and events.​
  • Uphold company policies, safety standards, and operational procedures.​
  • Foster a positive and inclusive store environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and learning.

What do you need to succeed?

We all bring unique skills to work each day. For this role, there are foundational skills needed to succeed, along with 1+ years of retail or store leadership experience in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment​. A High School Diploma or equivalent is preferred; but we value hands-on experience and demonstrated achievements most.

The foundation skills you will need in this position are:

· Proven ability to drive results through store teams and exceed sales and profit goals.​

· Skilled in coaching, motivating, and building high-performing, diverse teams.​

· Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to influence across all levels.​

· Solution-oriented and flexible in a fast-paced, dynamic retail environment.​

title: VP Info Security
description:
Overview

The VP of Information Security is the senior executive accountable for the protection of Piedmont Healthcare system's information assets, technology infrastructure, and patient data across a complex, integrated delivery network. Reporting directly to the Chief Information Officer (CIO), this position provides strategic vision, enterprise-wide governance, and hands-on leadership for all aspects of information security, cyber risk, and regulatory compliance.

Will be responsible for building and sustaining a mature security program capable of defending against sophisticated threats targeting healthcare — one of the most targeted sectors in the world — while enabling the organization to leverage digital innovation, cloud platforms, and advanced analytics in support of its clinical and operational mission.

This role serves as a primary advisor to the CIO and the Information Security Steering Committee on all matters of cybersecurity strategy, risk posture, and regulatory compliance, and is the organization's primary liaison to government agencies, law enforcement, and external security partners in the event of a significant cyber incident.

Responsibilities

Security Strategy & Program Leadership

  • Develop, implement, and continuously mature a comprehensive enterprise information security strategy aligned to business objectives, clinical operations, and the organization's risk appetite
  • Build and govern a security program spanning people, processes, and technology — including security architecture, engineering, operations, threat intelligence, and incident response
  • Establish and maintain a security governance framework, including policies, standards, procedures, and control frameworks (NIST CSF, HITRUST, ISO 27001, or equivalent)
  • Serve as the organization's authoritative voice on cybersecurity strategy, communicating risk posture and program maturity to the CIO, executive leadership, and Board Audit/Risk Committee
  • Define and manage a multi-year security roadmap, balancing proactive investment with operational sustainability

Risk Management & Threat Intelligence

  • Own the enterprise cyber risk management program — identifying, assessing, prioritizing, and remediating risks across clinical, operational, and administrative systems
  • Lead threat intelligence, vulnerability management, and red team/penetration testing programs to proactively identify and address exposure
  • Maintain situational awareness of the evolving healthcare threat landscape, including ransomware, nationstate actors, medical device vulnerabilities, and supply chain risk
  • Develop and maintain a comprehensive third-party and vendor risk management program, including security assessments for business associates and technology partners
  • Ensure cyber risk is effectively quantified, reported, and integrated into enterprise risk management and strategic planning processes

Regulatory Compliance & Privacy

  • Ensure the organization maintains compliance with all applicable information security and privacy regulations including HIPAA, HITECH, 21st Century Cures Act, state privacy laws, and CMS requirements
  • Collaborate with the Privacy Officer, Legal, and Compliance teams to align security controls with privacy obligations and to manage regulatory inquiries and breach notification requirements
  • Lead preparation for and response to OCR audits, state regulatory reviews, and other external assessments
  • Monitor the evolving regulatory and legislative landscape and proactively advise leadership on implications for the security program

Clinical & Operational Technology Security

  • Develop and lead a dedicated program for securing clinical technology, including medical devices, IoT/IoMT, connected diagnostics, and OT/ICS environments
  • Partner with clinical engineering, nursing informatics, and physician leaders to implement security controls that protect patient safety without disrupting care delivery
  • Drive secure design and deployment principles for EHR integrations, telehealth platforms, and digital health solutions
  • Ensure security is embedded into system development lifecycle (SDLC) and technology procurement processes across the enterprise

Leadership & Culture

  • Build, mentor, and retain a high-performing security team of 30 to 80+ professionals across security architecture, engineering, operations, GRC, and awareness
  • Cultivate a strong security culture across the organization through executive engagement, workforce training, and a security-by-design mindset
  • Foster a collaborative, transparent relationship with the CTO, infrastructure, and application teams to integrate security into technology operations
  • Establish strong relationships with peer CISOs, government agencies (HHS, CISA, FBI), and healthcare information sharing organizations (H-ISAC)

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Information Systems, or a related field required

Work Experience

  • 10 years of progressive information security experience, with at least 7 years in a senior security leadership role (CISO, Deputy CISO, VP of Security, or equivalent)
  • Demonstrated experience building and leading enterprise security programs at large, complex organizations — healthcare experience strongly preferred
  • Proven track record managing significant cybersecurity incidents, including ransomware response, data breach notification, and regulatory investigations
  • Experience presenting to and advising boards of directors, audit/risk committees, and C-suite executives on cyber risk and security strategy
  • Familiarity with clinical environments, medical device security, and the unique operational constraints of healthcare delivery

Licenses and Certifications

  • Professional certifications strongly preferred: CISSP, CISM, CISO, CRISC, GSLC, or equivalent; HCISPP or HITRUST certification
