title: Engineer-Design
description:
Career Area:

Engineering

Job Description:

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Role Definition
Product Engineering role who Designs, develops, builds, and implements Reman components, products, or technologies.


Responsibilities

  • The Position is responsible for End-to-End Product Engineering support for Reman Engine Arrangements and Engine Components.
  • The candidate should actively participate in Reman Engines NPI programs and be capable of leading program execution activities, including BOM configuration, completion of VDRA, validation of virtual builds, identification and resolution of build-related issues, and ensuring overall design readiness for production release.
  • The incumbent should have the capability to evaluate, resolve, and drive Engineering Change Requests (ECRs) originating from manufacturing plants, ensuring timely implementation of corrective actions and the successful release of engineering prints in support of production requirements
  • The candidate should be capable of evaluating and making informed decisions on Original Equipment (OE) design changes and assessing their impact on Reman products, ensuring technical feasibility, product quality, manufacturability, and alignment with Reman engineering objectives
  • The candidate should be capable of assessing reman ufacturability and making Reman/Reuse decisions for a wide range of engine components, ensuring technical feasibility, product quality, reliability, and cost effectiveness, while maximizing component recovery and reducing new part usage.
  • The candidate should possess strong technical knowledge of various remanufacturing and salvage techniques for engine components, with the ability to assess component recoverability, identify reclaim opportunities, and support cost-effective remanufacturing solutions while maintaining product quality and reliability
  • The candidate should possess strong product knowledge of Caterpillar diesel and gas engines and their major components, including cylinder heads, cylinder blocks, pistons and connecting rods, rotating components, fuel injectors, and turbochargers, along with a thorough understanding of remanufacturing and salvage techniques used to restore component functionality, reliability, and value
  • The candidate should be responsible for effectively collaborating and communicating with international process partners and cross-functional teams to obtain technical inputs, conduct design reviews, align on engineering decisions, and communicate project outcomes, recommendations, and status updates

Required Qualifications:

  • Requires a degree in an accredited Engineering or Materials Science curriculum.
  • The candidate should possess 10 to 15 years of experience in Product Engineering, Design Engineering, Remanufacturing and Salvage Technologies, with strong expertise in product development, engineering change management and component recovery processes.
  • Experience with Caterpillar diesel and gas engines and engine components will be considered a significant advantageStrong working knowledge in Creo for 3D design, modeling, detailing, and drawing creation.
  • Ability to apply Caterpillar engineering standards, design guidelines, and industry specifications in the development and release of high-quality engineering solutions.Strong verbal and written communication skills in English, with the ability to communicate effectively in a global work environment.
  • Demonstrated initiative, excellent interpersonal and organizational skills, strong problem-solving capabilities, and a proven sense of urgency in supporting and serving both internal and external customers.
    Skill Descriptors
    Analytical Thinking: Knowledge of techniques and tools that promote effective analysis; ability to determine the root cause of organizational problems and create alternative solutions that resolve these problems.
    Level Extensive Experience:
    • Seeks discrepancies and inconsistencies in available information; explains variances.
    • Organizes and prioritizes the sequence of steps to be taken to remedy the situation.
    • Identifies many possible causes for a problem based on prior experience and current research.
    • Quantifies the costs, benefits, risks and chances for success before recommending a course of action.
    • Approaches a complex problem by breaking it down into its component parts.
    • Chooses among a diverse set of analytical tools according to the nature of the situation.

    Effective Communications: Understanding of effective communication concepts, tools and techniques; ability to effectively transmit, receive, and accurately interpret ideas, information, and needs through the application of appropriate communication behaviors.
    Level Working Knowledge:
    • Delivers helpful feedback that focuses on behaviors without offending the recipient.
    • Listens to feedback without defensiveness and uses it for own communication effectiveness.
    • Makes oral presentations and writes reports needed for own work.
    • Avoids technical jargon when inappropriate.
    • Looks for and considers non-verbal cues from individuals and groups.

    Managing Multiple Priorities: Knowledge of effective self-management practices; ability to manage multiple concurrent objectives, projects, groups, or activities, making effective judgments as to prioritizing and time allocation.
    Level Working Knowledge:
    • Recognizes changing demands and priorities; validates changes with management.
    • Obtains information about how current assignments contribute to organizational goals.
    • Completes current work according to assigned priorities.
    • Responds to day-to-day operational priorities while still making progress on project work.
    • Performs at least 2-3 concurrent activities without reducing productivity.

    Technical Excellence: Knowledge of a given technology and various application methods; ability to develop and provide solutions to significant technical challenges.
    Level Working Knowledge:
    • Provides effective technical solutions to routine functional challenges via sound technical competence, effectively examining implications of events and issues.
    • Effectively performs the technical job aspects, continuously building knowledge and keeping up-to-date on technical and procedural job components.
    • Applies technical operating and project standards based on achieving excellence in delivered products, technologies and services.
    • Applies current procedures and technologies to help resolve technical issues in one's general area of technical competence.
    • Helps others solve technical or procedural problems or issues.

    Product Design - MFG: Knowledge of processes, approaches, tools and techniques of product design; ability to convert customer and market requirements into product design.
    Level Extensive Experience:
    • Develops improvement plans for senior management and evaluates the outcome of the design against the functionality.
    • Advises others on the development of multiple products and their functionality.
    • Trains others on advanced tools and approaches of product design.
    • Monitors the processes and procedures of a complex product design to ensure functional requirements are met.
    • Evaluates feedback from customers and consults on functional weaknesses.
    • Controls design and development costs of a proposed product through effective resource coordination.

    Product Design and Development: Knowledge of product features; ability to design, build, and develop a new product, technology, or service from concept through to production.
    Level Working Knowledge:
    • Builds three-dimensional models with basic materials.
    • Communicates with professionals to understand various requirements of product design.
    • Tests and evaluates alternative means of production being considered for use.
    • Uses automated tools to design or modify the design of a product.
    • Assists in building a complex prototype of product.

It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as an exhaustive summary of all responsibilities, duties and effort required of employees assigned to this job. Job Description

The Health & Wellness Promotion Coordinator position leads and manages Information, Education & Communication (IEC) efforts and Behavior Change Communication (BCC) strategies in a variety of projects throughout Winona State University. Responsibilities focus on the design, implementation and evaluation of these efforts for health and wellness promotion on campus using social media, target population level channels, interpersonal communication, and technology. A major focus of this position is on participatory learning and action to enable the empowerment of students. Primary topic areas include but are not limited to the following: holistic wellness, health and hygiene, prevention and proactive actions for well-being, addressing emotional issues, substance abuse prevention and early intervention, and other areas uniquely encountered by the student population.


Responsibilities:

1. Provide leadership on health & wellness promotion within Health & Wellness Services. Design and implement Behavior Change Communication strategies in partnership with relevant entities on and off campus. Evaluate all programs (oversee experiential learning opportunities, classroom projects/research, in-class presentations, peer health educator program, etc.) based on relevant public health policy and theory. Utilize American College Health Association’s (ACHA) Healthy Campus 2020 for planning, implementing, and evaluating effective health and wellness promotion programs across departments, disciplines, and community agencies. Leadership, marketing, and communication to engender behavior change through participatory, empowerment and capacity building techniques. Leading and directing health and wellness promotion needs, concerns, and resources from a prevention and early intervention framework utilizing evidence-based prevention and behavior change principles and programs. Demonstrating cultural competence and inclusiveness in working with diverse populations and cultures in addressing issues of diversity and health. Disseminate information via social media that is designed to increase awareness of current health and wellness concerns/issues and campus’ response to those issues regarding services and programs available.


2. Collaborate with the Director of Health & Wellness Services in ensuring compliance with the Federal DFSC Act & Amendments – completing the required Biennial Review and coordinating Campus efforts to comply with the Act (partnering with the VP of Student Life,, Residence Life, & Security, providing for prevention and early intervention activities).Monitor and conduct analysis of statistical data with regard to student’s health behavior, attitudes, and perceptions; assist in developing the strategic plan for Health & Wellness Services.


3. Empower students and encourage involvement by implementing peer education, advocacy and governance programs. Utilize social technology to reach students. Design and coordinate the delivery of customized presentations to students and internal and external constituencies on issues of student health, wellness and behavior.


4. Work collaboratively with academic departments, Residence Life, Counseling, and Fitness amongst others to assist and support them in efforts to enhance, motivate and prepare students for a successful healthy college experience.Promote campus wellness.


5. Serve as a university representative for student health and wellness issues on campus, local, state, and national committees, organizations and boards; and at conference presentations.


6. Manage health and wellness promotion budget and supervise student employees, including graduate assistants. Oversee Student Health & Wellness Advocates to act as liaisons for campus groups such as athletes and Residence Life staff, etc. (preventing excessive alcohol use/alcohol poisoning; referral mechanisms for sexual assault,).


7. Perform other duties as assigned to ensure the smooth functioning of the department and maintain the reputation of Winona State University. Including but not limited to in an innovative and independent manner pursue potential funding sources for health and wellness promotion programs i.e. grants, collaborative agreements or partnerships with internal and external constituencies and serving as a resource person for students, faculty, and staff regarding college and young adult health and wellness concerns – responding to emails, phone calls, speaking requests, and interviews – providing current and factual health information.

Job Description Summary

The Estimator 3/Sr. Estimator is responsible for business development and the preparation of complete electrical estimates of industrial and commercial projects including, automotive, mission critical, and healthcare. Complete estimates include all quotations and subcontractors required for the project. A high degree of accuracy, communication, and attention to detail is required.



Job Description:

Role & Responsibilities


•Accurately interpret the design drawings and specifications submitted. This includes all design drawings from all disciplines including civil, structural, architectural, and mechanical drawings
•Schedule and participate in estimating kickoff meetings.
•Perform the pre-bid bid reviews with the Estimating Team including the Chief Estimator.
•Lead final bid reviews with the entire Estimating Team.
•Prepare quotation of materials and subcontracts.
•Review and understand the Electrical and Low Voltage Systems specifications.
•Review bid documents and attend pre-bid meetings and job walks to determine the scope of work.
•Participate in interview prep meetings, customer interviews, and respond to customer questions.
•Participate in committee and department meetings.
•Identity and develop estimating standards.
•Accurately estimate labor, materials, and administrative costs for projects.
•Lead small teams of estimators tasked with preparing estimates for large projects.
•Assist the Chief Estimator with scheduling of estimating resources and planning required to ensure timely and accurate completion of estimates.
•Complete bid forms and prepare necessary supporting documentation.
•Create scope of work documents which accurately describe the inclusions, assumptions and clarifications used in preparing bid estimates.
•Develop scopes of work and/or bid leveling documents used in soliciting quotes for third-party products and services. Capable of leveling bidders to ensure complete scopes of work and accurate cost information.
•Collaborate with the Business Development team and/or division leadership to develop a bid strategy specific to each opportunity.
•Verify and maintain detailed records of estimate revisions and other supporting documents as needed, to serve as back-up for open book projects.
•Verify completion of the estimator check list.
•Facilitate communication with the Sales and Preconstruction team as well as Designers, Project Managers, General Foreman, and others to resolve issues throughout the project.
•Utilize estimating software to properly estimate projects, enter data, and perform takeoffs.
•Assist with the development of training and mentorship programs.
•Develop and mentor talent.

Qualifications and Education Requirements


•High School Diploma or equivalent.
•Two (2) year degree in related field or equivalent experience.
•8+ years of experience in electrical conceptual estimating, low voltage estimating, National Electrical Code requirements, and design/build estimating required.
•Strong computerized estimating skills using electrical estimating software; experience with Accubid or Enterprise is a plus.
•Strong knowledge in the use of Bluebeam software for estimating and construction-related purposes.
•Strong mathematical skills, coupled with strong Microsoft Office skills (with an emphasis on Excel) are mandatory requirements for this position.
•Competent organizational skills and attention to detail.
•Effective verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills. Additionally, presentation skills are highly desirable.
•Ability to multi-task and prioritize workload in a manner that ensures timely and accurate completion of all assigned tasks.
•Ability to work in both an autonomous environment, as well as part of a larger team.
•Effective problem-solving skills.
•Effective time management skills and ability to manage workload and meet deadlines.

Key Skills and Competencies


•Able to work cooperatively within diverse teams, both internally and externally, to achieve group and organizational goals.
•Maintains and promotes individual and organization integrity and values in conduct of all activities.
•Maintains effectiveness in varying work environments where circumstances and priorities are changing.
•Able to select and use appropriate technology to accomplish assigned tasks. The individual is able to manage and use data efficiently to solve problems and is able to learn and adapt to new technologies effectively, in teams and individually.
•Demonstrates a broad repertoire of ways to think about, understand and creatively handle complex ideas, problems, and situations.

The individual also has public speaking skills, is able to express ideas to others, and can write/edit memos, letters, and complex technical reports clearly and effectively.

This individual also follows through on commitments, implements decisions that have been agreed upon, maintains confidentiality with sensitive information, acknowledges and learns from mistakes without blaming others and recognizes the impact of one’s behavior on others.

Physical Requirements

The Credit & Collections team at Cohesity is responsible for managing the company’s receivables portfolio and driving timely collection of customer payments across all global entities. Leveraging NetSuite as our core ERP, the team partners closely with Billing, Cash Applications, Order Management, and Sales to maintain healthy DSO, resolve disputes, and support a seamless customer experience.


As a Credit & Collections Analyst I at Cohesity, you will own a portfolio of customer accounts, driving proactive collection of outstanding invoices, resolving billing and payment disputes, and partnering with cross-functional teams to reduce aging and support accurate accounts receivable reporting in NetSuite.


We are a collaborative and results-driven Credit & Collections team, passionate about building strong customer relationships while protecting Cohesity’s cash flow. Working in a fast-paced, global environment, we partner closely with Billing, Cash Applications, and Sales to resolve challenges, streamline processes, and ensure a seamless customer experience.   • Build strong, cross-functional relationships with Cash Applications, Billing, Order Management, Customer Service, and Sales to resolve customer and internal queries, and support internal, external, and SOX audits

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field

  • Hands-on experience with NetSuite, Oracle, or similar large ERP Accounts Receivable systems
  • Excellent verbal and written communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to work independently and manage a collections portfolio end-to-end
  • Advanced MS Excel skills for reporting and analysis, and comfortable working towards targets in a fast-paced, metrics-driven environment
  • Demonstrated experience leveraging AI tools to streamline workflows, enhance productivity, and support high-quality decision-making

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

Caterpillar’s BCP division is hiring a Sr. Design Engineering Specialist located in Sanford, NC. This role provides technical and project leadership for the performance, tuning, and integration of machine control systems on Compact Track Loader (CTL) and Skid Steer Loader (SSL) products.


Role Summary

The Senior Performance and Integration Engineer will lead and execute complex, cross-functional projects by building collaborative relationships across product, commercial, engineering, software, and manufacturing teams. A significant portion of this role is dedicated to hands-on machine tuning, calibration, and performance evaluation activities to ensure delivery of high-quality, customer-focused machine-control solutions and software features.


The successful candidate will serve as a technical leader, mentor engineers, and evaluate tradeoffs involving performance, velocity, cost, manufacturability, reliability, and customer value.


What You’ll Do

  • Use customer feedback, competitive benchmarking, field performance data, emerging-technology evaluation, and engineering analysis to identify and prioritize continuous improvement opportunities.
  • Collaborate with customers and product, commercial, and systems engineering teams to develop and execute multi-generational product plans for CTL and SSL machine systems.
  • Perform hands-on machine tuning, calibration, and performance evaluation activities to optimize machine behavior, validate control-system performance, and deliver customer-valued features.
  • Ensure machine hardware and software meet customer, product, and production requirements by developing and validating control systems that deliver best-in-class performance and customer value.
  • Coordinate activities across hydraulics, engines, electrical, and software teams while building stakeholder alignment.
  • Own system-level technical requirements and performance targets with validation plans for assigned machine systems.
  • Support factory testing and calibration of production machines and ensure control system design is robust for manufacturability.
  • Mentor and develop engineers through technical leadership, knowledge sharing, work reviews, and promotion of engineering best practices.

What You Have


Education

Bachelor's degree from an accredited Engineering, Computer Science, or Materials Science curriculum, or equivalent industry experience.


Core Skills

  • Systems Engineering and Technical Excellence - Demonstrated ability to solve significant technical challenges involving complex machine controls and integrated software and hydraulic systems.
  • Analytical Thinking - Ability to break complex problems into component parts, identify potential root causes, recognize discrepancies in available information, select appropriate analytical methods, and develop effective alternative solutions.
  • Decision-Making and Critical Thinking - Ability to evaluate alternatives with multiple stakeholders, distinguish between the technical content and organizational context of a decision, anticipate risks, and make timely, informed recommendations.
  • Product Development - Knowledge of product-development methodologies and the associated requirements, design, integration, testing, production, and support activities needed to deliver new or enhanced products.
  • Troubleshooting Technical Problems - Ability to anticipate, detect, isolate, and resolve complex or non-recurring problems involving interactions among mechanical, hydraulic, electrical, controls, software, and machine systems.



Top Candidates Will Also Have

  • Proven experience with on-machine tuning of complex control and hydraulic systems, including system-level ownership of requirements, performance, and customer outcomes.
  • Experience translating customer, competitive, field, and engineering insights into successful product improvements.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex technology, performance, or integration projects from concept through production by communicating effectively, building alignment, and influencing stakeholders across engineering, product, commercial, and manufacturing organizations.
  • Software and controls design experience, including the ability to interpret and evaluate implementations developed in MATLAB, C, and Simulink.
  • Demonstrated success developing the technical capability of other engineers.
  • Previous experience with hydraulic system design or testing.
  • Experience using Vector CANape to adjust control parameters and operating construction machines to validate the resulting machine behavior.

  • Visa sponsorship: Visa sponsorship is not available

title: Director, Operational Resilience
description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit

What You'll Be Doing


As a member of the Operational Resilience team, you’ll help strengthen how CIBC prepares for, responds to, and recovers from disruptions across the Regions. As a Director, Operational Resilience, you’ll lead the execution, management, and delivery of the Regional Operational Resilience Program in alignment with Enterprise direction, governance, and priorities. You’ll work closely with business, infrastructure, technology, and risk partners to ensure program requirements are clearly communicated, embedded, and operationalized across the Regions. You’ll also lead enterprise and regional reporting, oversee the maintenance and enhancement of the Operational Resilience repository, and provide insights that support effective oversight and decision-making. In this role, you’ll help advance CIBC’s resilience mandate by strengthening program execution, improving reporting, supporting regulatory compliance, and identifying opportunities to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.


At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.


How You'll Succeed

  • Program leadership - Lead the Regional Operational Resilience Program, ensuring alignment with Enterprise strategy, governance, and priorities. Partner with regional stakeholders to deliver key resilience activities and support the ongoing execution of the program across the Regions.
  • Reporting and insights - Lead the development and enhancement of Operational Resilience dashboards and reporting for both the Enterprise and the Regions. Analyze data, assess risk insights, and communicate clear, concise recommendations to support oversight and decision-making.
  • Process and repository management - Define requirements, create user stories, and test changes for the Operational Resilience repository. Monitor program actions and follow-up items, and support the timely completion of deliverables, remediation activities, and ongoing enhancements.
  • Automation and continuous improvement - Identify opportunities to automate reporting, improve operational efficiency, and strengthen program processes. Contribute lessons learned and recommendations that support the continued evolution of the Enterprise Operational Resilience Program.
  • Risk, controls, and compliance - Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and internal policies, standards, guidelines, and controls. Perform designated Operational Resilience controls by documenting processes clearly, executing controls consistently, and maintaining appropriate supporting evidence.
  • Leadership and partnership - Provide leadership, coaching, and development support to build team capability and performance. Foster strong collaboration across business, infrastructure, technology, and risk teams to support effective execution of the resilience mandate.

Who You Are

  • You’re a strategic thinker. You can connect day-to-day program execution to broader business goals and enterprise priorities. You bring strong planning, organization, and management skills to complex initiatives.
  • You are an expert communicator. You can take detailed or technical information and communicate it in a clear, concise, and audience-appropriate way. You have strong written, verbal, presentation, and reporting skills.

title: Emergency Medical Technician - Gouverneur, NY
description:
Job Title: Emergency Medical Technician
Department: Emergency Services
Location: Gouverneur, NY
Hours Per Week: per diem
Schedule: 12 - hour variable shift

SUMMARY:

The Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) provides immediate medical care and transport of patients during emergencies, playing a critical role in stabilizing and ensuring safe transport to medical facilities.


RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Responds to emergency calls, assess patients’ conditions, and determine appropriate medical interventions, coordinating with dispatch as necessary.
  • Safely transport patients to medical facilities, monitoring their condition and providing necessary care during transit.
  • Administer CPR, control bleeding, manage airways, and provide other life-saving measures to stabilize patients.
  • Utilize essential medical equipment such as, but not limited to, defibrillators, oxygen delivery systems.
  • Work closely with paramedics, firefighters, law enforcement, and hospital staff to ensure coordinated patient care reporting nature of injury as indicated.
  • Maintain accurate and detailed patient care reports, documenting assessments, treatments, and patient responses.
  • Ensure the cleanliness and readiness of emergency vehicles and medical equipment.
  • Interpret oral, written and diagnostic form instructions, including calculating weight and volume ratios.
  • Lift and move patients, often in challenging environments, such as extreme terrain or temperatures.
  • Participate in continuous education to stay current with medical protocols and enhance skills.
  • Ability to maintaining composure and professionalism in high-pressure situations.

Working Conditions and Physical Requirements (Expanded):

  • Work in a variety of uncontrolled and potentially hazardous environments (indoor/outdoor, inclement weather, confined spaces).
  • Maintain physical readiness to assist in lifting/moving patients using stretchers (up to 250 lbs with partner assist), medical equipment, and gear.
  • Walk, kneel, crawl, and climb over uneven terrain or in emergency conditions.
  • Transport essential medical equipment (e.g., EKG monitor, ALS/med bags) without assistance.
  • Remain calm and focused in high-stress, emotionally charged situations.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BLS required at hire, If not AHA, must obtain AHA BLS within 3 months of hire
  • Valid NYS Basic EMT
  • Valid Drivers License
  • Heavy Work - Exerting 50 to 100 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 25 to 50 pounds of force frequently, and/or 10 to 20 pounds of force constantly to move objects. Requires constant walking, standing or squatting

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Emergency Vehicle Operator Course (EVOC) or equivalent
  • Strong knowledge of medical procedures and emergency care techniques

EDUCATION:

LICENSES / CERTIFICATIONS:

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Drive - Clinical - Roles in this category require frequent driving combined with mobile clinical care across settings such as emergency response, mobile clinics, and home health environments. Staff must repeatedly enter and exit vehicles, occasionally lift and carry equipment weighing up to 100 lbs. or more, and perform care within patients’ homes or other confined, unpredictable, or uncontrolled environments. These positions demand strong fine and gross motor control, firm grasping, and heightened visual and auditory awareness to ensure safe and effective care delivery. Emotional and cognitive demands are substantial due to rapid decision‑making, direct exposure to critical or sensitive situations, and independently managing patient care in the field or home setting. Environmental exposures may include traffic hazards, infectious agents, extreme temperatures, variable home conditions, and hazardous materials. Valid licensure, physical readiness, and flexibility for extended or on‑call schedules are typically required.

For disease specific care programs refer to the program specific requirements of the department for further specifications on experience and educational expectations, including continuing education requirements.

Any physical requirements reported by a prospective employee and/or employee’s physician or delegate will be considered for accommodations.

title: Supply Chain Specialist (m/f/d)
description:
To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.



Group/Division

KLA has manufacturing sites worldwide. The Global Operations (GOPS) team, comprised of Manufacturing, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing Engineering, Installation and Quality, builds our leading-edge technology. GOPS partners with KLA's global supply base and design engineering teams to develop new products, working continuously to build better, faster and more cost-efficient solutions.

What You'll Do

In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.


We are looking for a proactive and technically minded Supply Chain Specialist (m/f/d) to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for the strategic procurement of mechanical, electronic, and optical components and systems, while driving supplier performance, cost optimization, and supply chain excellence.

Working within a highly innovative and international environment, you will collaborate closely with internal stakeholders across engineering, production, logistics, and global procurement teams in the United States, Singapore, and Israel. You will play a key role in ensuring supply continuity, developing supplier partnerships, and supporting the long-term success of our business.

Key Responsibilities


  • Manage the sourcing and procurement of mechanical, electronic, and optical components and systems.
  • Independently negotiate contracts, pricing agreements, and commercial terms with suppliers.
  • Drive Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) improvements through strategic sourcing initiatives and framework agreements.
  • Develop and maintain strong supplier relationships while continuously improving supplier performance.
  • Identify and implement supply chain optimization opportunities to increase efficiency and reduce risk.
  • Represent the interests of the local site within supplier negotiations and escalation processes.
  • Collaborate closely with engineering, production, quality, and logistics teams to support operational and business requirements.
  • Work effectively with global procurement and supply chain organizations in the USA, Singapore, and Israel to align sourcing strategies and leverage best practices.
  • Monitor supplier performance, market trends, and industry developments to identify opportunities for continuous improvement.


Preferred Qualifications


  • Experience sourcing mechanical, electronic, and/or optical components.
  • Knowledge of supplier development and supply chain optimization methodologies.
  • Experience with contract management and strategic supplier negotiations.
  • Ability to work effectively within global, cross-functional teams.
  • Strong analytical skills and commercial acumen.

What We Offer


  • A challenging position within a global technology leader.
  • Close collaboration with international teams and suppliers worldwide.
  • The opportunity to influence sourcing strategies and supplier performance on a global scale.
  • A dynamic, innovative, and collaborative work environment.
  • Professional development opportunities and long-term career growth.

Minimum Qualifications

Required Qualifications


  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or a related field.
  • Several years of professional experience in procurement, purchasing, supply chain, or supplier management within an industrial environment.
  • Experience working in a low-volume, high-mix manufacturing environment is highly desirable.
  • Strong negotiation, communication, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Pragmatic and solution-oriented mindset with the ability to drive results independently.
  • Good knowledge of SAP and Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
  • Business fluency in German and English, both written and spoken.
  • Occasional domestic and international travel, including to the United States, may be required as part of this role up to approximately 20%.

About KLA

We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.

With competitive pay, great benefits, and endless opportunities, working for the City and County of Denver means seeing yourself working with purpose — for you, and those who benefit from your passion, skills and expertise. Join our diverse, inclusive and talented workforce of more than 11,000 team members who are at the heart of what makes Denver, Denver.


What We Offer


The City and County of Denver offers competitive pay commensurate with education and experience. New hires are typically brought into the organization between $93,566 - $128,000/year. We also offer generous benefits for full-time employees which include but are not limited to:


  • A guaranteed life-long monthly pension, once vested after 5 years of service
  • 457B Retirement Plan
  • 140 hours of PTO earned within first year + 12 paid holidays, 1 personal holiday, 1 wellness day, and 1 volunteer day per year
  • Competitive medical, dental and vision plans effective within 1 month of start date



Location


In this position you can expect to work at least three (3) days in office at the Denver International Airport - Gateway Building (4347 Airport Way, Denver, CO 80249).



The City and County of Denver utilizes a hybrid model workplace that balances the responsibilities of public service with the benefits of a flexible work environment. Employees work where needed, at a city site and/or in the field at least three days a week, and telecommute remotely at a designated workplace within the State of Colorado the remaining days. This policy is subject to change based on the needs of DEN operations.



Who We Are & What You’ll Do

About DEN



Since opening on Feb. 28, 1995, Denver International Airport (DEN) has become one of the world’s busiest airports. In 2025, 82,427,962 passengers passed through DEN, making DEN 4th busiest airport in the U.S. and the world’s 10th busiest airport. DEN is Colorado’s primary economic engine, generating $47.2 billion in annual economic impact for the state. At DEN, we are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace. We celebrate individuality and strive to keep Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Accessibility (EDIA) at the center of all that we do.


We are currently seeking an Associate Project Manager for our Systems Integration Management Office!

The Associate Project Manager for the Systems Integration Management Office (SIMO) plays a pivotal role in advancing Denver International Airport’s mission to deliver a world-class passenger experience through integrated systems thinking. Reporting to the Director of Systems Integration Management, this position helps operationalize SIMO’s vision by performing professional-level project management work from inception to completion by managing and coordinating cross-functional initiatives that align DEN’s capital programs, operations, maintenance, and customer service into a unified ecosystem.


This role is ideal for individuals with experience in coordination, operations, continuous process improvement, program/project management, or systems improvement—especially those who bring transferable skills from other industries. We welcome candidates with some college coursework and equivalent work experience who are eager to grow, lead, and contribute to a collaborative and innovative culture.


Specifically, as the Associate Project Manager, you will:

  • Project Manage: Lead and coordinate SIMO initiatives, ensuring alignment with DEN’s strategic priorities and capital investment plans.
  • Coordinate & Engage Stakeholders: Convene and coordinate subject matter experts (SMEs) across departments to streamline communication and decision-making.
  • Project Plan & Integrate: Support the implementation of capital and operational projects by assessing project status, identifying lead stakeholders, and helping prioritize and execute top-impact initiatives.
  • Systems Thinking: Identify and manage interdependencies across workstreams to ensure cohesive, enterprise-wide integration of projects and programs.
  • Performance Monitor: Track project progress using KPIs, prepare status reports, and support management of risks and implement mitigation strategies.
  • Communication: Prepare and deliver project updates to stakeholders and leadership, including reports on risks, milestones, and deliverables.
  • Continuous Improvement: Contribute to a culture of innovation by identifying opportunities for process improvement and operational efficiency in support.
  • Workforce Development: Supervise and mentor interns and fellows, fostering professional growth and collaboration.
  • Matrix Management: Coordinate the work of consultants and internal staff assigned to specific projects.

What You’ll Bring


We value diversity of ethnicity, race, socioeconomic status, sexual identity, gender, religion, language, ability, and experience and exemplify this through the makeup of our team at all levels. You'll be right at home here if you cultivate strong relationships and push yourself, your work, the people around you and Denver to the next level.



Our ideal candidate has some or all the following experience, skills, and characteristics:



  • Using project management principles, you’ve led or supported complex projects, even if not in a formal project management role.
  • You’re a systems thinker who enjoys connecting the dots across teams and initiatives.
  • You’re a strong communicator who can manage conflict, influence stakeholders, build relationships, foster collaboration, and negotiate solutions.
  • You’re adaptable, proactive, and eager to learn and grow.
  • You bring curiosity, initiative, and a collaborative spirit to your work.
  • You have strong interpersonal and written communication skills.



Required Minimum Qualifications



  • Education requirements: Bachelor's Degree in Business, Management, Public Administration, or a related field.
  • Experience Requirement: Two (2) years of professional project management experience in the related occupational group including coordinating, administering, and monitoring projects.
  • Education/Experience Equivalency: One (1) year of the appropriate type and level of experience may be substituted for each required year of post-high school education. Additional appropriate education may be substituted for the minimum experience requirements.

Internal Candidates Only: Please note that probationary employees are not eligible to apply to open positions until they’ve successfully passed probation. Please only apply if you have already passed probation.



Application Deadline


This position is expected to stay open until 10/07/2026. Please submit your application as soon as possible and no later than 10/06/2026 at 11:59 p.m. to ensure consideration.



Additional Information


FBI Background Check: FBI criminal background check is required for all positions at Denver International Airport (DEN). Employees are also required to report any felony convictions and/or moving violations to maintain this clearance and be eligible for continued employment. By position, a pre-employment physical/drug test may be required.


Snow/Emergency Duties: Denver International Airport is a 24/7/365 team operation. If weather conditions warrant or an emergency crisis occurs, all DEN employees can be required to work extended hours and/or shifts.

description:
Job Summary

Perform first level of on-site technical, data recording and assessment within the manufacturing environment of Quaker Houghton customers. Follows standard procedures and has readily available supervision or management where necessary to provide a high standard of Fluidcare support.

Job Description

  • Participate in addition of chemicals; including coolants, greases, oils, lubricants, cleaners and biocides as directed by site staff.
  • Perform bio-stick dip tests of all machine sumps and central systems.
  • Assist in the maintenance of coolant filters, washers, paint systems, pumps, air handling systems, etc. for sump changes and cleaning, as required to keep fluids within proper limits.
  • Measure and record coolant parameters and maintain lubrication schedules to ensure parameters are met to maintain the highest coolant conditions. This may involve the dropping and cleaning of tanks when required.
  • Liaise directly with the customer so that changes in coolant parameters are highlighted and can then be acted upon and enter results in appropriate databases.
  • Prepare detailed shift reports.
  • Assist in routine maintenance on customer’s equipment and fluid systems including product additions, filter changes, emptying gons, sump cleaning, etc. as directed.
  • Assist in disposal of contaminated articles (i.e. pails, gloves, samples, etc.) in accordance with prescribed measures, including waste management and recycling initiatives.
  • Assist in maintaining and calibrating all laboratory equipment; such as scales, pH meters, glassware, incubators, etc. in accordance with site control plan.
  • Assist in properly maintaining tools and utility equipment such as pumps, sump suckers, coolant dispensers, etc. in a safe and efficient manner.
  • Where appropriate: Cut-up, mount and prepare parts for metallurgical testing. Surface etching of parts for analysis. Measurement and metallurgical determinations consisting of hardness and microstructure analysis.
  • Supports site staff general organization initiatives (inventory, storage rooms, labeling, etc.)
  • May work in manufacturing environment with union associates. Interact with customer’s production and technical personnel and other suppliers
  • May be required to operate hand tools, shop tools and equipment. May be required to operate industrial equipment, such as: fork trucks, sump suckers, power washers, tuggers, etc.
  • May require working flexible hours.
  • Carries out other duties as directed. May have tasks specifically related to quality control, metalogical heat treat and the steel industry.
  • Provide other specifically agreed Fluidcare services as and when required by the Site Manager and/or Lead Technician – this may include operating a fork truck, recycling equipment, etc.
  • Must be able to safely work in a variety of potentially hazardous situations while adhering to Quaker Houghton’s Life Saving Rules.

About Us

At Quaker Houghton, we are experts in the development, production and application of industrial process fluids, lubricants and coatings for the manufacturing industry. We have been an integral part in the growth of the world’s largest industrial and manufacturing companies from aerospace and automotive to primary metal and energy. Today, we have a global presence, with our corporate headquarters located in Conshohocken, PA. Quaker Houghton is a global publicly traded company with a unique collaborative culture that supports career growth for its associates and offers competitive compensation and benefit programs.

title: Staff Engineer, Cloud
description:
At Verda, we're building a full-stack AI cloud, covering everything from data centers and hardware to our own cloud platform that the world's leading AI teams use to do serious AI work.

We strive to make a positive mark on the world through the infrastructure we build and give leading teams a service they can truly depend on. Headquartered in Helsinki, we operate globally with offices in London and San Francisco.

Join Verda while it's still being built - not once it's finished.

About the role

As Staff Engineer for Cloud, you set technical direction across multiple domains and teams, not just one. Where a Lead owns a single domain end to end, you operate at the level above it: spotting where domains need to work together, resolving disputes that a single team can't settle alone, and lending your judgement to the hardest technical problems wherever they surface.

This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role. You have no direct reports; your influence comes from technical credibility, sound judgement, and a track record of being right about hard things. You work closely with Leads, Engineering Managers, Product, and our Principal Engineer to keep architecture, sequencing, and trade-offs coherent across Cloud as it grows.

Your responsibilities

  • Set technical direction across multiple Cloud domains and teams, identifying where local decisions need to fit into a coherent whole.

  • Lead high-impact, cross-team technical initiatives end to end, staying close enough to the code and production systems to make grounded calls.

  • Partner with Leads, the Principal Engineer, Product, and Engineering Managers to align architecture, surface trade-offs, and keep dependencies visible.

  • Set and uphold engineering standards for correctness, testing, security, observability, performance, and data integrity across the teams you touch.

  • Resolve technical disagreements that cross domain boundaries, make the call, and document the reasoning so others can follow it.

  • Review designs and code, and mentor senior engineers directly through real work, multiplying your impact through others.

  • Turn recurring incidents and cross-domain friction into durable systemic fixes rather than one-off patches.

Your key competencies

We're not counting years of experience. We're looking for evidence that you've led technical work beyond the boundary of a single team, and that you can build and operate production systems in our core languages.

  • Proficiency in both Go and JavaScript (or equivalent experience), with hands-on experience building and operating production systems in each.

  • Experience setting technical direction across multiple systems or teams, not just owning one domain.

  • Strong software-engineering fundamentals: sound judgement on architecture, APIs, data, reliability, security, and operability.

  • A track record of building or substantially reshaping systems, not only maintaining or migrating existing ones.

  • The ability to resolve technical disagreements across team boundaries and clearly explain the reasoning and trade-offs behind a decision.

  • Comfort working directly in the code: debugging, reviewing, and operating production systems yourself.

  • Proven ability to mentor engineers and Leads, raising technical quality without becoming the only person allowed to decide.

  • Clear communication with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Comfort operating with ambiguity, incomplete systems, and a high degree of autonomy.

Nice to have

  • Experience with cloud platforms, distributed systems, public APIs, billing or payments, identity and access management, or developer-facing products.

  • Experience with event-driven systems, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, or production workflow systems.

  • Prior experience in a Staff Engineer or equivalent org-wide technical role.

  • Experience helping a domain or platform scale from an early implementation into a dependable product.

Why Verda

  • Profitable operations with rapid, sustained growth.

  • 40+ nationalities, with 6 different ones on the management team.

  • A real chance to make an impact and work alongside world class engineers, researchers, and partners across the global AI ecosystem.

Practicalities

  • Work mode: Hybrid (Helsinki or London)

  • Level: Staff Engineer

  • Employment type: Full-time and permanent

What's next

We're building fast and this role needs the right person behind it. There's no artificial deadline, but when we find who we're looking for, we move. If this sounds like your next move, apply now.

Please submit your application through our Careers page. We don't accept applications sent by email.

title: Food Safety and Quality Assurance Technician
description:
JOB SUMMARY
Monitor Food Safety & Quality Assurance (FSQA) support/evaluation programs and inspection/audit procedures to ensure compliance of products and processes to corporate and regulatory requirements at a Sysco Specialty Meat and/or Seafood Company.
RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Monitoring of FSQA programs including HACCP Program, sanitation standard operating procedures, pest control, good manufacturing practices, approved supplier program, foreign material control, plant sanitation, chemical control, product quality assurance, FSQA Customer complaints, food defense and security
  • Assist in Employee Training of FSQA Programs, Policies, and Procedures
  • Assist in Implementation of Independent FSQA Audit Program – SQF Audits
  • Assist when necessary for product evaluations, plant visits, and supplier/customer communication to assist other staff members. Assist as needed in any manner capable of during emergencies the plant President or GM (general manager) determines are paramount to the business.
  • Frequently interacts with the following: SSMC/SSSC Personnel, Operations, Sales, Transportation and Maintenance as well as Sysco Operating Companies, and supplier/customer personnel at the line level.
QUALIFICATIONS
Education
  • Formal job training in TQM principles, SPC, HACCP concepts, CFIA/FDA regulations would be beneficial.
  • Formal quality and sensory analysis training would be helpful.

Experience
  • One to 3 years of meat and/or seafood industry (as appropriate) experience at a federal CFIA/FDA meat and/or seafood processing plant (as appropriate).
  • Raw meat or seafood industry the only experience will be accepted instead of combined experience

Professional Skills
  • Demonstrate the ability to write reports, basic business correspondence, as well as to effectively present information and respond to questions from managers.
  • Demonstrate the ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide into all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.
  • Demonstrate the ability to define problems, collect data and establish facts.
  • Demonstrate the ability to interpret basic technical instructions.
  • Ability to use personal computer, lab equipment, food preparation equipment and office communication equipment.

Certifications, Licenses and/or Registrations
  • Valid driver’s license.


Physical Demands
  • Regularly required to talk or hear.
  • Frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls.
  • Occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and taste or smell.
  • Occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
  • Plant audits and inspections may require lifting of products up to 100 pounds and inspection requires working in a production environment on a moving line, lifting cartons, and visual inspection.
  • Corrected vision required for sensory analysis to identify color, clarity.
  • Warehouse and plant audit also requires close and distance vision to judge GMPs; peripheral vision and depth perception mandatory for safety.
Work Environment
  • Frequently exposed to fumes or airborne particles.
  • Occasionally works near mechanical parts and in high, precarious places and is occasionally exposed to wet and/or humid conditions, extreme cold, and risk of radiation.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate and operating in a refrigerated environment is common.
  • Plant audits/inspections and working at remote in-transit processing facilities and Sysco Operating Companies contain both moderate/loud noise and exposure to fumes and mechanical hazards.

title: Director, Legal Commodities
description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

What You’ll Be Doing

We're seeking Commodities Counsel to join our team to provide legal and regulatory advice for CIBC’s physical and financial commodities trading activities. The role supports CIBC’s Commodities team across energy, metals, power and environmental products, with a strong focus on transaction structure, regulatory analysis and risk identification.

You will be expected to demonstrate a solid foundation in the documentation of physical commodity transactions. You will review collateral packages to identify key terms and advise on the structuring of transactions to mitigate risk associated with debtor insolvency, commodity title claims, security interest perfection, and other risks related to CIBC’s secured creditor status.

You are expected to have knowledge of relevant US commodity derivatives regulatory requirements and US bankruptcy principles and must demonstrate the capacity to engage and manage external counsel as and when needed based on business requirements and transaction complexity. You should have experience dealing with major physical commodity classes relevant for CIBC, including, but not limited to, metal, natural gas and power, and environmental commodities.

Ideal candidates will have experience advising on U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”) and ISO/RTO licensing and/or membership requirements and their applicability to commodity transactions. You are expected to advise the business and relevant compliance teams on the implementation of relevant requirements and processes.

You should have a strong working knowledge of standard Master Agreements under which physical commodities are transacted, including the ISDA, NAESB, EEI, and associated physical annexes and credit documentation. Ideal candidates will have a working knowledge of emissions trading schemes and the documentation of transactions relating to environmental products. Ideal applicants will demonstrate an understanding of the trading book and the use of hedging tools, including listed futures contracts, to mitigate risks associated with CIBC’s hedging and financing activity for clients.

The successful candidate must coordinate the foregoing legal advice across a range of internal stakeholders across North America and London, including our compliance teams, trading desks, sales personnel, credit risk teams, and senior business management. The position is based in New York and reports directly to Senior Counsel, Commodity Finance (US) in CIBC’s US Capital Markets division.

How You’ll Succeed

· Provide day-to-day legal coverage for physical and financial commodities trading

· Draft, review, and negotiate a range of commodity financing and hedging agreements, including loans, leases, consignments, prepays, repos, forwards, options, and swaps, as well as security agreements, intercreditor agreements, and guarantee agreements supporting the foregoing

· Support the business with amendments to existing credit agreements as needed

· Review and advise on commodity storage and transportation agreements as needed

· Advise on enforceability risks associated with these agreements

· Advise on CFTC, FERC, and other regulations applicable to commodities trading in partnership with Compliance and Risk teams

· Provide time-sensitive legal advice to sales and trading personnel within CIBC’s US Capital Markets commodities business unit

· Analyze licensing and non-disclosure agreements that may be needed in support of the commodities business

· Support new commodity trading related initiatives advanced by CIBC’s US Capital Markets commodities business unit in a rapid-paced environment

Who You Are

  • JD from an accredited US law school
  • NY State Bar admission in good standing
  • 5 to 7 years experience as counsel in a top law firm, financial institution, commodity trading firm or US regulatory or self-regulatory organization in financial services

description:
Whether you’re a recent grad or a seasoned professional, you can experience meaningful career growth at Rosendin. We offer a wide range of job opportunities, competitive compensation, full benefits, an Employee Stock Ownership Plan and more.

Why Rosendin?

Committed. Innovative. Engaged.

If you’re looking to take your career to the next level and work with some of the best and brightest in the industry, we want to hear from you. Since our founding over 100+ years ago, Rosendin has been driven to positively impact the communities where we live and work. We are an organization built on integrity and we have a culture that empowers people, embraces diversity, and inspires everyone to do their best. As one of the largest EMPLOYEE-OWNED electrical contractors in the United States, you will have the unique benefit of being a shareholder at a company that is experiencing tremendous growth and success. When our people succeed and fuel our success, we reward them. We'd love to have you as a shareholder!


YOUR NEXT OPPORTUNITY:

We are seeking a driven and analytical Data Scientist to join our Data Analytics Team. In this role, you will leverage advanced analytics, statistical modeling, machine learning, and data visualization to transform raw procurement, supply chain, and job-cost data into actionable strategic insights. The successful candidate will work closely with procurement leaders, category managers, estimators, and field operations to optimize spend, mitigate market risk, forecast electrical commodity price volatility, and enhance supplier performance across electrical construction projects nationwide.



WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Build, maintain, and enhance enterprise spend intelligence models across electrical commodities (e.g., conduit/EMT, wire & cable, switchgear, solar/renewables, heavy equipment rentals).
  • Develop and maintain statistical forecasting models to project monthly, quarterly, and annual procurement spend across major electrical material categories and equipment.
  • Perform advanced spend classification, taxonomy alignment, and anomaly detection across ERP, invoicing, and purchase order datasets.
  • Identify cost-saving opportunities, leakage, rebate capture, and volume aggregation points across regional organizational units.
  • Develop predictive price models and index tracking algorithms for volatile electrical raw materials (e.g., copper, aluminum, steel, resins) to inform risk mitigation strategies and bid estimating.
  • Analyze tariff impacts, market surcharges, and macroeconomic trends to project material lead times and cost exposure.
  • Design and deploy automated supplier scorecards evaluating vendor performance on lead-time compliance, pricing variance, fill rates, and quality standards.
  • Model supplier financial health, capacity constraints, and risk profiles to support strategic sourcing decisions and RFP evaluations.
  • Analyze transactional procurement workflows (requisitions, PO conversions, invoice matching, catalog compliance) to identify operational bottlenecks and cycle-time reduction opportunities.
  • Partner with IT and systems teams to design, test, and integrate machine learning algorithms into enterprise procurement tools (e.g., Oracle Fusion, automated requisition tools).
  • Track and model inventory recirculations, regional warehouse pilot metrics, and excess material usage to minimize waste across field operations.
  • Design, build, and maintain interactive dashboards and reports (Power BI / Tableau / OBTI) for Procurement leadership team, executive leadership and category managers.
  • Build predictive TCO and asset depreciation models across owned and leased vehicles/heavy equipment to determine optimal economic replacement thresholds (e.g., mileage, engine hours, maintenance cost tipping points).
  • Translate complex statistical findings into clear executive summaries, strategic recommendations, and actionable field guidance.
  • Serve as the primary analytics subject matter expert within the Procurement organization, promoting data-driven decision-making across the enterprise.
  • The duties and responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and scope of work being performed by this position. This is not a complete listing and other duties will be assigned based on the position’s role within the business unit.


WHAT YOU BRING TO US:

  • Education: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in data science, Business Analytics, Statistics, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or a related quantitative field. Preferably a master’s degree. Minimum of 2 years in procurement or related field.
  • Experience: 3–5+ years of experience in data science, advanced analytics, or business intelligence—preferably within construction, manufacturing, engineering, or heavy industrial supply chains.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:

  • Proficiency in Python or R for data manipulation, statistical modeling, and machine learning. Proficient in using a computer and Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, etc.); Oracle preferred.
  • Advanced SQL skills for querying, joining, and structuring large enterprise datasets from relational databases and ERP platforms (e.g., Oracle, SAP).
  • Expertise with Power BI, Tableau, or similar enterprise BI tools.
  • Knowledgeable with time-series forecasting (ARIMA, Prophet, XGBoost), regression analysis, clustering, and NLP for spend categorizations.
  • Proficiency in advanced Microsoft Excel (complex functions, data modeling) and data pipeline orchestration.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to convey technical analytical concepts to non-technical leaders and procurement teams.
  • Curiosity, self-direction, and a problem-solving mindset suited for building processes from concept to execution.

TRAVEL:

  • 0% - 25%

WORKING CONDITIONS:

The Data Scientist II will work in a professional office environment, with the following conditions:

  • Extended periods of sitting, standing, walking, typing, carrying, pushing, and bending may be required.
  • Work is primarily conducted indoors, with varying environmental conditions such as fluorescent lighting and air conditioning.
  • Noise levels are usually low to medium.
  • Occasional lifting of up to 30 lbs. may be required.

title: FTC Customer Experience Specialist
description:
ABOUT US


PHINIA: Advancing sustainability today, powering a cleaner tomorrow.


PHINIA is a diversified industrial supplier and global leader in the development of fuel systems, electrical systems, and aftermarket solutions, with a strong portfolio of trusted brands that includes DELPHI®, DELCO REMY®, and HARTRIDGE™. With over 100 years of manufacturing expertise and industry relationships, PHINIA has approximately 12,500 talented employees and over 40 locations in 20 countries and is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, USA. Read More

JOB PURPOSE

The CX Specialist supports the delivery of a seamless and positive customer experience by capturing and analyzing the Voice of the Customer (VoC), identifying customer journey improvement opportunities, and supporting the enhancement of customer touchpoints. The role works closely with cross-functional teams to translate customer insights into actionable improvements and support continuous improvement across the EMEA customer experience.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Key Responsibilities


Voice of the Customer (VoC) & Insights

  • Support VoC activities including surveys, customer feedback, interviews, and other listening channels.
  • Analyze customer feedback and CX data to identify trends, pain points, and opportunities, and translate findings into actionable insights.
  • Support country teams in using customer insights to identify improvement priorities.

Customer Journey & Experience Improvement

  • Support customer journey mapping and identify key pain points and opportunities across customer touchpoints.
  • Coordinate CX improvement initiatives with relevant teams and track agreed actions and outcomes.
  • Regularly update journey maps to reflect changes in customer behaviour and business processes.

Digital Customer Experience

  • Support the continuous improvement of EMEA customer portals and other digital touchpoints by gathering customer needs, feedback, and improvement opportunities.
  • Collaborate with Digital, IT, Service, Product, and other teams to ensure customer needs are reflected in digital initiatives.
  • Monitor customer feedback and experience across digital touchpoints and identify improvement opportunities.

CX Performance, Reporting & Stakeholder Management

  • Develop and maintain EMEA CX scorecards, tracking key KPIs such as NPS, CSAT, and CES.
  • Monitor country-level CX performance, identify trends and gaps, and highlight key areas for improvement.
  • Coordinate regular KPI follow-ups with country teams and track agreed actions.
  • Prepare regular CX performance reports and insights for the CX Manager and relevant stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional and country teams to support a customer-centric approach and continuous improvement.

What we’re looking for

Qualifications

· Education: Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Marketing, or a related field.

· Experience: Minimum of 3-5 years in Customer Experience, Customer Insights or related fields preferably within the automotive aftermarket industry.

Skills

· Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret customer feedback, CX data, and identify actionable insights.

· Proven experience in customer journey mapping, VoC programs, and CX metrics such as NPS, CSAT, and CES.

· Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across functions.

· Good project coordination and organizational skills, with a proactive and customer-focused mindset.

· Fluency in English; additional languages are a plus.

Desirable Attributes

· Technical Proficiency: Experience with CRM systems, customer feedback platforms, reporting tools, and/or data visualization tools.

· Industry Knowledge: Understanding of the automotive aftermarket industry and customer needs is an advantage.

· Certifications: Relevant Customer Experience, Customer Insights, or quality management certification is a plus.

The position is responsible for the performance of tasks associated with the cleaning of hazardous, non-hazardous and food grade tanker trailers, on-site remediation, clean-up, equipment de-contamination and handling of hazardous materials.

  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent

  • Six or more months industry-related experience

Preferred qualifications:

title: Director, Payments Chapter Lead-1
description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit

What you'll be doing


As the Director, Payments Chapter Lead within Everyday Banking, you'll play a pivotal role in Personal and Business Banking, helping to shape and deliver CIBC’s purpose to make our clients’ ambitions a reality. You’ll manage and develop a team of ~8-15 payment product specialists building capabilities within your Chapter/team, drive consistency of tooling and methodologies, and support resourcing needs. Your leadership will foster a collaborative culture, ensure quality delivery, and build specialist expertise aligned with CIBC’s client aspirations. Payments expertise is at the heart of this role—you’ll leverage your deep understanding of open banking, payments products, networks, industry trends, and regulatory requirements to drive innovation and excellence. You’ll work closely with the Chapter Area Lead, Product Owners, and other leaders to diagnose, draft, and implement standards, supporting initiatives across multiple squads. As an active member of a Squad, you’ll contribute to high-quality work that advances Squad objectives and supports the Quarterly Business Review (QBR) process, while nurturing your team’s growth and ensuring compliance with CIBC policies and standards.


At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.


How you'll succeed


  • Chapter leadership and development – Manage and develop team members through coaching, performance management, and capability building to ensure expertise aligns with business needs.
  • Payments industry expertise – Apply advanced knowledge of payments products, networks (such as Visa, Interac, and mobile wallet platforms), open banking and emerging industry trends to guide Chapter strategy and delivery.
  • Strategic planning and standards implementation – Diagnose, draft, and implement standards in collaboration with the Chapter Area Lead and Product Owners, advancing craft-building initiatives and workforce planning.
  • Cross-chapter collaboration – Drive standards, best practices, and initiatives across multiple Chapters, facilitating knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.
  • People management and positive work environment – Set context for assigned work, provide fair and accurate feedback, clarify performance expectations, and create a winning workplace.
  • Compliance and risk management – Ensure adherence to policies, standards, guidelines, and controls, applying them consistently and fairly.
  • Squad contribution – Deliver work as a Squad member, supporting Squad outcomes and participating in the QBR process.

Who you are


  • You’re an experienced people leader. You bring a minimum of 5 years of direct leadership experience, guiding teams to achieve their best.
  • You’re a payments expert. You possess 7-9 years of hands-on experience in payments products, ecosystems, and networks—including Visa, Interac, open banking, and mobile wallet spaces. You stay current with industry developments, regulatory changes, and competitive trends, and you have an established network within the payments industry.
  • You’re a strategic thinker. You excel at operational, tactical, and strategic planning, supporting business objectives for the short and long term.

Basic Qualifications:

description:

Innovate UK is implementing a significant strategic shift to strengthen its support for innovative businesses and maximise impact across the UK's innovation ecosystem.
