title: The Forum Network Northeastern University Co-Op
description:
GBH enriches people's lives through programs and services that educate, inspire, and entertain, fostering citizenship and culture, the joy of learning, and the power of diverse perspectives.

At GBH, we believe in the advantages of coming together to build community, mentor and learn from colleagues, and connect more deeply with our mission. As a result, the majority of our staff are hybrid and work both from home and onsite. Our current hybrid approach requires staff to work onsite a minimum of two days each week, every Tuesday and Wednesday, Hybrid staff are also welcome to come in additional days each week or may be asked to come in on other days by their manager.

DEPARTMENT OVERVIEW

GBH is an audience-focused, multimedia news organization creating distinctive journalism informed by the communities we cover.

The mission of GBH Forum Network is to project and protect the public voice, to inform and inspire lifelong learners, and to foster deeper understanding of the culture, education, politics, science, and literature of our time.

The Forum Network is a public media service funded by the Lowell Institute to document public speaking in the Boston region delivered by the world's foremost scholars, authors, artists, scientists, policymakers, and community leaders. Recordings are made available online to the public for free and are a resource of information and sourcing for GBH News. The Forum Network is committed to encouraging deeper understanding and civic engagement around the vital issues of our time.

JOB OVERVIEW

Co-ops will work for six-month terms on a full-time basis (including some evening hours) to support the Forum Network team with production planning, recordings, live streaming and digital publishing of public speaking events on the current issues of our time. This position supports the team’s work with internal and external stakeholders to deliver media production projects from initiation to final product. Co-op are also expected to suggest and develop new activities and strategies to increase the Forum Network’s reach to a younger audience.

The co-op’s unique perspective is welcome in the Forum Network team’s editorial planning and a co-op’s suggestions for content and social strategies will help grow the team’s reach. Successful candidates will have some experience and an interest in developing their skills as a multimedia producer able to record, edit, publish video content, hone camera and editing skills, as well as online communication and writing skills.

Other duties include cataloguing assets and media management, curation of assets on the Forum Network website and in social media platforms, and supporting external partnerships.

This role is based in Boston, MA, and requires your on-site presence every Tuesday and Wednesday at our Brighton office. Additional in-office days may be required at the discretion of your manager.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Participate in video field shoots and support digital distribution
  • Participate in hosting live streaming events
  • Suggest strategies and support execution on Forum Network’s website and social media workflows
  • Participate in team editorial planning and suggest new opportunities

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

  • Familiarity with the visual and audio elements for HD video.
  • Familiarity with video editing software
  • Solid writing and copy-editing skills
  • Knowledge of Photoshop and other illustration tools
  • Proficiency with social media platforms
  • Organization skills and time management

EDUCATION

Must be enrolled in a formal co-op program while obtaining a higher education degree.

LOCATION

This role is based in Boston, MA, and requires your on-site presence every Tuesday and Wednesday at our Brighton office. Additional in-office days may be required at the discretion of your manager.

Salary Range

$19.00 - $19.00

Compensation offered within this range is determined by skills, experience and internal pay equity.

GBH is an equal opportunity employer. The community and audience we serve are diverse, and we wish to foster that diversity in our workplace. Toward that end, GBH does not discriminate against individuals in hiring, employment, or promotion based on race, religion, color, sex/gender, gender identity and gender expression, age, marital status, national origin, sexual orientation, citizenship, disability, veteran or military status, political belief, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Senior Analyst, Tax Operations - US Indirect Tax
description:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.


Location: Los Angeles (preferred) or Los Gatos, CA. Hybrid schedule, 3x a week in-office (Tues-Thurs).
Department: Tax Operations

Reports To: Senior Manager, Tax Operations - US Indirect Tax



The Role


Netflix's US Indirect Tax ("ITX") team manages transaction taxes collected from customers and remitted to state and local governments — including sales, use, amusement, communication services, and admissions taxes — as well as property tax, business license tax, and certain gross receipts taxes.

We're looking for an experienced, detail-oriented US Indirect Tax Senior Analyst to own compliance, audit, analytical, and research work across multiple tax types. The ideal candidate has extensive compliance and audit experience and is a self-starter with strong organizational, communication, and process improvement skills. This is a hands-on role for someone who can successfully execute multiple priorities in parallel, is highly detail-oriented in calculations and writing, and identifies and implements process improvements.

Responsibilities

  • Manage sales and use tax audits from notice through resolution, including data gathering, workpaper preparation, exposure analysis, and correspondence with state and local auditors.
  • Prepare and review sales/use, gross receipts, business license, and other transaction taxes compliance filings across multiple jurisdictions, ensuring accuracy and timeliness.
  • Perform Month End accounting reviews, including preparing journal entries for tax reclassification and completing account reconciliations.
  • Gather and review information for Unclaimed Property Compliance, including coordinating data deliverables from AP, Payroll, and Production Finance.
  • Assist in personal and real property tax compliance, including valuation review and coordination with outside property tax consultants (e.g., appeal filings and support).
  • Support personal and real property tax audits, including responding to information requests and evaluating assessment notices.
  • Identify and implement process improvements across audit and compliance workflows — including automation opportunities — to reduce manual effort and improve accuracy.
  • Research and analyze technical indirect tax issues (e.g., nexus, taxability, sourcing) and summarize conclusions for the team and stakeholders.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Finance, Accounting, Legal, and outside advisors on process improvement projects, audit strategy, business support, and compliance matters.
  • Maintain clear, audit-ready documentation and workpapers to support internal review, SOX testing, and external audit requests.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field, is required.
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in state and local/indirect tax, including sales/use tax audit and compliance work.
  • Strong analytical skills and experience working with large transactional data sets.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage competing audit and compliance deadlines and an array of competing priorities.
  • A track record of identifying and driving process improvement in indirect tax operations.
  • Excellent communication and project management skills, with the ability to collaborate and manage a variety of competing priorities.

Generally, our compensation structure consists solely of an annual salary; we do not have bonuses. You choose each year how much of your compensation you want in salary versus stock options. To determine your personal top of market compensation, we rely on market indicators and consider your specific job family, background, skills, and experience to determine your compensation in the market range. The range for this role is $160,000.00 - $245,000.00.

Netflix provides comprehensive benefits including Health Plans, Mental Health support, a 401(k) Retirement Plan with employer match, Stock Option Program, Disability Programs, Health Savings and Flexible Spending Accounts, Family-forming benefits, and Life and Serious Injury Benefits. We also offer paid leave of absence programs. Full-time hourly employees accrue 35 days annually for paid time off to be used for vacation, holidays, and sick paid time off. Full-time salaried employees are immediately entitled to flexible time off. See more details about our Benefits here.

Netflix is a unique culture and environment. Learn more here.

Inclusion is a Netflix value and we strive to host a meaningful interview experience for all candidates. If you want an accommodation/adjustment for a disability or any other reason during the hiring process, please send a request to your recruiting partner.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and celebrate diversity, recognizing that diversity builds stronger teams. We approach diversity and inclusion seriously and thoughtfully. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, ancestry, national origin, caste, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic makeup, marital status, or military service.

title: Intern, Product Business
description:
THE BUSINESS

We are Everyday Luxury™.

It's what we do and how we do it — together.

It's working alongside world-class talent in pursuit of world-class results.

It's maximizing your potential in a high-performance culture.

It's knowing that wherever you are, you belong.

THE TEAM

The mission of the Product Business Department is to drive the top and bottom line by making strategic and entrepreneurial inventory investments.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Aritzia is growing, and our Product Business team is growing with it. This is a unique opportunity to be part of the team responsible for ensuring that the right products are available at the right time, in the right quantities, at the right stores, and for the right prices. As the Intern, Product Business, you will support the team in executing their day-to-day merchandising and inventory management activities. Responsibilities you may support with are to:

  • Curate the right assortment across our brands, programs, and commodities to maximize sales in every climate
  • Allocate the product at the right time to each store

  • Identify products to order into future seasons

description:
Whether you’re a recent grad or a seasoned professional, you can experience meaningful career growth at Rosendin. Enjoy a true sense of ownership as you work with a proven industry leader on some of the most exciting and high-profile projects in the nation. We offer a wide range of job opportunities, competitive compensation, full benefits, an Employee Stock Ownership Plan and more.


Why Rosendin?


Committed. Innovative. Engaged.

If you’re looking to take your career to the next level and work with some of the best and brightest in the industry, we want to hear from you. Since our founding over 100+ years ago, Rosendin has been driven to positively impact the communities where we live and work. We are an organization built on integrity and we have a culture that empowers people, embraces diversity, and inspires everyone to do their best. As one of the largest EMPLOYEE-OWNED electrical contractors in the United States, you will have the unique benefit of being a shareholder at a company that is experiencing tremendous growth and success. When our people succeed and fuel our success, we reward them. We'd love to have you as a shareholder!


YOUR NEXT OPPORTUNITY:

Power System Protection Engineer III is a senior-level engineering position responsible for performing protection studies and developing relay settings to support the implementation, commissioning, and testing of protection systems for electrical power networks. This role focuses on designing and applying protection strategies for medium and high-voltage systems serving mission critical, commercial, and industrial facilities. The position requires advanced technical expertise, the ability to work independently on complex protection challenges, and the capability to mentor and train other engineering staff.


WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Design, specification, setting calculation, and coordination of protective relaying and relay control schemes.
  • Develop protection schemes and relay settings for electrical equipment, including transformers, generators, transmission lines, feeders, and buses, in accordance with client requirements and system specifications.
  • Develop and configure protection relay settings, including overcurrent, differential, distance and backup protection relays.
  • Perform coordination studies to ensure proper relay operation and minimize system downtime during fault conditions.
  • Use power system modeling tools (e.g. ETAP, SKM, CAPE, ASPEN) to simulate and analyze protection systems, fault scenarios, and equipment ratings.
  • Conduct studies such as fault analysis, short circuit, AC and DC arc flash and harmonics studies.
  • Support field testing, commissioning, and validation of protection relays and control systems to ensure proper operation and compliance with project requirements.
  • Diagnose and troubleshoot relay protection issues, perform root cause analysis, and develop corrective actions for mis-operations or unexpected trips.
  • Collaborate with other engineers, project managers, and clients to ensure the successful implementation of protection systems.
  • Prepare technical documentation, including relay settings, test reports, system protection studies, and coordination diagrams.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable industry standards and regulatory requirements (e.g., IEEE, IEC, NEC, NFPA 70E, NERC).
  • Act as a proactive technical leader, guiding project teams, solving complex protection challenges, and supporting project execution across all phases from design through commissioning.

WHAT YOU BRING TO US:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering (BSEE) with a power systems focus.
  • 6+ years relevant application experience in protection and relay settings for electric power systems supporting mission critical infrastructure, commercial and industrial facilities and substations.
  • A U.S.-based Professional Engineer (PE) registration is required.
  • High proficiency with power system modeling tools such as ETAP, SKM, ASPEN, and CAPE.
  • Applied knowledge and experience of Power system Protection on: Overcurrent / Over-Undervoltage, Transformer Differential, High and Low Impedance Busbar Differential, Generator Protection, Motor Protection, and Medium/High Voltage Line Differential and Distance Protection.
  • Strong experience developing protection schemes and relay settings for redundant power architectures supporting data centers and other mission critical facilities.
  • High proficiency in relay settings development and programming for SEL, Siemens, and GE protective relays.
  • Experience developing and managing relay settings files using vendor software such as SEL AcSELerator, GE Enervista, or equivalent.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor and develop technical teams.
  • Strong leadership, written and oral communication, and organizational skills.
  • Strong computer skills with the ability to identify and apply appropriate software tools to support complex engineering analysis.
  • Proven ability to manage

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL:

  • Advanced experience using Mathcad and Microsoft Excel for developing protective setting calculation sheets.
  • Working knowledge of NERC reliability standards, particularly PRC-019/023/024/025/026/027
  • Experience with commonly utilized communication protocols (DNP, SEL, MMS, Modbus, etc).
  • Working Knowledge of IEC 61850 (GOOSE, MMS, SV) and its application in modern substations and mission critical facilities.
  • Experience designing and supporting protection systems for redundant power topologies (e.g., N, N+1, 2N) common to data center electrical systems.
  • Proven ability to lead small to mid-size projects, including management of schedules, budgets, staffing, and technical execution.
  • Experience supporting proposal development including scope of work, level of work, engineering estimates, and schedule.
  • •Strong leadership skills with a demonstrated interest in training and developing early career engineers.

title: Quality Analyst
description:
Job Description :

About us:


With over 200 brands sold in nearly 180 countries, Diageo is home to some of the world’s most iconic drinks. From Johnnie Walker and Guinness to Tanqueray, Smirnoff and Don Julio, we craft brands chosen for life’s moments — from everyday connections to landmark celebrations.

Bring your talent, curiosity and ambition, and strive for your personal best alongside people who challenge, support and learn from each other. Together, as one outstanding team, we keep learning, improving and raising the bar for our brands, our business and each other.


Join us and play your part in making life’s moments mean a little more

About the Function:

Supply Chain & Manufacturing is where our brands are made, moved and delivered to the world.

With over half of our people working across more than 100 sites, this is a sophisticated, large-scale operation that brings together production, logistics, engineering and supplier partnerships.

It’s fast-paced and hands-on, with teams working together to ensure quality, efficiency and sustainability at every stage. From sourcing ingredients to getting products into customers’ hands, you’ll play a role in delivering the brands people know and love.


About the role

Role ensures that the beer produced in a brewery is of exceptional quality. Works with the primary goals of improving brewery operations, improving product quality, improving customer satisfaction levels, reducing costs (e.g. reworks) and helps to ensure that food safety standards are adhered to and maintained


Role Dimensions

Market/Function Complexity

(In-country depth vs regional breath)

The company makes both beer and spirits and operates 24 hours. To beat competition, an effective Quality Control/Assurance system is very critical. The process involves monitoring process inputs (Local raw materials) process control and finished product. To remain at the top in the market and satisfy the expectations and needs of the consumer at competitive cost, requires highly skilled and trained quality analysts



Financial Accountability (Budget/Revenue)

This role works with a shared budget in the quality department of UGX 2 Billion per year and takes care of Lab equipment that are essential in beer analysis worth 942,406 USD



Leadership Responsibilities

This position works within the Quality Team and has responsibility of influencing shift managers and operators respond timely to decisions that guarantee quality of the products


Top Accountabilities

· Adherence to analytical sampling plans ensuring 100% coverage.

· Production of timely, accurate, reliable results and reports, and ensure closure of process non-conformances by engaging relevant stakeholders.

· Ensure analytical lab performance important metrics are met.

· Generate statistical process control charts, supervise and advise any process deviations to ensure product consistence.

· Validate the performance of measuring systems critical to quality within the process to ensure product safety and meet regulatory requirements

· Ensure sensory evaluation is conducted for in process and finished product to guarantee product quality. Where applicable, managing sensory tests in the spirits' plant.


Qualifications required:

A holder of BSc preferably in food science and technology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Industrial Chemistry or microbiology

Skills & Experience:


· Minimum of 2 - 3 years meaningful work experience.

· Knowledge of Quality, Safety and Environmental Management systems.

. Solid Understanding in Microbiology/ hygiene, Brewing and Packaging process

Working with Us


Flexibility is key to our success. Talk to us about what flexibility means to you so that you’re supported to manage your wellbeing and balance your priorities from day one.

Our purpose is crafting iconic drinks chosen for life’s moments. And it’s our people, with their different experiences, perspectives and talents, who make that possible.


We value diversity in its broadest sense and want everyone to feel they can belong, contribute and strive for their personal best. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives — challenging, supporting and learning from one another as one outstanding team.


Together, we’re constantly learning and improving, combining the strength of our people, capabilities and iconic brands to raise the bar, grow and win. Wherever you join us, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, make an impact and play your part in making life’s moments mean a little more.


Ready to bring your best? This could be your opportunity.

title: Technical Artist
description:

In 2018, our hard work came to fruition and Two Point Hospital was born into the world to much acclaim. After Hospital we had a dream of creating an entire world of these little people games within the place we call "Two Point County", and in 2022 our latest game Two Point Campus was released. Two Point Studios sizzled into existence in the summer heat of 2016 with a goal to

We are looking for an experienced, self-sufficient technical artist to join the team, to

push the visual quality of Two Point Museum and our exciting, upcoming little people

games to the next level!

You will comfortably bridge the gap between art and code, driving pipeline efficiencies

and solving complex visual challenges. While we are aiming for 5+ years of experience,

Key Responsibilities:

  • Workflow Automation: Build, maintain, and support custom tools for the Art team using Python for Blender/Maya and C# for Unity editor extensions to streamline production.

  • Tool Development: Proven experience writing Python scripts for DCC tools (Blender/Maya) and C# tools/inspectors within Unity.
  • Shader Expertise: Good knowledge of HLSL and node-based shader editing.
  • Strong Documentation: Passion for (and history of) creating clean, readable technical documentation for non-technical artists.
  • Collaboration: A proactive team player who communicates complex technical ideas simply and works seamlessly across disciplines.
  • Industry Experience: 5+ years of game industry experience (or equivalent exceptional talent).

Not essential, but it helps if you have:

  • Blender Geometry Nodes: Hands-on experience creating procedural content or tools using Blender's Geometry Nodes.
  • Render Pipelines: Familiarity with Unity’s Universal Render Pipeline (URP).
  • Console Development: Experience optimizing games for platforms like Xbox,
  • PlayStation, or Nintendo Switch.

The role utilizes a solid understanding of business dynamics to define and document criteria for testing and present results following the defined testing methodology. Manage and coordinate end to end testing activities for small and large projects across many teams with both onsite and offshore resources
  • Relationship Building- Respond to client's inquiries and requests, providing professional high quality customer service for the assigned portfolio to ensure client satisfaction. You will liase and interact with clients as part of the daily management of your portfolio technology to support objectives or address issues. Work with test leads, business, business analysts and development teams to establish test plans, standards, and procedures that add value to software project and satisfy the constraints of the project by reviewing project documentation.
  • Monitor & Reporting- Monitor project adherence to quality standards and track/provide progress testing status reporting as needed. Adhere to CIBC’s processes through all phases of the software development life cycle-ensure test activities are compliant to test standards. Recognizing, anticipating, and resolving testing activities challenges during the testing life cycle.

Who you are

  • You put our clients first. You engage with purpose to find the right solutions. You go the extra mile, because it's the right thing to do.

  • You're passionate about people. You find meaning in relationships and surround yourself with a diverse network of partners. You connect with others through respect and authenticity.
  • You love to learn. You're passionate about growing your knowledge. You have a strong sense of curiosity.
  • You’re a certified professional. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Computer Science or Technical discipline.
  • Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

  • We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.

  • Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.

  • We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

title: Appliance Technician II
description:
**This position is eligible for a $1,500 sign-on bonus!**

Great teams make the #Best8Hours of your day. At Seneca Resorts & Casinos, we work hard, celebrate often, and build a culture people actually want to be part of.

*1st SHIFT*

The Appliance Technician II is responsible for the overall maintenance of the kitchens appliances. Under minimal supervision, performs refrigeration, electrical, electronic and mechanical maintenance work independently on kitchen equipment such as dishwashers, freezers, disposals, pumps, motors, steam kettles, ovens, and compressors. Also involves installation of equipment and performs related work as required. All duties are to be performed within the guidelines of the Seneca Gaming Corporation’s policies and procedures, Internal Control Standards and objectives.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

1. Service, repair, replace and maintain walk-in and reach-in freezers, refrigerators, ice makers, and milk coolers replacing components including motors, Freon, belts, thermometers, and adjust controls to accommodate specific types of Freon used in any particular appliance.

2. Repair, descale, maintain, and replace dishwashers and electric or gas water and booster heaters.

3. Maintain pumps.

4. Replace valves, belts, filters, bearings, gears, and motor parts.

5. Maintain and repair electronic combo-ovens, convection and standard ovens, steam ovens, industrial mixers, choppers, steam kettles, tilting braisers, and steamers.

6. Install gas valves, electric fans, vents, thermocouples, pilot lights, and door springs.

7. Repair and maintain heating and refrigeration units on food carts, fabricates and mounts sneeze guards.

8. Install electrical lines by running conduit, pulling wire, installing outlets; and repairs motors, switches, plugs, and appliance cords.

9. Replace pipes, faucets, and reversing and standard switches; locate and repair leaks; repair or replace industrial garbage disposals, clear minor blockages from sinks and disposals; cut and thread pipe, and sweat copper pipes.

10. Assemble a variety of kitchen racks and carts, mounts computer brackets for touch screens.

11. Maintain records of materials and time spent performing various maintenance and repair jobs.

12. Recommend repair or replacement of specific kitchen equipment.

13. Responsible for the guiding of the day-to-day operations of the on-site Appliance Technicians including the training of staff and the planning and scheduling of work performed by other appliance technicians and subcontractors in regards to projects.

14. Maintain a current understanding of all policy and guidelines regarding information security including the Seneca Gaming Corporation Acceptable Use Policy. Understand and comply with all information security policies and procedures at all times.

15. Provide exceptional customer service to all patrons and communicate in a pleasant, friendly and professional manner at all times. Maintain a professional work environment with supervisors, managers and staff.

16. Meet the attendance guidelines of the job and adhere to regulatory, departmental and company policies.

17. Must complete all required SGC Training programs within nine (9) months from commencement of employment.

18. Attend all necessary meetings.

19. Duties, responsibilities, requirements and expectations pertaining to this job are subject to change as needed. Hours are determined by a 24-hour schedule.


QUALIFICATIONS/REQUIREMENTS:

Education/Experience:

1. Must be 18 years of age or older upon employment.

2. High school diploma or equivalent is required and any combination equivalent to ten (10) years of experience in the journey-level repairs of kitchen equipment.

3. Must have knowledge of electrical, plumbing, steam, gas, electronic and refrigeration methods, current technology, principles and practices related to institutional kitchens. Kitchen maintenance and repair, including circuit tracing and troubleshooting skills related to electric motors, pumps, compressors, and electronic sensors knowledge required.

4. Must know current refrigeration technology and EPA regulations.

5. Must possess and maintain a valid driver’s license and be able to substantiate a safe driving record within the parameters acceptable to our liability insurance carrier.


Language Skills and Reasoning Ability:

1. Must possess excellent communication skills.

2. Ability to write routine correspondence and to speak effectively to the public, employees and customers.

3. Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts and draw valid conclusions.

4. Must have the ability to deal effectively and interact well with the customers and employees.

5. Must have the ability to resolve problems/conflicts in a diplomatic and tactful manner.


Physical Requirements and Work Environment:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderately loud. When on the casino floor, the noise levels increase to loud. Must be able to work in an environment where smoking is permitted.

1. Adequate manual dexterity to operate small and large kitchen equipment.

2. Works in wet, cold, hot, and greasy conditions inside and outside central kitchen areas. Works in confined areas including over ceilings, through crawl spaces, and on roofs, climbing ladders to and from roof to repairs or replace motors and ventilation equipment.

3. Regular exposure to electricity, gas, Freon, motor oil, and other hazardous materials.

4. Occasionally lifts over fifty (50) pounds, moving heavy kitchen equipment.

5. Occasional travel is required.

6. Must be able to effectively understand and communicate to employees.

7. Must be able to stand, walk, and move through all areas of the casino.

8. Maintain physical stamina and proper mental attitude to work under pressure in a fast-paced, casino environment and effectively deal with customers, management, employees, and members of the business community in all situations.

$24.40

title: Principal Engineer - Software Development
description:
When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

What you’ll be doing...

At Verizon Corporate Security, we are driving innovation and completely transforming how we build software to protect the world's most reliable network. We’ve proven that by pairing precise business requirements with AI-assisted development, we can compress delivery timelines by an order of magnitude—delivering the promise of the digital world faster than ever. To scale this capability across our organization, we are bringing on a Principal Automation Engineer: AI & Agentic Workflows.

This is not a role for someone who wants to manage from the sidelines. This is an opportunity for a highly autonomous, hands-on builder to join the V Team. If you have a "founding engineer" mindset, you will thrive here—turning written concepts into working, high-impact production software that unlocks immediate business value and helps us move the world forward.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Build applications from specifications: Take completed business requirements specifications and deliver working software against them as a hands-on individual contributor (write code, configure platforms, wire data, and demo results).

  • Build and operate the AI toolchain: Own internal tooling making the spec-to-build loop repeatable, including structured intake requirements-interview agents, reusable prompt/context/evaluation scaffolding, and build telemetry instrumentation.

  • Scale Automation Through Agentic Workflows: Design, build, and deploy agents on the Kairos platform, leveraging the enterprise ecosystem to ensure consistency, reusability, rapid iteration, and maximum speed-to-value.

  • Build necessary data plumbing: Integrate against imperfect upstream systems (SQL Server, BigQuery/EDW, GCP services, Looker, vendor APIs), managing schema drift, partial coverage, and inconsistent definitions while ensuring proper data lineage and governance.

  • Prove it works before it is trusted: Build evaluation harnesses alongside features (shadow-mode testing, precision/recall measurement, override-feedback loops, human-in-the-loop approval paths).

  • Demo, ship, and iterate weekly: Ship high-value features to staging weekly and demo to stakeholders on a standing cadence while navigating operational and policy complexity.

​What we’re looking for...

You’ll need to have:

  • Bachelor’s degree or four or more years of work experience.

  • Six or more years of relevant experience required, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training.

  • 5+ years of experience building and shipping production software end-to-end, demonstrating clear personal ownership, identifying specific users impacted, and delivering measurable business outcomes.

  • Experience shipping Large Language Model (LLM) applications to end users, applying hands-on expertise in prompt and context engineering, retrieval mechanisms, agent design, and system evaluation.

  • Demonstrated experience integrating data across complex, imperfect systems, leveraging strong SQL skills, practical data agility, and deep comfort navigating cloud environments (GCP) and business intelligence tools (Looker or equivalent).

Even better if you have one or more of the following:

  • 10+ years of relevant engineering experience building, shipping, and scaling enterprise software.

  • A Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related technical field.

  • Direct experience working alongside business operators in a highly embedded capacity, such as a forward-deployed engineer, solutions engineer, or founding engineer.

  • Define standards for alerting, dashboards, observability data quality, and integration with ITSM platforms (ServiceNow).
  • Design and manage multi-org Datadog architecture, including org structure, RBAC, SSO/SAML, secrets management, and cybersecurity compliance.

SOX Compliance and IT Governance

  • SOX control owner for enterprise monitoring applications — approve monthly reviews, participate in internal/external audits (EY), and maintain ITGC/SOX compliance.
  • Provide audit evidence, walkthrough documentation, and coordinate with auditors on logging, access management, and change management controls.
  • Review and approve technical designs for compliance-driven logging use cases, including SOX audit logs and security visibility.
  • Participate in the App Owner Community for SOX, staying current on IGA, ITAC evidence, and PUAR activities.

Operational Leadership and Incident Escalation

  • Serve as a senior escalation point for monitoring and observability-related incidents, coordinating troubleshooting across internal teams and external vendors.
  • Lead root-cause analysis and remediation efforts for complex ingestion, alerting, or platform stability issues.
  • Balance operational stability with ongoing platform evolution and cost optimization.

Vendor and Stakeholder Management

  • Manage relationships with external vendors and implementation partners (RapDev, Wipro), including escalations, resource availability, and contract deliverables.
  • Coordinate with cybersecurity and identity teams on security reviews, MFA/SSO integration, and secrets management architecture.
  • Lead steering committee meetings with senior leadership to align on platform strategy, budget, and cross-organizational adoption.


Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or equivalent experience.
  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise infrastructure architecture, monitoring/observability, or platform engineering.
  • Proven experience operating in large, complex IT environments with strong governance and compliance requirements.

Technical

  • Enterprise monitoring and logging platforms (Datadog, Splunk, or equivalent)
  • Infrastructure observability: metrics, logs, events, alerting, dashboards, and ITSM integrations (ServiceNow)
  • Server, network, and platform monitoring; agent-based and agentless architectures

title: Balancing Authority Operator In-Training - Minneapolis, MN
description:
Xcel Energy (NASDAQ: XEL) is a leading energy provider and Fortune 500 company, dedicated to serving millions of electricity and natural gas customers across eight states: Minnesota, Colorado, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota, New Mexico and Texas. We make energy work better for our customers, helping them thrive every day. That means always raising the bar - delivering better service and providing more reliable, resilient, and sustainable energy.

Xcel Energy is a place where you’ll have opportunities to grow, expand your skills, and help lead the clean energy transition. We offer meaningful rewards, recognition, and support to help you build your career and make an impact - both on the job and beyond. Most importantly, it means you’ll be joining a company that knows employees are the driving force behind its success and is committed to helping you be your best.

We anticipate the need for one or more Balancing Authority Operator In-Training at our Marshall Operations Center in Minneapolis, MN. The rate of pay for this job classification is $57.92 per hour. This position will be posted for 5 Working Days from September 24, 2026, to September 30, 2026.


Position Summary
The Balancing Authority Operator position is responsible for the real-time monitoring and operation of Xcel Energy's Balancing Authority Area/Local Balancing Authority Area. Monitor the Xcel Balancing Authority Area and take independent actions to ensure the security and reliability is consistent with NERC and RRO requirements. Ensure the accuracy of Energy Management System data relating to Balancing Authority Area interchange, load, and generation; and Transmission service schedules; and interconnected tie lines. The Balancing Authority Operator has the independent authority to perform necessary actions to maintain reliability, including emergency generation replacement, unscheduled load relief, firm load shedding, and black-start recovery.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Monitor the Xcel Balancing Authority Area and take necessary steps to ensure the security and reliability of the Balancing Authority Area consistent with NERC requirements. Ensure Xcel Energy Balancing Authority Area operation parameters are within internal operating guidelines, NERC and RRO standards, and when applicable, RTO guidelines. Ensure adequate energy supply for the Xcel Energy Balancing Authority Area by managing spinning and operating reserves, balancing generation to load, planning to meet load forecasts, and through generation commitments. Take appropriate steps to ensure replacement of lost resources due to generation unit trips.
  • Ensure the accuracy of Energy Management System data relating to Balancing Authority Area interchange, load, and generation; and Transmission service schedules; and interconnected tie lines. Implement Xcel Energy Balancing Authority Area and Transmission Provider energy tagging function. Implement Xcel Energy Balancing Authority Area scheduling system and provide appropriate interface with the RTO when required. Perform nightly checkout with the adjacent Balancing Authority Area for Actual and Scheduled Interchange, as well as with the RTO as appropriate. Perform nightly checkout for transmission Energy Accounting.
  • Implement Emergency Procedures including, but not limited to, emergency generation replacement, unscheduled flow relief, emergency firm load shedding and black-start recovery. Order Balancing Authority Area generation on-line or order re-dispatch as necessary to maintain Balancing Authority Area security. Work with Network or other customers to ensure proper implementation of peak day interruptible loads. Work with the Transmission System Operator and Xcel Energy generating plants in system restoration.
  • Maintain close communications with Generator Operators to ensure safety, reliability and regulatory compliance with respect to transmission operations. Jointly develop, review and approve plans to return the Balancing Authority Area to recognized system parameters.
  • Monitor transmission system conditions using available tools, such as the Energy Management System, Energy Accounting System, and other data systems. Communicate system status to the Reliability Coordinator, affected electric transmission systems and Balancing Authority Areas, and Xcel Energy management. Work with network customers to ensure generation and scheduling needs are met. Write and maintain a chronological log of Balancing Authority Area events including, but not limited to, transmission service curtailments and requests for emergency energy.
  • Monitor proper tagging of OASIS transmission service requests for Xcel Energy and all other relevant tariffs. Back-up the Transmission System Operator and the Network Reliability Leader (NRL) relating to transmission service requests and help resolve transmission service request problems.
  • Maintain thorough knowledge and understanding of Balancing Authority Area operation, including but not limited to new operating practices, NERC compliance issues, Xcel Energy and regional tariffs, FERC, RRO and RTO requirements. Participate in annual training plans designed to enhance expertise and assist other team members in expanding overall knowledge. Maintain NERC Certification through completion of required training is a condition of continued employment. Other duties as assigned.


Minimum Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Successful completion of certificate program in Electric Power Technology or equivalent program preferred.
  • Minimum of 3 years utility operations experience in electric distribution, transmission or power generation OR 3 years' experience working with high-voltage auxiliary electrical systems, instrumentation & control or relay systems in manufacturing, refinery or chemical plant environment.
  • Successful completion of Edison Electric Institute (EEI) System Operator / Power Dispatching (SOPD) screening test is required.
  • NERC certification required or ability to successfully obtain the NERC Certification that is applicable for Balancing Authority Area operation within 6 months of position start date.
  • Demonstrated ability to successfully complete the initial qualifications as defined in the training program for the Balancing Authority Operator position. Demonstrated ability to respond quickly and appropriately in a real-time, stressful environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize job tasks. Strong communication skills required. Knowledge of or ability to learn Xcel Energy, NERC, and FERC requirements. This position requires working rotating shifts.

title: Associate Project Director, GRAPS - Job ID: 2035
description:
Ascendis Pharma is a dynamic, fast-growing global biopharmaceutical company with locations in Denmark, Europe, and the United States. Today, we're advancing programs in Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology.

Here at Ascendis, we pride ourselves on exceptional science, visionary leadership, and skilled and passionate colleagues.

Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we use our TransCon® drug development platform to fulfill our mission of developing new and potentially best-in-class therapies to address unmet medical needs.

Our culture fosters a place where skilled, adaptable, and highly resourceful professionals can truly make their mark. We offer a dynamic workplace for employees to grow and develop their skills.

Position summary

The Associate Project Director, GRAPS is a senior project-management professional who translates GRAPS priorities into disciplined execution across Global Regulatory Affairs, Global Patient Safety, and enterprise partners. The role establishes fit-for-purpose governance, integrated plans, decision pathways, performance reporting, and risk management for a portfolio of strategic and operational initiatives.

Working with the Chief Regulatory & Safety Officer, GRAPS Leadership Team, functional leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders, this individual will lead small-to-medium, complex projects and selected larger workstreams that require coordination across functions, geographies, vendors, and systems. The role combines strategic perspective with hands-on delivery and is expected to influence without authority, improve ways of working, and strengthen quality, compliance, predictability, and organizational scalability.

Key responsibilities

Strategic portfolio and project leadership

  • Lead assigned GRAPS projects and programs from definition through closeout, with clear charters, scope, objectives, outcomes, milestones, owners, dependencies, and success measures.
  • Partner with GRAPS leaders to translate strategic priorities into integrated roadmaps and sequenced execution plans aligned with portfolio and enterprise objectives.
  • Maintain a consolidated view of the GRAPS project portfolio, distinguishing project work from base-business activity and highlighting capacity constraints, interdependencies, and decisions required.
  • Facilitate project initiation, prioritization, stage reviews, lessons learned, and benefits realization.

Governance, planning, and delivery

  • Establish and run proportionate governance, including core teams, steering forums, agendas, decision logs, action tracking, and escalation pathways.
  • Develop and maintain integrated project plans, critical paths, resource assumptions, budgets, RAID (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, and Dependencies or Decisions) logs, and change controls.
  • Monitor execution against scope, schedule, quality, cost, and expected outcomes; identify emerging issues early and drive recovery plans.
  • Prepare concise executive dashboards, status reports, decision memos, and recommendations for the GRAPS Leadership Team and other governance bodies.

Cross-functional collaboration and communication

  • Coordinate stakeholders across Regulatory Affairs, Patient Safety, Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Quality, IT, Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement, and external partners, as applicable.
  • Create clarity on roles, accountabilities, interfaces, and handoffs, using fit-for-purpose RACI or equivalent tools.
  • Facilitate complex workshops and working sessions that align stakeholders, resolve ambiguity, and convert discussion into decisions and accountable actions.
  • Communicate proactively and tailor content for executive, technical, and operational audiences across cultures and time zones.

Operational excellence, quality, and compliance

  • Identify opportunities to standardize, simplify, and scale GRAPS processes, templates, tools, and operating practices.
  • Partner with process owners and Quality to ensure project deliverables support applicable GxP, regulatory, pharmacovigilance, documentation, training, inspection-readiness, and records-management requirements.
  • Use data and trend analysis to monitor performance, identify root causes, and recommend sustainable improvements.
  • Support adoption of digital project-management, collaboration, dashboarding, workflow, and knowledge-management capabilities.

Resource, vendor, and change management

  • Coordinate resource planning for assigned initiatives and surface trade-offs requiring leadership action.
  • Support vendor selection, statements of work, onboarding, purchase-order coordination, deliverable oversight, and performance monitoring in partnership with Procurement and Finance.
  • Develop stakeholder and change-impact assessments, communication plans, readiness activities, and adoption measures for new processes, systems, and operating models.
  • Provide direction, coaching, and project-methodology support to workstream leads and more junior project-management colleagues; may lead contractors or matrixed team members.

Requirements

Professional qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, business, project management, engineering, or a related discipline; advanced degree is preferred.
  • Typically 8 or more years of relevant experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or other highly regulated industry, including substantial responsibility for cross-functional project or program delivery.
  • Demonstrated experience leading small-to-medium complex projects or major workstreams with functional-management stakeholders and limited day-to-day supervision.
  • Working knowledge of drug development and commercialization, with experience in Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance/Patient Safety, Quality, Regulatory Operations, or adjacent functions strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated command of project and program management practices, including scope, schedule, resource, budget, dependency, risk, issue, change, governance, and benefits management.
  • Experience preparing executive-ready dashboards, status reports, decision materials, and presentations using Microsoft 365 and relevant project-management or reporting tools.
  • Project-management certification such as PMP, PRINCE2, or equivalent is preferred; Agile or change-management training is an advantage.

Leadership capabilities and personal attributes

  • Enterprise mindset and patient focus, with sound judgment about business, quality, compliance, and reputational risk.
  • Advanced stakeholder-management and influencing skills, including the ability to establish alignment and accountability without formal authority.
  • Highly structured, analytical, and detail-oriented while maintaining focus on strategic intent and outcomes.
  • Able to simplify complexity, frame options, recommend a path forward, and communicate decisions clearly.
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity, managing competing priorities, and adapting plans as conditions change.
  • Collaborative, inclusive, culturally aware, and effective in a global matrix environment.
  • High integrity, discretion, ownership, and commitment to transparent communication and follow-through.

Key interfaces

Primary - Chief Regulatory & Safety Officer; GRAPS Leadership Team; GRAPS Enablement & Insights

Functional - Global Regulatory Affairs; Global Patient Safety; Regulatory Operations; Quality and Compliance

Enterprise - Clinical Development; Medical Affairs; IT; Finance; HR; Legal; Procurement; Communications

External - Consultants, CROs, technology providers, and other vendors, as required

Measures of success

  • Projects have agreed scope, governance, accountabilities, milestones, risk controls, and measurable outcomes.
  • Leadership receives timely, decision-ready visibility into progress, dependencies, resource needs, risks, and trade-offs.
  • Priority deliverables are completed to agreed quality and timelines, with issues escalated early and recovery actions documented.
  • Ways of working become more consistent, efficient, scalable, and inspection-ready across GRAPS.
  • Stakeholders understand decisions, responsibilities, and next steps, and demonstrate sustained adoption of implemented changes.

Additional information

  • Travel: Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 10%, based on business needs.
  • Location: Proposed as a US or EU remote or hybrid role, with travel to Ascendis locations and business-critical meetings as needed.
  • This description summarizes the principal responsibilities of the role and may be adjusted as organizational priorities evolve.

The estimated salary range for this position is $180k - $190k. Actual salary determination is dependent on a variety of factors some of which include: experience, qualifications, and geographic location. This position may be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus or an incentive compensation plan (eligibility varies based on role and position level), discretionary stock-based long-term incentives, paid time off, and a comprehensive benefits package.

title: Sr Database Administrator
description:
Take your career to the next level! In the last few years our goal has been expansion, creating growth opportunities for many of our team members. Not only are we serious about growth, but we are also serious about helping our customers during hard financial times.

We take pride in providing solutions and offering a helping hand, not only to our customers but also to the communities we serve. As we continue to expand and grow into a national leader in consumer financing, we invite you to consider joining our team.

If you're passionate about making a meaningful impact in people's lives and bringing a personal touch to finance, we'd love to have you on board!

Job purpose

The Senior Database Administrator ensures the stability, security, and performance of the organization's Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL environments. This role owns database administration, high availability and disaster recovery, and performance tuning for systems that power key business applications, and serves as a primary responder for database incidents as part of an on-call rotation. The Senior DBA also supports ETL and reporting through SSIS and SSRS, partners with business stakeholders to turn requirements into technical solutions, and mentors other team members while helping set database standards and best practices.


Duties and responsibilities

  • Administration & Operations
    • Manage backup, recovery, and high availability/disaster recovery strategies, including Always On Availability Groups, log shipping, and PostgreSQL streaming replication.
    • Handle database security, including access control, permissions, and auditing.
    • Plan and perform patching, upgrades, and capacity planning.
    • Respond to SQL Server and PostgreSQL outages and incidents, including after-hours and weekends, as part of a weekly on-call rotation.
  • Performance & Troubleshooting
    • Lead performance tuning efforts using execution plans, indexing and statistics strategy, wait analysis, and query optimization.
    • Use SQL Server tools such as SSMS, Extended Events, Query Store, DMVs, and PerfMon, as well as PostgreSQL tools such as EXPLAIN ANALYZE, pg_stat_statements, system catalogs, and VACUUM/autovacuum tuning to diagnose and resolve issues.
    • Perform root-cause analysis, working backward from known issues to identify and permanently resolve underlying problems.
  • Database Development & Design
    • Design, write, and optimize database code across Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL, including stored procedures, functions, views, triggers, tables, indexes, partitions, and constraints.
    • Review new and existing database code to ensure it meets company standards for readability, reliability, scalability, and performance.
    • Build new code and processes to support a growing business and evolving application needs.
  • Automation, ETL & Reporting
    • Design, develop, deploy, and monitor SSIS packages and SQL Agent jobs for ETL and operational automation.
    • Create, maintain, and deploy reports in SSRS.
  • Business Partnership & Leadership
    • Facilitate requirements sessions with stakeholders and translate business needs and change requests into technical deliverables.
    • Mentor junior and mid-level DBAs and developers and help define database best practices and standards.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in database administration and development in Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL environments, including installation, configuration, security, backup and recovery, and ongoing support.

  • Deep expertise in performance tuning, including query analysis, execution plans, index strategy, statistics maintenance, and blocking, deadlock, and wait analysis.

  • Proven ability to troubleshoot and resolve database integrity, performance, replication, connectivity, and security issues in production environments.

  • Experience with High Availability and Disaster Recovery solutions for SQL Server (e.g., Always On Availability Groups, log shipping) and PostgreSQL (e.g., streaming replication, failover).

  • Hands-on experience with SSIS package development, deployment, and troubleshooting, and SSRS report design, deployment, and subscription setup.

  • Experience automating operational tasks with scripting (e.g., PowerShell, T-SQL, Python, or Bash).

  • Experience with source control (Git/GitHub) and the full software development lifecycle.Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write clear technical documentation and explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

  • Self-motivated and detail-oriented, with the ability to prioritize and deliver in a fast-paced environment.

  • Collaborative approach, with experience mentoring or guiding other team members.

Preferred Qualifications


  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

  • Relevant certifications, such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Database Administrator Associate, AWS Certified Database – Specialty, or PostgreSQL certification.Experience with SQL Server 2019 and newer, including migrating or upgrading from older versions.

  • Experience with cloud database platforms, such as AWS RDS, Aurora, or SQL Server on EC2.

  • Experience with database tooling such as Redgate or Idera, and work tracking tools such as Jira.Familiarity with C# or other application languages for supporting development teams.

title: Quality Tech
description:
Job Summary

Job Profile Summary
Responsible for assisting with all aspects of the quality systems as needed included: in process inspections, testing and release of all raw materials and finished products. Responsible for the effective completion of raw materials and product release and ensuring compliance with established quality procedures and company policy.

Job Description

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Ensure complaints are logged and closed appropriately. Coordinate stock checks and rework of product as required in response to complaints.
  • Coordinate test samples and results with internal and external laboratories.
  • Log test results, product manufacturing information, and retain samples in spreadsheets.
  • Issue required documentation needed for production such as production records.
  • Review receiving documentation for raw materials and inspect to ensure raw materials meet all requirement standards.
  • Assist Quality staff with stock checks, deviations, running and distributing repots, and other various documentation requirements including maintaining training requirements, SOP and specification generation updates CIA/DHR review and filling and test method development.

title: Pyro Product specialist
description:
Pyro Product Specialist
People behind the solutions

At Fuller Technologies we know that building a strong team starts with creating opportunities for growth. For over a century, we’ve supported the people behind the solutions, fostering a culture where hard work is valued, learning is encouraged, and teamwork drives success.

About the role

Our global Service Engineering team is looking for a technically sharp and motivated Pyro Product Specialist to take ownership of aftermarket, retrofit, and product improvement solutions for Rotary Kilns and other Pyro equipment in the cement industry.

Service Engineering sits at the intersection of sales and execution – we are the technical backbone behind proposals, troubleshooting, and high-value retrofits. You will join a team of specialists with global responsibility for mechanical Pyro equipment, including rotary kilns, preheaters, burners, and similar heavy machinery, bringing together hands-on engineering, product ownership, and cross-functional collaboration.

You will apply your specialist knowledge across the full equipment lifecycle – from design and fabrication through to installation and operation – supporting both internal stakeholders and customers around the world. You will work independently with limited supervision, influencing outcomes through deep technical expertise.


Your role & Responsibilities:

  • Collaboration: Work closely with other departments (e.g., Customer Service, Sales departments, Business development, Procurement, Customers and quality assurance) to ensure alignment on deliverables, goals and timelines.

  • Documentation: Prepare detailed engineering documentation, including specifications, reports, and manuals, ensuring compliance with regulations and standards.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Responsibility for technical proposal preparation and execution of engineered parts for our aftermarket and retrofit business
  • Responsible for on-time, on budget, quality of engineering packages for individual projects

  • Create, review and approves design drawings prepared in SolidWorks 3D and AutoCad
  • Create and review configuration program prepared in Tacton

  • Promotes a culture of personal and team safety, including others who may be affected by the company’s operational activities

You bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Marine or related field).

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork abilities.
  • Familiarity with industry regulations and standards.
  • Preferred experience within Cement industry or similar heavy industry.
  • You have experience with machine design, engineering documentation and SolidWorks

  • You have a mindset for continuous improvements in methodologies and working procedures

Job Description

Tarleton State University, a distinguished Doctoral National Comprehensive University, invites applications for the position of Senior Counselor in the Department of Student Counseling Services. As part of a vibrant academic community dedicated to excellence in teaching, research, and service, this role offers the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to a university that values innovation, collaboration, and inclusive growth. Join us in advancing knowledge and transforming lives—on campus and beyond. Tarleton State University continues to grow its impact across Texas, with four distinct campuses located in Stephenville, Fort Worth, RELLIS-Bryan and Waco, along with a robust online community that extends our reach even further.

At the heart of it all is Stephenville, where Tarleton State offers a dynamic environment for faculty and staff. From a lively live music scene and numerous local festivals to rich traditions rooted in the surrounding community, Stephenville provides a vibrant and welcoming atmosphere.

No matter where you're located—on campus or online—you are part of a mission that transforms lives and makes a difference across the state of Texas and beyond.

________________________________________________________________________

Important Immigration Information:

A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. Please be advised that Tarleton State University will NOT pay this fee. Therefore, if you need immigration sponsorship for your employment, we recommend that you consult with your private immigration counsel at your own expense to ascertain whether your current immigration status would make a potential offer of employment from Tarleton State University subject to this fee.

In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate.

________________________________________________________________________



The Stephenville Senior Counselor, under supervision of the Director of Student Counseling Services (SCS), supports the overall wellness of the campus community through direct clinical services, administrative coordination, oversight of the Academic Training Lab, and outreach leadership. This role balances individual and group counseling responsibilities with added administrative and outreach efforts aimed at expanding Counseling Services’ presence and impact.


Depending on experience and qualifications, the role may include mentorship, supervision, and training of student employees and/or counseling interns. The counselor participates in the on-call crisis response rotation and performs other duties as assigned. Serves as Campus Security Authority (CSA).


This position is in-office, located in Stephenville, Texas, and works Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 5 PM. Occasional travel to the Fort Worth campus, conferences, after-hours outreach, and weekend support for university events will be required.


Responsibilities:

Direct Clinical Services:

  • Renders individual and group counseling to students experiencing developmental, psychological, and interpersonal concerns. Group offerings may include process-oriented, psychoeducational, and drop-in formats. Provides crisis counseling and response and serves as a resource to the university community in matters of crisis intervention. Participates in on-call crisis rotation. Supports the Leadership Team in maintaining and managing records within the clinic’s electronic health record system, including conducting audits and facilitating record expungement in accordance with state laws and university policies.

Program Leadership:

  • Serves as part of the leadership team for SCS, providing guidance to SCS staff in managing day-to-day operations, crisis intervention, clinical scheduling, professional development, and outreach requests.
  • Coordinates and supports grant related activities, including identifying funding opportunities, assisting with proposal development, monitoring project timelines and deliverables, and preparing required reports. Collaborates with university departments and community partners to implement grant funded initiatives and special projects that enhance Counseling Services programming, outreach, and student wellness. Assists with the planning, coordination, and evaluation of strategic initiatives that align with departmental and university priorities.
  • Oversees staff professional development, including leading internal case review and consultation, accessing / arranging external consultation when appropriate, and providing and promoting CEU and educational opportunities.
  • Oversees the Academic Training Lab including coordinating intern selection, onboarding, and training, and matching interns with SCS supervisors. Serves as an SCS site supervisor for one to three interns per academic year. Provides consultation and support to supervisors, including addressing performance concerns and coordinating communication with intern faculty as needed.

Outreach:

  • Coordinates outreach activities in collaboration with campus departments and community resources. Supports marketing, website updates, and event planning to promote SCS. Prepares internal and external documentation and reports. Represents SCS on university committees, community collaboratives, professional coalitions, and at conferences.

Case Management and External Consultation:

  • Maintains timely and thorough documentation in accordance with licensure standards and departmental policies. Coordinates care with campus partners and external providers. Participates in regular clinical consultations and staff meetings. Provides consultation to campus partners regarding concern for students, referrals, processes, etc.

Other duties as assigned:

  • Serve as representative on Department, Division, and University committees and task forces, at events, and to department stakeholders as assigned / needed.
  • Attend and actively engage in Department and Division meetings, trainings, and functions.

Minimum Qualifications

Required Education and Experience:

  • Master’s degree in Counseling, Social Work, Psychology, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Experience working in or with a complex organization with an understanding of larger institutional goals and objectives.
  • One year of experience in a college counseling center or related mental health setting.
  • Must hold a current Clinical Supervisor designation or be eligible and willing to begin the Clinical Supervisor designation process upon hire.

Licensure Requirement:

  • Must hold a current, unrestricted Texas license as a Licensed Psychologist (LP), Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT), or Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), and maintain the license in good standing with BHEC as a condition of continued employment.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Proficiency in standard office software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).
  • Strong written communication, analytical, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and adhere to relevant state laws and ethical standards.
  • Effective collaboration and multitasking skills in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.
  • Comfortable presenting to groups and engaging with a broad range of students and stakeholders.

Preferred:

  • Experience with outreach programming and student engagement
  • Previous work in a university counseling center
  • Familiarity with Titanium Schedule or similar EHR systems
  • Experience with CBT, DBT, and / or solution-focused, brief therapy models.


Compensation & Benefits

Salary: Commensurate with experience

Salary Range:

The target base annual salary range is $53,745 up to $76,321 and may be negotiable based on funding availability and candidate experience/skillset in relation to the minimum requirements of this position.

We are proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package for full-time and qualifying part-time employees. Our Careers Page offers an overview of the great benefits we offer; for detailed information visit our Benefits Information page.
